target: Selamat pagi! Apa kabar?
english: Good morning! How are you?
grammar: Apa kabar? is literally 'what news?' — the everyday 'how are you?'. Reply: Kabar baik.

target: Selamat siang, Bu Sari.
english: Good day, Mrs. Sari.
grammar: Bu (short for Ibu) is the polite title for a woman: Selamat siang, Bu Sari.

target: Selamat sore, Pak Budi.
english: Good afternoon, Mr. Budi.

target: Selamat malam, semuanya.
english: Good evening, everyone.

target: Kabar baik, terima kasih.
english: I'm fine, thank you.

target: Halo, senang bertemu dengan kamu.
english: Hello, nice to meet you.
grammar: bertemu = ber- + temu (meet): Senang bertemu dengan kamu = nice to meet you.

target: Sampai jumpa besok!
english: See you tomorrow!

target: Selamat tinggal, Pak.
english: Goodbye, sir.
grammar: Selamat tinggal is a final goodbye; for 'see you later' say Sampai jumpa.

target: Selamat datang di rumah kami.
english: Welcome to our house.

target: Apa kabar keluarga kamu?
english: How is your family?

target: Nama saya Andi.
english: My name is Andi.
grammar: Indonesian drops 'is' in simple sentences: Nama saya Andi = My name (is) Andi.

target: Siapa nama kamu?
english: What is your name?

target: Saya dari Inggris.
english: I am from England.

target: Kamu tinggal di mana?
english: Where do you live?
grammar: di mana = where; question words often sit at the end: Kamu tinggal di mana?

target: Saya tinggal di Jakarta.
english: I live in Jakarta.

target: Perkenalkan, ini istri saya.
english: Let me introduce you, this is my wife.
grammar: Perkenalkan opens an introduction: Perkenalkan, ini istri saya = meet my wife.

target: Senang berkenalan dengan Anda.
english: Pleased to make your acquaintance.

target: Saya bekerja di rumah sakit.
english: I work at a hospital.
grammar: bekerja = ber- + kerja (work): Saya bekerja di rumah sakit = I work at a hospital.

target: Dia teman saya dari kantor.
english: He is my friend from the office.

target: Ini kartu nama saya.
english: This is my business card.

target: Saya guru bahasa Inggris.
english: I am an English teacher.
grammar: No word for 'am/is' before nouns: Saya guru = I am a teacher.

target: Kamu murid baru, ya?
english: You are a new student, right?

target: Pak Budi manajer kami.
english: Mr. Budi is our manager.

target: Dia adik saya.
english: He is my younger sibling.
grammar: In conversation just drop 'is': Dia adik saya. adalah sounds formal, like a definition.

target: Kami dari Australia.
english: We are from Australia.

target: Kita teman sekarang.
english: We are friends now.
grammar: kita includes the listener, kami excludes them: kita pergi (you too) / kami pergi (not you).

target: Mereka turis dari Jepang.
english: They are tourists from Japan.

target: Bahasa Indonesia adalah bahasa nasional.
english: Indonesian is the national language.

target: Kami tinggal bersama di Bandung.
english: We live together in Bandung.

target: Mereka datang dari Surabaya.
english: They came from Surabaya.

target: Ini rumah orang tua saya.
english: This is my parents' house.
grammar: ini before a noun = 'this is'; after it = 'this': ini rumah (this is a house) / rumah ini (this house).

target: Itu kantor pos.
english: That is the post office.

target: Ini paspor saya.
english: This is my passport.

target: Itu hotel kami.
english: That is our hotel.

target: Ini suami saya, namanya Tono.
english: This is my husband, his name is Tono.

target: Itu anak-anak mereka.
english: Those are their children.

target: Terima kasih banyak, Pak!
english: Thank you very much, sir!

target: Sama-sama, Bu.
english: You're welcome, ma'am.
grammar: Sama-sama ('same-same') is the standard reply to terima kasih.

target: Permisi, saya mau lewat.
english: Excuse me, I want to get past.

target: Maaf, saya datang terlambat.
english: Sorry, I arrived late.

target: Saya tidak lapar sekarang.
english: I am not hungry now.
grammar: tidak negates verbs/adjectives, bukan negates nouns: Saya tidak lapar. / Ini bukan rumah saya.

target: Dia tidak suka kopi.
english: He does not like coffee.

target: Kami tidak punya mobil.
english: We do not have a car.

target: Ini bukan tas saya.
english: This is not my bag.

target: Dia bukan guru, dia dokter.
english: He is not a teacher, he is a doctor.
grammar: bukan can correct a noun: Dia bukan guru, dia dokter = not a teacher but a doctor.

target: Itu bukan masalah besar.
english: That is not a big problem.

target: Saya bukan orang Jepang.
english: I am not Japanese.

target: Mereka tidak bekerja hari ini.
english: They are not working today.

target: Anak itu tidak mau tidur.
english: That child does not want to sleep.

target: Rumah ini tidak besar.
english: This house is not big.

target: Ibu saya bukan orang Bali.
english: My mother is not from Bali.

target: Kopi ini tidak panas.
english: This coffee is not hot.

target: Saya tidak tahu jalan itu.
english: I do not know that road.

target: Itu bukan kunci kamar saya.
english: That is not my room key.

target: Kami bukan turis, kami tinggal di sini.
english: We are not tourists, we live here.

target: Saya tidak bisa datang besok.
english: I cannot come tomorrow.
grammar: bisa = can: Saya tidak bisa datang = I cannot come.

target: Dia tidak minum teh.
english: He does not drink tea.

target: Apakah kamu suka makanan pedas?
english: Do you like spicy food?
grammar: Apakah turns a statement into a yes/no question: Kamu suka kopi. → Apakah kamu suka kopi?

target: Apakah masih ada kamar kosong?
english: Are there still any rooms available?

target: Apakah dia kakak kamu?
english: Is she your older sibling?

target: Apakah bus ini pergi ke bandara?
english: Does this bus go to the airport?

target: Apakah Anda bisa membantu saya?
english: Can you help me?
grammar: membantu = mem- + bantu (help); meN- makes the active verb.

target: Apakah kantor buka hari Sabtu?
english: Is the office open on Saturday?

target: Apakah ini kereta ke Bogor?
english: Is this the train to Bogor?

target: Apakah kamu sudah makan?
english: Have you eaten yet?
grammar: sudah = already: Apakah kamu sudah makan? = Have you eaten (yet)?

target: Kamu orang Indonesia?
english: Are you Indonesian?
grammar: In speech a rising tone alone makes a yes/no question: Kamu orang Indonesia?

target: Dia datang besok?
english: Is he coming tomorrow?

target: Ini tempat duduk saya?
english: Is this my seat?

target: Anda bekerja di sini?
english: Do you work here?

target: Apa itu, Pak?
english: What is that, sir?

target: Kamu mau minum apa?
english: What do you want to drink?
grammar: apa can sit at the end: Kamu mau minum apa? = What do you want to drink?

target: Apa nama jalan ini?
english: What is the name of this street?

target: Siapa nama anak kamu?
english: What is your child's name?
grammar: Asking a name uses siapa (who), not apa: Siapa nama kamu? = What is your name?

target: Siapa itu di depan pintu?
english: Who is that at the front door?

target: Siapa manajer kamu di kantor?
english: Who is your manager at the office?

target: Saya sudah makan siang di kantor.
english: I already ate lunch at the office.
grammar: sudah marks completion — no past tense needed: Saya sudah makan. (I already ate.)

target: Kami sudah tiba di hotel.
english: We have already arrived at the hotel.

target: Ibu sudah bangun sejak jam lima pagi.
english: Mom has been up since five in the morning.

target: Dia sudah selesai bekerja hari ini.
english: He has already finished working today.

target: Apakah kamu sudah minum kopi?
english: Have you already had coffee?
grammar: Answer a sudah question with the marker itself: Sudah. (Already.) or Belum. (Not yet.)

target: Anak-anak sudah tidur di kamar.
english: The children are already asleep in the bedroom.

target: Kereta sudah tiba di stasiun.
english: The train has already arrived at the station.

target: Saya belum sarapan pagi ini.
english: I have not had breakfast yet this morning.
grammar: belum = not yet — expected to happen later: Saya belum makan. (I have not eaten yet.)

target: Ayah belum pulang dari kantor.
english: Dad has not come home from the office yet.

target: Kami belum membeli tiket pesawat.
english: We have not bought the plane tickets yet.

target: Dia belum selesai mencuci piring.
english: She has not finished washing the dishes yet.

target: Kamu belum tidur?
english: You're not asleep yet?

target: Saya belum menerima jawaban dari mereka.
english: I have not received an answer from them yet.

target: Ibu sedang memasak di dapur.
english: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
grammar: sedang marks action in progress: Ibu sedang memasak. (Mom is cooking right now.)

target: Saya sedang menunggu bus di halte.
english: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.

target: Mereka sedang makan malam bersama.
english: They are having dinner together.

target: Adik sedang belajar untuk ujian besok.
english: My younger sibling is studying for tomorrow's exam.
grammar: untuk = for (purpose): belajar untuk ujian (study for the exam)

target: Kami sedang mengerjakan proyek baru.
english: We are working on a new project.

target: Dia sedang berbicara dengan tamu.
english: He is speaking with a guest.

target: Saya akan pergi ke pasar besok pagi.
english: I will go to the market tomorrow morning.
grammar: akan marks the future — the verb never changes: Saya akan pergi. (I will go.)

target: Kami akan datang ke rumah kamu nanti malam.
english: We will come to your house tonight.

target: Dia akan mulai pekerjaan baru bulan depan.
english: She will start a new job next month.

target: Pesawat akan tiba sebentar lagi.
english: The plane will arrive shortly.

target: Saya akan membayar dengan uang tunai.
english: I will pay with cash.

target: Mereka akan menjual rumah itu tahun depan.
english: They will sell that house next year.

target: Saya baru saja bangun tidur.
english: I just woke up.
grammar: baru saja = just now: Saya baru saja bangun. (I just woke up.)

target: Tamu itu baru saja pergi.
english: That guest just left.

target: Kami baru saja selesai makan malam.
english: We just finished dinner.

target: Bus ke bandara baru saja berangkat.
english: The bus to the airport just left.

target: Dia baru saja mengirim email itu.
english: He just sent that email.

target: Saya masih menunggu di depan toko.
english: I am still waiting in front of the store.

target: Ayah masih bekerja di kantor.
english: Dad is still working at the office.
grammar: masih = still, the action continues: Dia masih bekerja. (He is still working.)

target: Kopi ini masih panas.
english: This coffee is still hot.

target: Kami masih punya waktu satu jam.
english: We still have one hour.

target: Toko itu masih buka sekarang.
english: That store is still open now.

target: Saya pernah pergi ke Bali dua kali.
english: I have been to Bali twice.
grammar: pernah = have ever done at least once: Saya pernah ke Bali. (I have been to Bali.)

target: Apakah kamu pernah makan sate?
english: Have you ever eaten satay?

target: Dia belum pernah naik pesawat.
english: He has never been on a plane.
grammar: belum pernah = never so far: Dia belum pernah naik pesawat. (He has never flown.)

target: Kami pernah tinggal di Jakarta.
english: We once lived in Jakarta.

target: Ibu pernah bekerja di rumah sakit.
english: Mom once worked at a hospital.

target: Permisi, di mana kamar mandi?
english: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?
grammar: di mana asks where something is: Di mana kamar mandi? (Where is the bathroom?)

target: Kamu tinggal di mana sekarang?
english: Where do you live now?

target: Ke mana kamu pergi hari ini?
english: Where are you going today?
grammar: ke mana asks where to (motion): Ke mana kamu pergi? (Where are you going?)

target: Bus ini ke mana?
english: Where does this bus go?
grammar: Destination questions can drop the verb: Bus ini ke mana? (Where does this bus go?)

target: Dari mana asal keluarga kamu?
english: Where is your family from?

target: Dari mana kamu tahu berita itu?
english: Where did you hear that news from?

target: Kapan kamu pulang ke rumah?
english: When are you going home?
grammar: kapan = when: Kapan kamu pulang? (When are you going home?)

target: Kapan toko ini buka lagi?
english: When does this store open again?

target: Kapan kita bertemu lagi?
english: When will we meet again?

target: Kapan kamu mulai kerja di kantor baru?
english: When do you start work at the new office?

target: Berapa harga tiket ini?
english: How much is this ticket?
grammar: berapa asks how much or how many: Berapa harga tiket ini? (How much is this ticket?)

target: Harga tiket masuk lima puluh ribu rupiah.
english: The entrance ticket costs fifty thousand rupiah.
grammar: Tens stack simply: lima puluh = five tens = 50, dua puluh = 20.

target: Kopi ini harganya dua puluh lima ribu.
english: This coffee costs twenty-five thousand.

target: Berapa orang di keluarga kamu?
english: How many people are in your family?

target: Ada empat orang di keluarga saya.
english: There are four people in my family.
grammar: ada = there is/are: Ada empat orang. (There are four people.)

target: Saya mau beli tiga kilo beras.
english: I want to buy three kilos of rice.
grammar: After mau, the bare root is natural in speech: mau beli = want to buy.

target: Berapa umur anak kamu sekarang?
english: How old is your child now?
grammar: berapa umur = how old: Berapa umur anak kamu? (How old is your child?)

target: Umur saya tiga puluh dua tahun.
english: I am thirty-two years old.

target: Kamar ini seratus ribu rupiah semalam.
english: This room is one hundred thousand rupiah a night.
grammar: se- means one: seratus = one hundred, semalam = one night.

target: Kami butuh dua kamar untuk empat orang.
english: We need two rooms for four people.

target: Jam berapa sekarang di sana?
english: What time is it there now?
grammar: jam berapa = what time: Jam berapa sekarang? (What time is it now?)

target: Sekarang jam sembilan pagi.
english: It is nine in the morning now.
grammar: Time of day follows the hour: jam sembilan pagi = 9 a.m., jam sembilan malam = 9 p.m.

target: Jam berapa kamu bangun setiap pagi?
english: What time do you wake up every morning?

target: Saya mulai kerja jam delapan pagi.
english: I start work at eight in the morning.

target: Kereta ke Bandung datang jam tiga sore.
english: The train to Bandung arrives at three in the afternoon.
grammar: sore = late afternoon, about 3-6 p.m.: jam tiga sore = 3 p.m.

target: Kami makan malam jam tujuh.
english: We eat dinner at seven o'clock.

target: Pasar buka dari pagi sampai sore.
english: The market is open from morning until late afternoon.

target: Siang ini saya makan di rumah.
english: This afternoon I am eating at home.

target: Bagaimana kabar keluarga kamu?
english: How is your family doing?
grammar: bagaimana = how: Bagaimana kabar kamu? (How are you?)

target: Bagaimana cara pergi ke stasiun?
english: How do I get to the station?

target: Bagaimana cuaca di Jakarta hari ini?
english: How is the weather in Jakarta today?

target: Hari ini hari Senin, bukan?
english: Today is Monday, isn't it?
grammar: Days take hari first: hari Senin = Monday, hari Sabtu = Saturday.

target: Kami pergi ke pantai hari Sabtu.
english: We are going to the beach on Saturday.

target: Saya tidak bekerja hari Minggu.
english: I do not work on Sunday.

target: Rapat itu hari Jumat jam sepuluh pagi.
english: The meeting is on Friday at ten in the morning.

target: Saya bangun pagi setiap hari.
english: I wake up early every day.

target: Dia mencuci muka di kamar mandi.
english: She washes her face in the bathroom.
grammar: Before c, meN- becomes men-: cuci → mencuci (wash).

target: Ibu memasak nasi goreng untuk sarapan.
english: Mom cooks fried rice for breakfast.
grammar: Roots starting with m keep a simple me-: masak → memasak (cook).

target: Kami sarapan bersama di dapur.
english: We have breakfast together in the kitchen.

target: Saya menulis catatan di buku kecil.
english: I write notes in a small book.
grammar: Before t, meN- becomes men- and the t drops: tulis → menulis (write).

target: Ayah membaca koran setiap pagi.
english: Dad reads the newspaper every morning.
grammar: Before b, meN- becomes mem- and the b stays: baca → membaca (read).

target: Saya membeli kopi sebelum bekerja.
english: I buy coffee before working.

target: Dia bekerja di kantor sampai sore.
english: He works at the office until late afternoon.

target: Kakak menonton televisi setelah makan malam.
english: My older sibling watches television after dinner.

target: Saya tidur jam sepuluh malam.
english: I sleep at ten at night.

target: Setiap pagi saya mandi air dingin.
english: Every morning I bathe with cold water.

target: Dia menyapu lantai sebelum berangkat.
english: She sweeps the floor before leaving.
grammar: Before s, meN- becomes meny- and the s drops: sapu → menyapu (sweep).

target: Saya mengambil handuk dari lemari.
english: I take a towel from the cupboard.
grammar: Vowel-first roots take meng-: ambil → mengambil (take).

target: Ibu mencuci baju setiap hari Sabtu.
english: Mom washes clothes every Saturday.

target: Saya sedang membaca buku baru.
english: I am reading a new book.
grammar: sedang marks an action happening right now: sedang membaca = is reading.

target: Adik menulis surat untuk teman.
english: My younger sibling writes a letter to a friend.

target: Kami memasak makan malam bersama.
english: We cook dinner together.

target: Saya minum teh hangat pagi ini.
english: I drink warm tea this morning.

target: Dia sudah bangun sebelum matahari terbit.
english: He already woke up before sunrise.
grammar: sudah marks a finished action: sudah bangun = already woke up.

target: Saya menutup jendela sebelum tidur.
english: I close the window before sleeping.
grammar: sebelum (before) takes a verb directly: sebelum tidur = before sleeping.

target: Ayah membuka toko jam delapan pagi.
english: Dad opens the shop at eight in the morning.

target: Saya mendengarkan musik sambil memasak.
english: I listen to music while cooking.
grammar: sambil = while (one person, two actions): makan sambil membaca = eat while reading.

target: Setelah kerja saya langsung pulang.
english: After work I go straight home.
grammar: langsung means straight away: langsung pulang = go straight home.

target: Kakak sedang mencuci piring di dapur.
english: My older sibling is washing dishes in the kitchen.

target: Saya memakai baju kerja setiap hari Senin.
english: I wear work clothes every Monday.

target: Dia membawa bekal ke kantor.
english: She brings packed food to the office.

target: Saya menonton berita sebelum berangkat kerja.
english: I watch the news before leaving for work.

target: Anak-anak belajar setelah makan siang.
english: The children study after lunch.

target: Saya mengirim pesan ke teman kerja.
english: I send a message to a coworker.

target: Ibu membangunkan adik jam enam pagi.
english: Mom wakes my younger sibling at six in the morning.
grammar: -kan makes a verb act on someone: bangun (wake up) → membangunkan (wake someone up).

target: Saya menulis daftar belanja untuk besok.
english: I write a shopping list for tomorrow.

target: Dia membacakan cerita untuk anaknya setiap malam.
english: She reads her child a story every night.
grammar: -kan can mean doing it for someone: membaca (read) → membacakan (read aloud to someone).

target: Kami membersihkan rumah di akhir pekan.
english: We clean the house on the weekend.

target: Saya mulai bekerja jam sembilan pagi.
english: I start work at nine in the morning.

target: Ayah mematikan lampu sebelum tidur.
english: Dad turns off the lamp before sleeping.

target: Saya sarapan roti dan telur.
english: I have bread and eggs for breakfast.

target: Dia sedang menulis laporan untuk kantor.
english: He is writing a report for the office.

target: Saya mencuci tangan sebelum makan.
english: I wash my hands before eating.

target: Setiap malam saya membaca sebelum tidur.
english: Every night I read before sleeping.

target: Kami tidur lebih awal di hari kerja.
english: We sleep earlier on workdays.

target: Saya mau pesan nasi goreng satu.
english: I want to order one fried rice.
grammar: mau + verb = want to: mau pesan = want to order.

target: Makanan di warung ini enak sekali.
english: The food at this food stall is very tasty.

target: Tolong jangan terlalu pedas.
english: Please do not make it too spicy.

target: Saya ingin mencoba sate ayam.
english: I want to try chicken satay.

target: Minumnya es teh manis saja.
english: Just sweet iced tea to drink.
grammar: saja means just/only: es teh saja = just iced tea.

target: Berapa harga satu porsi mie goreng?
english: How much is one portion of fried noodles?
grammar: Berapa harga ...? asks a price: Berapa harga kopi ini? = How much is this coffee?

target: Apakah makanan ini pedas?
english: Is this food spicy?

target: Saya pesan ayam goreng dan nasi putih.
english: I order fried chicken and white rice.

target: Boleh minta air putih?
english: May I have plain water?
grammar: Boleh minta ...? politely asks for something: Boleh minta air? = May I have water?

target: Rasanya manis dan sedikit pedas.
english: It tastes sweet and a little spicy.
grammar: -nya can mean the/its: rasa (taste) → rasanya (the taste of it).

target: Kami makan malam di restoran dekat hotel.
english: We have dinner at a restaurant near the hotel.

target: Boleh lihat menunya lagi?
english: May I see the menu again?

target: Saya suka masakan Indonesia.
english: I like Indonesian food.

target: Pelayan itu membawa pesanan kami.
english: The waiter brings our order.

target: Makanannya sudah datang, silakan makan.
english: The food has arrived, please eat.
grammar: silakan politely invites someone to act: silakan makan = please eat.

target: Saya mau membeli oleh-oleh untuk keluarga.
english: I want to buy souvenirs for my family.

target: Berapa harga tas ini?
english: How much is this bag?

target: Wah, itu terlalu mahal untuk saya.
english: Wow, that is too expensive for me.
grammar: terlalu = too (more than you want): terlalu mahal = too expensive.

target: Boleh kurang sedikit harganya?
english: Can the price come down a little?

target: Kalau beli dua, ada diskon?
english: If I buy two, is there a discount?
grammar: kalau means if: kalau beli dua = if (you) buy two.

target: Baju ini murah dan bagus.
english: This shirt is cheap and nice.

target: Saya membeli buah di pasar pagi.
english: I buy fruit at the morning market.

target: Penjual itu memberi saya harga khusus.
english: That seller gives me a special price.

target: Saya membayar dengan uang tunai.
english: I pay with cash.

target: Ada ukuran yang lebih besar?
english: Is there a bigger size?
grammar: yang turns a description into the one that: yang lebih besar = the bigger one.

target: Toko itu tutup hari Minggu.
english: That shop is closed on Sundays.

target: Saya mencari sandal untuk pantai.
english: I am looking for sandals for the beach.

target: Harga di pasar bisa ditawar.
english: Prices at the market can be bargained.
grammar: di- makes a verb passive: tawar (bargain) → ditawar (be bargained over).

target: Dia menjual kain batik yang cantik.
english: She sells beautiful batik cloth.

target: Saya coba dulu baju ini, ya?
english: Let me try this shirt first, okay?
grammar: dulu after a verb means first: coba dulu = try it first.

target: Terima kasih, kembaliannya ambil saja.
english: Thank you, just keep the change.

target: Kami membeli air minum di toko kecil.
english: We buy drinking water at a small shop.

target: Pesanan saya belum datang.
english: My order has not come yet.

target: Kopi di sini lebih murah daripada di hotel.
english: Coffee here is cheaper than at the hotel.
grammar: lebih ... daripada compares: lebih murah daripada di hotel = cheaper than at the hotel.

target: Saya kenyang, makanannya enak sekali.
english: I am full, the food is very tasty.

target: Saya punya dua kakak dan satu adik.
english: I have two older siblings and one younger sibling.
grammar: punya = have: Saya punya adik = I have a younger sibling.

target: Ibu saya suka memasak di rumah.
english: My mother likes to cook at home.
grammar: Possessor comes AFTER the noun: ibu saya = my mother (lit. mother I).

target: Ayah saya bekerja di kantor besar.
english: My father works at a big office.

target: Kakak saya tinggal di Bandung.
english: My older sibling lives in Bandung.

target: Adik saya masih kecil.
english: My younger sibling is still small.

target: Rumah saya dekat pasar.
english: My house is near the market.

target: Anaknya sudah besar sekarang.
english: Her child is already big now.

target: Suami saya suka kopi hitam.
english: My husband likes black coffee.

target: Istrinya orang Bali.
english: His wife is Balinese.

target: Nama teman saya Sari.
english: My friend's name is Sari.

target: Keluarga kami tinggal di Jakarta.
english: Our family lives in Jakarta.
grammar: kami = we (not you); kita = we (with you): keluarga kami = our family.

target: Ibunya sedang tidur di kamar.
english: His mother is sleeping in the bedroom.
grammar: -nya on a noun = his/her: ibunya = his/her mother.

target: Rumahnya besar dan bersih.
english: His house is big and clean.
grammar: No word for 'is' before adjectives: Rumahnya besar = His house (is) big.

target: Dia suka bermain bola dengan temannya.
english: He likes playing football with his friend.

target: Kakek dan nenek saya tinggal di desa.
english: My grandfather and grandmother live in a village.

target: Dia punya banyak teman di sekolah.
english: She has many friends at school.

target: Teman saya sangat baik.
english: My friend is very kind.

target: Orang itu tinggi dan kurus.
english: That person is tall and thin.

target: Adik kamu sudah makan belum?
english: Has your younger sibling eaten yet?
grammar: sudah ... belum? = already or not yet: Sudah makan belum? = Eaten yet?

target: Saya sayang keluarga saya.
english: I love my family.

target: Kami punya satu anak perempuan.
english: We have one daughter.
grammar: anak perempuan = daughter (lit. child female); anak laki-laki = son.

target: Anak laki-laki itu anak saya.
english: That boy is my son.

target: Ibu saya lebih muda dari ayah saya.
english: My mother is younger than my father.
grammar: lebih + adjective + dari = more ... than: lebih muda dari = younger than.

target: Kakak saya menikah tahun lalu.
english: My older sibling got married last year.

target: Suaminya bekerja di rumah sakit.
english: Her husband works at a hospital.

target: Nenek saya pandai memasak rendang.
english: My grandmother is good at cooking rendang.

target: Anak-anak sedang bermain di depan rumah.
english: The children are playing in front of the house.
grammar: Doubling a noun makes it plural: anak-anak = children.

target: Berapa umur kamu sekarang?
english: How old are you now?

target: Umur adik saya sepuluh tahun.
english: My younger sibling is ten years old.

target: Orang tua saya tinggal jauh dari sini.
english: My parents live far from here.
grammar: orang tua = parents (lit. old people): orang tua saya = my parents.

target: Dia anak pertama di keluarganya.
english: He is the first child in his family.

target: Guru saya orang yang sabar.
english: My teacher is a patient person.

target: Teman saya datang dari Surabaya kemarin.
english: My friend came from Surabaya yesterday.

target: Mereka punya rumah baru di kota.
english: They have a new house in the city.

target: Orang-orang di sini sangat ramah.
english: People here are very friendly.

target: Istri saya guru bahasa Inggris.
english: My wife is an English teacher.
grammar: No word for is: Istri saya guru = My wife (is) a teacher.

target: Saya tinggal dengan orang tua saya.
english: I live with my parents.

target: Keluarga besar kami berkumpul setiap tahun.
english: Our extended family gathers every year.
grammar: keluarga besar = extended family (lit. big family).

target: Belok kiri di lampu merah itu.
english: Turn left at that traffic light.
grammar: belok kiri = turn left; belok kanan = turn right.

target: Kantor pos ada di sebelah kanan.
english: The post office is on the right side.

target: Jalan lurus terus sampai pasar.
english: Keep going straight until the market.

target: Hotel itu dekat dengan pantai.
english: That hotel is near the beach.

target: Kantor saya jauh dari rumah.
english: My office is far from home.
grammar: jauh dari = far from; dekat dengan = near to.

target: Saya naik bus ke kantor setiap hari.
english: I take the bus to the office every day.
grammar: naik + vehicle = take/ride: naik bus = take the bus.

target: Dia naik kereta ke Bogor pagi ini.
english: She takes the train to Bogor this morning.

target: Kami naik ojek karena jalan macet.
english: We took a motorcycle taxi because the road was jammed.

target: Tas saya ada di atas meja.
english: My bag is on the table.
grammar: di + position word: di atas meja = on (top of) the table.

target: Kucing itu tidur di bawah kursi.
english: That cat is sleeping under the chair.

target: Kunci ada di dalam tas hitam itu.
english: The key is inside that black bag.

target: Mobil saya parkir di depan gedung.
english: My car is parked in front of the building.
grammar: di depan = in front of; di belakang = behind.

target: Toilet ada di belakang ruang rapat.
english: The toilet is behind the meeting room.

target: Saya bekerja di kantor dekat stasiun.
english: I work at an office near the station.

target: Rapat mulai jam sembilan pagi.
english: The meeting starts at nine in the morning.

target: Bos saya sedang rapat dengan klien.
english: My boss is in a meeting with a client.

target: Saya berangkat ke kantor jam tujuh.
english: I leave for the office at seven.

target: Dari sini ke bandara berapa lama?
english: How long from here to the airport?
grammar: dari ... ke ... = from ... to: dari sini ke bandara = from here to the airport.

target: Naik taksi ke bandara mahal sekali.
english: Taking a taxi to the airport is very expensive.

target: Di mana halte bus terdekat?
english: Where is the nearest bus stop?
grammar: ter- + adjective = the most: terdekat = the nearest, from dekat (near).

target: Halte bus ada di depan bank.
english: The bus stop is in front of the bank.

target: Saya turun di halte berikutnya.
english: I get off at the next stop.
grammar: naik = get on, turun = get off: turun di halte = get off at the stop.

target: Kereta ke Surabaya berangkat jam delapan.
english: The train to Surabaya departs at eight.

target: Maaf, saya datang terlambat ke rapat.
english: Sorry, I came late to the meeting.

target: Kantor kami ada di lantai lima.
english: Our office is on the fifth floor.

target: Saya sudah mengirim email ke bos.
english: I have already sent an email to the boss.

target: Jangan lupa bawa laptop ke rapat.
english: Don't forget to bring a laptop to the meeting.
grammar: jangan = don't (command): Jangan lupa! = Don't forget!

target: Dia sedang bekerja dari rumah hari ini.
english: He is working from home today.

target: Stasiun kereta ada di dekat hotel.
english: The train station is near the hotel.

target: Belok kanan setelah kantor pos.
english: Turn right after the post office.

target: Saya jalan kaki ke pasar setiap pagi.
english: I walk to the market every morning.
grammar: jalan kaki = go on foot: Saya jalan kaki ke pasar = I walk to the market.

target: Minggu ini saya sangat sibuk dengan pekerjaan.
english: This week I am very busy with work.

target: Ruang rapat ada di sebelah dapur.
english: The meeting room is next to the kitchen.

target: Bus itu berhenti di depan sekolah.
english: That bus stops in front of the school.

target: Saya pulang dari kantor naik kereta.
english: I go home from the office by train.

target: Mereka pergi ke luar kota untuk bekerja.
english: They go out of town for work.

target: Selamat, kamu dapat pekerjaan baru itu!
english: Congratulations, you got that new job!

target: Orang yang duduk di sana itu teman saya.
english: The person who is sitting over there is my friend.
grammar: yang links a noun to its description: orang yang duduk = the person who is sitting.

target: Saya mencari buku yang murah untuk adik saya.
english: I am looking for a cheap book for my little sibling.

target: Hotel yang dekat pantai itu sudah penuh.
english: The hotel that is near the beach is already full.

target: Dia teman kerja yang selalu datang pagi.
english: He is a coworker who always arrives early in the morning.

target: Kami suka warung yang buka sampai malam.
english: We like food stalls that stay open until night.

target: Baju yang kamu beli kemarin bagus sekali.
english: The shirt that you bought yesterday is really nice.
grammar: yang also links a noun to what someone did to it: baju yang kamu beli = the shirt that you bought.

target: Siapa nama orang yang berdiri di depan pintu?
english: What is the name of the person standing in front of the door?

target: Rumah yang besar itu rumah nenek saya.
english: That big house is my grandmother's house.

target: Saya mau kamar yang ada jendela besar.
english: I want a room that has a big window.

target: Makanan yang dia masak selalu enak.
english: The food that she cooks is always delicious.
grammar: The verb after yang can keep its own subject: yang dia masak = that she cooks.

target: Bus yang ke bandara berangkat jam enam.
english: The bus that goes to the airport leaves at six.

target: Orang yang menjual buah itu sangat ramah.
english: The person who sells that fruit is very friendly.

target: Saya lupa nama film yang kami tonton kemarin.
english: I forgot the name of the film that we watched yesterday.

target: Tas yang hitam itu punya siapa?
english: Whose bag is the black one?
grammar: yang + adjective works like 'the ... one': yang hitam = the black one.

target: Dia membeli sepatu yang dijual di pasar malam.
english: She bought shoes that are sold at the night market.

target: Anak yang bermain di depan rumah itu anak saya.
english: The child playing in front of that house is my child.

target: Saya butuh orang yang bisa berbicara bahasa Inggris.
english: I need someone who can speak English.
grammar: yang bisa = who can: orang yang bisa berbicara = a person who can speak.

target: Ini bus yang ke stasiun, bukan?
english: This is the bus that goes to the station, isn't it?

target: Guru yang mengajar adik saya sangat sabar.
english: The teacher who teaches my little sibling is very patient.

target: Saya mau kopi yang tidak terlalu manis.
english: I want coffee that is not too sweet.
grammar: yang tidak = 'that is not': kopi yang tidak manis = coffee that isn't sweet.

target: Mereka tinggal di rumah yang dekat kantor pos.
english: They live in a house that is near the post office.

target: Saya sudah membaca laporan yang kamu tulis.
english: I have already read the report that you wrote.

target: Pelayan yang membawa pesanan kami sangat cepat.
english: The waiter who brought our order was very fast.

target: Kamu kenal orang yang tinggal di sebelah?
english: Do you know the person who lives next door?

target: Ini foto keluarga yang kami ambil tahun lalu.
english: This is the family photo that we took last year.

target: Kopi ini lebih enak daripada kopi di kantor.
english: This coffee is tastier than the coffee at the office.
grammar: lebih ... daripada compares two things: lebih enak daripada = tastier than.

target: Naik kereta lebih cepat daripada naik bus.
english: Taking the train is faster than taking the bus.

target: Adik saya sekarang lebih tinggi daripada saya.
english: My younger sibling is now taller than me.

target: Harga di pasar lebih murah daripada di toko.
english: Prices at the market are cheaper than at the shop.
grammar: daripada is only for comparing; 'from' a place is plain dari.

target: Hari ini lebih panas daripada kemarin.
english: Today is hotter than yesterday.

target: Rumah baru kami lebih besar daripada rumah lama.
english: Our new house is bigger than the old house.

target: Saya lebih suka teh daripada kopi.
english: I prefer tea to coffee.
grammar: lebih suka X daripada Y = prefer X to Y: lebih suka teh = prefer tea.

target: Jalan ini lebih macet daripada jalan itu.
english: This road is more congested than that road.

target: Bekerja dari rumah lebih nyaman daripada di kantor.
english: Working from home is more comfortable than at the office.

target: Mana yang lebih murah, taksi atau ojek?
english: Which is cheaper, a taxi or a motorbike taxi?
grammar: mana yang lebih ... asks 'which one is more': mana yang lebih murah? = which is cheaper?

target: Ini restoran paling enak di kota kami.
english: This is the tastiest restaurant in our town.

target: Dia karyawan paling rajin di kantor kami.
english: He is the most diligent employee in our office.
grammar: paling before an adjective makes 'the most': paling rajin = the most diligent.

target: Desember adalah bulan paling sibuk untuk kami.
english: December is the busiest month for us.

target: Siapa yang paling muda di keluarga kamu?
english: Who is the youngest in your family?

target: Kamar ini yang paling murah di hotel ini.
english: This room is the cheapest one in this hotel.

target: Stasiun mana yang paling dekat dari sini?
english: Which station is the closest from here?
grammar: mana after a noun asks 'which': stasiun mana = which station.

target: Sate paling enak ada di warung dekat stasiun.
english: The tastiest satay is at the food stall near the station.

target: Dia orang yang paling sabar di keluarga kami.
english: He is the most patient person in our family.

target: Kakak saya sekarang setinggi ayah saya.
english: My older sibling is now as tall as my father.
grammar: se- + adjective means 'as ... as': setinggi ayah = as tall as father.

target: Kopi di sini semahal kopi di hotel.
english: The coffee here is as expensive as the coffee at the hotel.

target: Rumah barunya sebesar rumah orang tua saya.
english: His new house is as big as my parents' house.

target: Bahasa Indonesia tidak sesulit bahasa Jepang.
english: Indonesian is not as difficult as Japanese.
grammar: tidak se- + adjective = 'not as ... as': tidak sesulit = not as hard as.

target: Kota ini tidak seramai Jakarta.
english: This city is not as crowded as Jakarta.

target: Masakan ibu saya seenak masakan restoran.
english: My mother's cooking is as tasty as restaurant cooking.

target: Hari ini tidak sepanas kemarin.
english: Today is not as hot as yesterday.

target: Tolong tutup pintu itu, di luar dingin.
english: Please close that door, it is cold outside.
grammar: tolong before a verb makes a polite request: tolong tutup pintu = please close the door.

target: Tolong ambil tas saya di kamar depan.
english: Please get my bag in the front room.

target: Tolong kirim laporan itu sebelum jam lima.
english: Please send that report before five o'clock.

target: Tolong bicara pelan-pelan, saya masih belajar.
english: Please speak slowly, I am still learning.
grammar: Doubling an adjective makes a gentle adverb: pelan-pelan = slowly.

target: Tolong tunggu sebentar, saya ambil uang dulu.
english: Please wait a moment, I will get money first.
grammar: dulu after a verb means 'first, before anything else': saya ambil uang dulu.

target: Tolong panggil taksi untuk kami, ya.
english: Please call a taxi for us, okay?
grammar: In requests the bare root is normal: tolong panggil, not tolong memanggil.

target: Tolong bantu saya bawa kotak ini ke atas.
english: Please help me carry this box upstairs.

target: Tolong matikan lampu sebelum kamu keluar.
english: Please turn off the light before you leave.

target: Tolong tulis nama kamu di kertas ini.
english: Please write your name on this paper.

target: Tolong jangan lupa bawa kunci rumah.
english: Please don't forget to bring the house key.

target: Silakan duduk, Pak Budi datang sebentar lagi.
english: Please have a seat, Mr. Budi is coming shortly.
grammar: silakan invites someone to do something: silakan duduk = please have a seat.

target: Silakan masuk, rumah kami sederhana saja.
english: Please come in, our house is just simple.

target: Silakan makan dulu, jangan malu-malu, ya.
english: Please go ahead and eat, don't be shy, okay?

target: Silakan coba dulu sebelum membeli baju itu.
english: Please try it on first before buying that shirt.

target: Silakan tunggu di ruang rapat sebelah kiri.
english: Please wait in the meeting room on the left.

target: Silakan isi nama dan nomor telepon di sini.
english: Please fill in your name and phone number here.

target: Silakan pilih tempat duduk yang masih kosong.
english: Please choose a seat that is still empty.

target: Jangan lupa bawa payung, hari ini akan hujan.
english: Don't forget to bring an umbrella, it is going to rain today.
grammar: jangan lupa = don't forget: jangan lupa bawa payung = don't forget the umbrella.

target: Jangan pergi sekarang, makanannya belum datang.
english: Don't go now, the food hasn't arrived yet.
grammar: jangan + verb = don't: jangan pergi = don't go.

target: Jangan tinggalkan tas kamu di kursi itu.
english: Don't leave your bag on that chair.

target: Jangan bicara keras-keras, adik saya sedang tidur.
english: Don't talk loudly, my little sibling is sleeping.

target: Jangan makan terlalu cepat, nanti sakit perut.
english: Don't eat too fast, you will get a stomachache.
grammar: nanti in a warning means 'or else': nanti sakit perut = you'll get a stomachache.

target: Jangan parkir mobil di depan pintu gedung.
english: Don't park the car in front of the building entrance.

target: Jangan khawatir, saya bisa antar kamu ke stasiun.
english: Don't worry, I can take you to the station.
grammar: jangan khawatir = don't worry — a set phrase you will hear every day.

target: Boleh saya minta segelas air putih?
english: May I have a glass of plain water?
grammar: boleh saya minta = 'may I have': boleh saya minta air? = may I have water?

target: Boleh saya minta menunya, Bu?
english: May I have the menu, ma'am?

target: Boleh saya minta nomor telepon kantor ini?
english: May I have this office's phone number?

target: Boleh saya minta sambal sedikit lagi?
english: May I have a little more chili sauce?

target: Boleh saya pinjam pulpen kamu sebentar?
english: May I borrow your pen for a moment?
grammar: boleh saya + verb asks permission: boleh saya pinjam = may I borrow.

target: Boleh saya buka jendela ini? Panas sekali.
english: May I open this window? It is very hot.

target: Boleh saya bayar dengan kartu di sini?
english: May I pay by card here?

target: Boleh kami duduk di dekat jendela itu?
english: May we sit near that window?

target: Coba dulu sepatu ini sebelum kamu bayar.
english: Try these shoes first before you pay.

target: Coba tanya ke petugas di depan sana.
english: Try asking the attendant over there at the front.
grammar: coba before a verb softens a suggestion: coba tanya = try asking.

target: Coba lihat foto ini, lucu sekali, bukan?
english: Take a look at this photo, it's really cute, isn't it?

target: Coba telepon dia lagi nanti sore.
english: Try calling him again later this afternoon.

target: Coba cicipi sup ini, rasanya enak sekali.
english: Try a taste of this soup, it tastes really good.

target: Mari kita mulai rapat ini sekarang.
english: Let's start this meeting now.
grammar: mari kita + verb = 'let's': mari kita mulai = let's begin.

target: Mari kita makan siang di warung sebelah.
english: Let's have lunch at the food stall next door.

target: Mari kita berfoto bersama di pantai.
english: Let's take a photo together at the beach.
grammar: ber- turns a noun into 'do X': berfoto = take a photo.

target: Mari kita jalan kaki saja, tidak jauh.
english: Let's just walk, it is not far.

target: Mari kita berangkat sebelum jalan macet.
english: Let's leave before the road gets congested.

target: Mari kita istirahat sebentar, saya lelah sekali.
english: Let's rest for a moment, I am really tired.

target: Tolong antar tamu itu ke ruang rapat.
english: Please take that guest to the meeting room.

target: Silakan telepon saya kalau ada masalah.
english: Please call me if there is a problem.
grammar: kalau = if/when in everyday speech: kalau ada masalah = if there is a problem.

target: Jangan tutup toko sebelum jam sembilan malam.
english: Don't close the shop before nine at night.

target: Boleh saya coba baju yang biru itu?
english: May I try on that blue shirt?

target: Tolong jaga tas saya sebentar, ya.
english: Please watch my bag for a moment, okay?

target: Mari kita pesan dua es teh manis.
english: Let's order two sweet iced teas.

target: Jangan lupa istirahat, kamu bekerja terlalu keras.
english: Don't forget to rest, you work too hard.
grammar: terlalu = too (excessively): terlalu keras = too hard.

target: Kemarin saya pergi ke pasar dengan ibu saya.
english: Yesterday I went to the market with my mother.
grammar: Time words do the past-tense work: Kemarin saya pergi. = Yesterday I went. The verb never changes.

target: Tadi pagi saya bangun jam enam.
english: This morning I woke up at six.
grammar: tadi = earlier today: tadi pagi = this morning (already past).

target: Minggu lalu kami pergi ke Yogyakarta naik kereta.
english: Last week we went to Yogyakarta by train.

target: Kemarin sore saya bertemu teman lama di kafe.
english: Yesterday afternoon I met an old friend at a cafe.

target: Tadi malam kami makan sate di dekat rumah.
english: Last night we ate satay near the house.

target: Setelah sarapan, saya langsung berangkat ke kantor.
english: After breakfast, I left for the office right away.
grammar: langsung = straight away: langsung berangkat = leave right away.

target: Sebelum tidur, saya menulis rencana untuk besok.
english: Before sleeping, I wrote a plan for tomorrow.

target: Waktu saya kecil, keluarga kami tinggal di desa.
english: When I was little, our family lived in a village.
grammar: waktu opens a past when-clause: Waktu saya kecil... = When I was little...

target: Kemarin dia pulang kerja jam sembilan malam.
english: Yesterday he came home from work at nine at night.

target: Bulan lalu saya mulai belajar bahasa Indonesia.
english: Last month I started learning Indonesian.
grammar: lalu after a time word = last: bulan lalu = last month, minggu lalu = last week.

target: Tadi pagi saya mandi dulu, lalu sarapan dengan keluarga.
english: This morning I showered first, then had breakfast with my family.
grammar: dulu after a verb means 'first': mandi dulu = shower first, before anything else.

target: Kami masuk museum, kemudian makan siang di taman.
english: We went into the museum, then had lunch in the park.

target: Tadi saya minum kopi, terus lupa membayar.
english: Earlier I drank coffee, and then forgot to pay.
grammar: terus strings actions in speech: ..., terus lupa = ..., and then (I) forgot.

target: Kemarin pagi hujan deras sekali.
english: Yesterday morning it rained really hard.

target: Setelah rapat selesai, kami makan siang bersama.
english: After the meeting ended, we had lunch together.

target: Sebelum berangkat, dia menutup semua jendela.
english: Before leaving, she closed all the windows.

target: Minggu lalu saya menginap di rumah nenek.
english: Last week I stayed over at grandma's house.
grammar: menginap = stay overnight: menginap di rumah nenek = sleep over at grandma's.

target: Waktu kami tiba, toko itu sudah tutup.
english: When we arrived, the shop was already closed.
grammar: sudah inside a story = already: sudah tutup = was already closed.

target: Kemarin saya lupa membawa dompet ke kantor.
english: Yesterday I forgot to bring my wallet to the office.

target: Tadi pagi kereta datang terlambat tiga puluh menit.
english: This morning the train arrived thirty minutes late.

target: Dua hari lalu kami berenang di pantai.
english: Two days ago we swam at the beach.
grammar: lalu after a time span = ago: dua hari lalu = two days ago.

target: Setelah makan malam, ayah bercerita tentang masa kecilnya.
english: After dinner, dad told stories about his childhood.

target: Saya membeli tiket dulu, kemudian menunggu di peron.
english: I bought a ticket first, then waited on the platform.

target: Kemarin malam kami menonton film Indonesia di rumah.
english: Last night we watched an Indonesian film at home.

target: Tadi siang saya makan bakso di warung sebelah.
english: At midday I ate meatball soup at the food stall next door.

target: Tahun lalu mereka pindah ke Surabaya.
english: Last year they moved to Surabaya.

target: Sebelum pergi, jangan lupa kunci pintu depan.
english: Before going, don't forget to lock the front door.
grammar: jangan lupa = don't forget: Jangan lupa kunci pintu. = Don't forget to lock the door.

target: Waktu hujan turun, kami berteduh di halte bus.
english: When the rain came down, we took shelter at the bus stop.

target: Setelah pulang sekolah, anak-anak bermain di halaman.
english: After coming home from school, the kids played in the yard.

target: Kemarin saya menelepon ibu saya di kampung.
english: Yesterday I called my mother back in the village.

target: Tadi pagi saya jalan kaki ke stasiun.
english: This morning I walked to the station.

target: Minggu lalu bos saya pergi ke Singapura.
english: Last week my boss went to Singapore.

target: Kami berbelanja di pasar, lalu memasak bersama.
english: We shopped at the market, then cooked together.

target: Setelah film selesai, kami langsung pulang.
english: After the film ended, we went straight home.

target: Kemarin sore saya mampir ke rumah teman.
english: Yesterday afternoon I dropped by a friend's house.
grammar: mampir = drop by: mampir ke rumah teman = stop by a friend's place.

target: Waktu saya di Bali, saya belajar sedikit bahasa daerah.
english: When I was in Bali, I learned a bit of the local language.

target: Tadi malam saya begadang karena pekerjaan.
english: Last night I stayed up late because of work.
grammar: begadang = stay up late into the night — one everyday word, no extra phrase needed.

target: Sebelum makan, kami berdoa bersama.
english: Before eating, we prayed together.

target: Dua minggu lalu kami berlibur ke Lombok.
english: Two weeks ago we went on holiday to Lombok.
grammar: berlibur = go on holiday, from libur (day off): berlibur ke Lombok.

target: Setelah itu, kami minum es kelapa di pantai.
english: After that, we drank iced coconut on the beach.
grammar: Setelah itu = after that — the glue between story sentences.

target: Kemarin dia lupa mematikan lampu dapur.
english: Yesterday he forgot to turn off the kitchen light.

target: Tadi pagi saya memberi makan kucing kami.
english: This morning I fed our cat.

target: Waktu kecil, dia sering berenang di sungai.
english: When he was little, he often swam in the river.

target: Setelah kelas selesai, kami minum teh bersama.
english: After class ended, we drank tea together.

target: Kemarin kami menjemput tamu di bandara.
english: Yesterday we picked up guests at the airport.

target: Bulan lalu harga beras naik lagi.
english: Last month the price of rice went up again.

target: Tadi sore anak saya pulang sekolah lebih awal.
english: This afternoon my child came home from school early.

target: Sebelum rapat mulai, saya membaca laporan itu.
english: Before the meeting started, I read the report.

target: Minggu lalu kami mengunjungi kakek di desa.
english: Last week we visited grandpa in the village.

target: Kemarin malam listrik mati selama dua jam.
english: Last night the electricity was out for two hours.
grammar: selama = for (a duration): selama dua jam = for two hours.

target: Saya sakit kepala sejak tadi pagi.
english: I have had a headache since this morning.
grammar: sakit + body part = it hurts: sakit kepala = headache, sakit perut = stomachache.

target: Perut saya sakit setelah makan pedas.
english: My stomach hurts after eating spicy food.

target: Anak saya demam sejak kemarin malam.
english: My child has had a fever since last night.
grammar: sejak = since: sejak kemarin malam = since last night.

target: Kamu harus pergi ke dokter hari ini.
english: You have to go to the doctor today.

target: Saya mau minum obat dulu sebelum tidur.
english: I want to take my medicine first before sleeping.
grammar: minum obat = take medicine — literally 'drink medicine', even for pills.

target: Gigi saya sakit sekali, saya perlu dokter gigi.
english: My tooth really hurts, I need a dentist.

target: Dia tidak masuk kerja karena sakit flu.
english: He did not come to work because he has the flu.

target: Cepat sembuh, ya! Istirahat yang cukup.
english: Get well soon! Get enough rest.
grammar: Cepat sembuh! = Get well soon — the standard sympathy phrase.

target: Ibu membeli obat batuk di apotek.
english: Mom bought cough medicine at the pharmacy.

target: Pagi ini saya pusing dan mual.
english: This morning I feel dizzy and nauseous.

target: Badan saya capek setelah kerja seminggu penuh.
english: My body is worn out after a full week of work.
grammar: capek = tired (everyday speech); lelah is its slightly dressier twin.

target: Tenggorokan saya sakit, susah menelan.
english: My throat hurts, it is hard to swallow.

target: Kaki saya luka karena jatuh dari sepeda.
english: My leg got injured because I fell off my bike.

target: Dokter bilang saya harus istirahat tiga hari.
english: The doctor said I have to rest for three days.
grammar: bilang = say, the conversational verb: Dokter bilang... = The doctor said...

target: Apakah ada apotek dekat hotel ini?
english: Is there a pharmacy near this hotel?

target: Saya mencari obat untuk sakit kepala.
english: I am looking for medicine for a headache.

target: Jangan lupa minum obat tiga kali sehari.
english: Don't forget to take your medicine three times a day.
grammar: kali = times: tiga kali sehari = three times a day.

target: Dia sedang istirahat di kamar karena demam.
english: She is resting in her room because of a fever.

target: Mata saya lelah karena bekerja di depan komputer.
english: My eyes are tired from working in front of the computer.

target: Ayah pergi ke rumah sakit untuk periksa kesehatan.
english: Dad went to the hospital for a health check-up.
grammar: ke-...-an builds nouns: sehat (healthy) becomes kesehatan (health).

target: Perawat itu memeriksa tekanan darah saya.
english: The nurse checked my blood pressure.

target: Setelah minum obat, dia merasa lebih baik.
english: After taking the medicine, she felt better.

target: Tangan saya sakit setelah mengangkat kotak berat.
english: My hand hurts after lifting heavy boxes.

target: Saya batuk terus sejak dua hari lalu.
english: I have been coughing constantly since two days ago.
grammar: terus after a verb = keeps on: batuk terus = keeps coughing.

target: Kalau masih demam besok, pergi ke dokter, ya.
english: If you still have a fever tomorrow, go to the doctor, okay.

target: Punggung saya sakit karena duduk terlalu lama.
english: My back hurts from sitting too long.

target: Dia alergi obat itu, jadi hati-hati.
english: He is allergic to that medicine, so be careful.

target: Saya mau membuat janji dengan dokter gigi.
english: I want to make an appointment with the dentist.
grammar: membuat janji = make an appointment: membuat janji dengan dokter gigi.

target: Anak itu menangis karena giginya sakit.
english: That child is crying because his tooth hurts.

target: Minum air putih yang banyak supaya cepat sembuh.
english: Drink lots of water so you get better quickly.
grammar: supaya = so that: supaya cepat sembuh = so you recover fast.

target: Kepala saya pusing kalau kurang tidur.
english: I get dizzy when I don't get enough sleep.

target: Dokter memberi saya resep obat baru.
english: The doctor gave me a prescription for new medicine.

target: Anak-anak menyikat gigi sebelum tidur.
english: The children brush their teeth before bed.

target: Badan saya panas, mungkin saya demam.
english: My body feels hot, maybe I have a fever.
grammar: mungkin = maybe: Mungkin saya demam. = Maybe I have a fever.

target: Dia dirawat di rumah sakit selama tiga hari.
english: He was treated in the hospital for three days.

target: Saya minta izin pulang cepat karena sakit.
english: I asked permission to go home early because I am sick.
grammar: minta izin = ask permission: minta izin pulang = ask to leave early.

target: Olahraga setiap pagi membuat badan sehat.
english: Exercising every morning keeps the body healthy.

target: Hidung saya tersumbat karena pilek.
english: My nose is blocked because of a cold.

target: Kakek saya jalan pelan-pelan karena kakinya sakit.
english: My grandpa walks slowly because his leg hurts.

target: Semoga kamu cepat sembuh dan sehat kembali.
english: I hope you get well soon and are healthy again.
grammar: Semoga = I hope: Semoga cepat sembuh. = Hope you get better soon.

target: Saya tidak bisa tidur karena batuk semalaman.
english: I could not sleep because I was coughing all night.

target: Perawat itu sangat ramah kepada pasien.
english: That nurse is very friendly to the patients.

target: Obat ini harus diminum setelah makan.
english: This medicine must be taken after eating.
grammar: di- flips the verb passive: diminum = is taken (drunk).

target: Dia terjatuh di tangga dan kakinya luka.
english: He fell on the stairs and injured his leg.

target: Minggu lalu saya memeriksakan mata di klinik.
english: Last week I had my eyes checked at a clinic.

target: Istirahat dulu, pekerjaan bisa menunggu sampai besok.
english: Rest first, the work can wait until tomorrow.

target: Telinga saya sakit setelah berenang di kolam.
english: My ear hurts after swimming in the pool.

target: Dia minum vitamin setiap pagi supaya tidak mudah sakit.
english: She takes vitamins every morning so she doesn't get sick easily.

target: Kalau capek, jangan lupa istirahat sebentar.
english: If you are tired, don't forget to rest for a bit.

target: Terima kasih, saya sudah merasa jauh lebih baik.
english: Thank you, I already feel much better.

target: Hari ini cuacanya cerah sekali.
english: The weather today is really clear.

target: Kalau hujan, saya naik taksi ke kantor.
english: If it rains, I take a taxi to the office.
grammar: kalau starts an if-clause; no 'then' word needed after the comma: Kalau hujan, saya naik taksi.

target: Di luar sedang hujan deras.
english: It is raining heavily outside.

target: Jangan lupa bawa payung hari ini.
english: Don't forget to bring an umbrella today.
grammar: Jangan lupa + verb = don't forget to: Jangan lupa bawa payung.

target: Langit mendung, mungkin sebentar lagi hujan.
english: The sky is overcast, maybe it will rain soon.

target: Musim hujan di Jakarta mulai bulan November.
english: The rainy season in Jakarta starts in November.

target: Saya tidak suka udara panas dan lembap.
english: I don't like hot and humid air.

target: Cuaca di Bandung lebih sejuk daripada di Jakarta.
english: The weather in Bandung is cooler than in Jakarta.
grammar: lebih + adjective + daripada compares: lebih sejuk daripada Jakarta = cooler than Jakarta.

target: Apakah besok akan hujan lagi?
english: Will it rain again tomorrow?

target: Kalau cuaca cerah, kami pergi ke pantai.
english: If the weather is clear, we go to the beach.

target: Anginnya kencang sekali malam ini.
english: The wind is really strong tonight.

target: Jalan di depan rumah kami banjir lagi.
english: The street in front of our house is flooded again.

target: Musim kemarau biasanya mulai bulan Mei.
english: The dry season usually starts in May.
grammar: musim = season. Indonesia has two: musim hujan (rainy) and musim kemarau (dry).

target: Hari ini panas sekali, sampai tiga puluh lima derajat.
english: It is very hot today, up to thirty-five degrees.

target: Saya kehujanan waktu pulang dari pasar tadi.
english: I got caught in the rain coming home from the market earlier.
grammar: ke-…-an around a noun = affected by it: kehujanan = caught in the rain.

target: Bawa jas hujan kalau naik motor hari ini.
english: Bring a raincoat if you ride a motorbike today.

target: Udara pagi di gunung dingin dan segar.
english: The morning air in the mountains is cold and fresh.

target: Kalau banjir, anak-anak tidak pergi ke sekolah.
english: If there is a flood, the children don't go to school.

target: Cuaca hari ini bagus untuk jalan-jalan.
english: Today's weather is good for going out for a stroll.
grammar: Doubling a verb relaxes it: jalan-jalan = to stroll, go out (not just 'walk').

target: Sudah tiga hari hujan tidak berhenti.
english: It has been raining nonstop for three days.

target: Di musim kemarau, sungai kecil itu kering.
english: In the dry season, that small river is dry.

target: Besok kami mendaki gunung kalau tidak hujan.
english: Tomorrow we will climb the mountain if it doesn't rain.

target: Baju saya basah karena hujan tadi sore.
english: My clothes are wet because of the rain this afternoon.

target: Jemur pakaian di luar, hari ini panas.
english: Hang the laundry outside, it is hot today.

target: Kalau malam, suhu di sini turun.
english: At night, the temperature here drops.

target: Kata ramalan cuaca, besok akan cerah.
english: According to the weather forecast, tomorrow will be clear.
grammar: kata + source = 'according to': Kata ramalan cuaca, besok cerah.

target: Saya suka duduk di teras waktu hujan.
english: I like sitting on the terrace when it rains.

target: Kalau panas begini, saya minum es teh.
english: When it is hot like this, I drink iced tea.
grammar: begini = 'like this': panas begini = hot like this.

target: Musim dingin di Jepang mulai bulan Desember.
english: Winter in Japan starts in December.

target: Awan hitam itu tanda hujan akan turun.
english: Those black clouds are a sign rain is coming.

target: Kami berteduh di halte sampai hujan berhenti.
english: We took shelter at the bus stop until the rain stopped.

target: Jalanan licin, hati-hati kalau naik motor.
english: The roads are slippery, be careful if you ride a motorbike.

target: Tahun ini ada banjir besar di kota kami.
english: This year there was a big flood in our city.

target: Anak saya senang main hujan di halaman.
english: My child loves playing in the rain in the yard.

target: Pakai topi, matahari siang ini terik sekali.
english: Wear a hat, the midday sun is really scorching.

target: Kalau mendung begini, jangan jemur pakaian dulu.
english: When it is overcast like this, don't hang out the laundry yet.
grammar: dulu after a command = 'for now / yet': Jangan jemur dulu = don't hang it out yet.

target: Tadi siang cuaca di pantai panas sekali.
english: At midday today the weather at the beach was very hot.

target: Hujan gerimis tidak apa-apa, kita tetap jalan.
english: A little drizzle is fine, we are still going.
grammar: tidak apa-apa = 'it's okay, no problem' — the everyday reassurance phrase.

target: Setelah hujan, udara jadi sejuk dan bersih.
english: After the rain, the air becomes cool and clean.
grammar: jadi before an adjective = 'becomes': udara jadi sejuk = the air turns cool.

target: Banjir kemarin masuk sampai ke dalam rumah.
english: Yesterday's flood came all the way into the house.

target: Saya selalu mengecek ramalan cuaca sebelum berangkat.
english: I always check the weather forecast before leaving.

target: Kalau musim hujan, bawa payung ke mana-mana.
english: In the rainy season, take an umbrella everywhere.
grammar: Doubled mana = 'everywhere': ke mana-mana (to everywhere), di mana-mana (everywhere).

target: Kalau sore, angin laut di sini enak sekali.
english: In the late afternoon, the sea breeze here is really pleasant.

target: Kantor kami tutup karena banjir besar hari ini.
english: Our office is closed because of the big flood today.

target: Jangan berenang di laut kalau ombaknya besar.
english: Don't swim in the sea when the waves are big.

target: Kemarin hujan es turun di kota Bandung.
english: Yesterday hail fell in the city of Bandung.
grammar: hujan es = hail, literally 'ice rain': Kemarin hujan es turun.

target: Cuaca panas membuat saya cepat lelah.
english: Hot weather makes me tired quickly.

target: Kalau dingin, ibu membuat teh jahe hangat.
english: When it is cold, Mom makes warm ginger tea.

target: Musim hujan tahun ini datang lebih awal.
english: This year's rainy season came earlier.

target: Sepatu saya kotor karena jalan masih basah.
english: My shoes are dirty because the road is still wet.

target: Apa yang biasanya kamu lakukan di waktu luang?
english: What do you usually do in your free time?
grammar: waktu luang = free time: di waktu luang = in your free time.

target: Saya suka membaca novel sebelum tidur.
english: I like reading novels before sleeping.
grammar: suka + verb = like doing something: suka membaca = like reading.

target: Setiap akhir pekan kami bermain sepak bola.
english: Every weekend we play soccer.
grammar: akhir pekan = weekend ('end of week'): setiap akhir pekan = every weekend.

target: Kakak saya biasanya berenang setiap hari Minggu.
english: My older sibling usually swims every Sunday.
grammar: biasanya (usually) sits before the verb: Dia biasanya berenang hari Minggu.

target: Kadang-kadang saya menonton film di bioskop.
english: Sometimes I watch movies at the cinema.
grammar: kadang-kadang = sometimes: Kadang-kadang saya menonton film.

target: Ayah suka memancing di sungai dekat rumah.
english: Dad likes fishing in the river near the house.

target: Kami sekeluarga suka memasak bersama hari Minggu.
english: Our whole family likes cooking together on Sundays.
grammar: se- + noun = one whole unit: sekeluarga = the whole family, sekelas = the whole class.

target: Saya belajar main gitar dari video di internet.
english: I am learning to play guitar from videos on the internet.

target: Teman kantor saya suka bersepeda ke mana-mana.
english: My office friend likes cycling everywhere.

target: Musik apa yang biasanya kamu dengarkan?
english: What music do you usually listen to?
grammar: yang links a question word to its verb: Musik apa yang kamu suka? = what music do you like?

target: Setiap pagi dia lari di taman kota.
english: Every morning he runs in the city park.

target: Hobi saya menggambar wajah orang di kereta.
english: My hobby is drawing people's faces on the train.

target: Akhir pekan ini kami mau menonton konser musik.
english: This weekend we want to watch a music concert.

target: Saya suka memasak makanan Korea di rumah.
english: I like cooking Korean food at home.

target: Dia bisa bermain piano sejak kecil.
english: She has been able to play the piano since she was little.
grammar: sejak = since: sejak kecil = since childhood, sejak tadi = for a while now.

target: Kami biasanya jalan-jalan ke mal hari Sabtu.
english: We usually go out to the mall on Saturdays.

target: Suami saya suka menanam sayur di kebun kecil.
english: My husband likes growing vegetables in a small garden.

target: Setelah kerja, saya berolahraga di gym dekat kantor.
english: After work, I exercise at the gym near the office.

target: Film Indonesia sekarang bagus-bagus sekali.
english: Indonesian films these days are all really good.
grammar: Doubling an adjective spreads it over many items: bagus-bagus = all (of them) good.

target: Anak saya suka menyanyikan lagu anak-anak.
english: My child likes singing children's songs.
grammar: menyanyikan = sing something: menyanyikan lagu = to sing a song.

target: Saya membaca berita di ponsel setiap pagi.
english: I read the news on my phone every morning.

target: Kadang-kadang kami bermain kartu sampai larut malam.
english: Sometimes we play cards until late at night.

target: Olahraga apa yang paling kamu suka?
english: What sport do you like the most?
grammar: paling = the most: paling suka = like most, paling bagus = the best.

target: Di waktu luang, dia menulis cerita pendek.
english: In her free time, she writes short stories.

target: Kami menonton pertandingan bola di rumah teman.
english: We watch the football match at a friend's house.

target: Saya baru mulai belajar memasak masakan Padang.
english: I just started learning to cook Padang cuisine.
grammar: baru before a verb = just (recently): baru mulai = just started.

target: Setiap sore anak-anak bermain layang-layang di lapangan.
english: Every afternoon the children fly kites on the field.

target: Ibu saya suka menarikan tarian tradisional Bali.
english: My mother likes dancing traditional Balinese dances.
grammar: menarikan = dance a specific dance: menarikan tarian Bali.

target: Akhir pekan lalu kami mendaki gunung bersama.
english: Last weekend we hiked a mountain together.

target: Saya lebih suka membaca buku daripada menonton televisi.
english: I prefer reading books to watching television.
grammar: lebih suka X daripada Y = prefer X to Y: lebih suka membaca daripada menonton.

target: Dia memotret pemandangan waktu jalan-jalan.
english: He photographs scenery while traveling around.

target: Kolam renang dekat rumah buka sampai jam sembilan.
english: The swimming pool near the house is open until nine o'clock.

target: Teman saya suka main catur setelah makan siang.
english: My friend likes playing chess after lunch.

target: Biasanya saya mendengarkan musik waktu membersihkan rumah.
english: I usually listen to music while cleaning the house.

target: Apa yang biasanya kamu lakukan hari Minggu?
english: What do you usually do on Sundays?

target: Kami suka mencoba kafe baru setiap bulan.
english: We like trying a new cafe every month.

target: Dia berlatih badminton dua kali seminggu.
english: He practices badminton twice a week.
grammar: kali counts times: dua kali seminggu = twice a week, sekali = once.

target: Saya suka masak, tapi tidak suka cuci piring.
english: I like cooking, but I don't like washing dishes.
grammar: In conversation the meN- prefix often drops: memasak → masak, mencuci → cuci.

target: Setiap Jumat malam kami berkumpul dan bernyanyi bersama.
english: Every Friday night we get together and sing.
grammar: Jumat malam = Friday night; malam Jumat means Thursday night (the eve of Friday).

target: Menonton film horor bukan hobi saya.
english: Watching horror films is not my hobby.
grammar: bukan negates nouns, tidak negates verbs: bukan hobi saya = not my hobby.

target: Dia belajar bahasa Jepang sebagai hobi baru.
english: She is learning Japanese as a new hobby.

target: Kami main musik bersama di garasi setiap Sabtu.
english: We play music together in the garage every Saturday.

target: Saya suka membuat kue untuk teman kantor.
english: I like making cakes for my office friends.

target: Kapan kamu biasanya punya waktu luang?
english: When do you usually have free time?

target: Akhir pekan depan ada festival musik di pantai.
english: Next weekend there is a music festival at the beach.
grammar: depan after a time word = next: akhir pekan depan = next weekend, bulan depan = next month.

target: Dia jarang menonton televisi, lebih suka membaca.
english: He rarely watches television, he prefers reading.
grammar: jarang = rarely, before the verb: Dia jarang menonton televisi.

target: Bermain game di ponsel itu hobi anak muda sekarang.
english: Playing games on the phone is young people's hobby now.

target: Saya menulis catatan perjalanan setiap kali liburan.
english: I write travel notes every time I go on vacation.

target: Kadang-kadang kami membakar sate di halaman belakang.
english: Sometimes we grill satay in the backyard.
grammar: membakar = to grill or burn: membakar sate = to grill satay.

target: Hobi baru saya memotret burung di taman.
english: My new hobby is photographing birds in the park.

target: Kita bertemu jam tujuh malam, ya?
english: We are meeting at seven tonight, okay?
grammar: jam + number tells the time: jam tujuh = seven o'clock; jam berapa? = what time?

target: Nanti malam kamu ada acara tidak?
english: Do you have any plans tonight?
grammar: nanti = later (today): nanti malam = tonight; nanti sore = later this afternoon.

target: Saya mau mengajak kamu makan malam.
english: I want to invite you to dinner.

target: Boleh saya menelepon kamu nanti sore?
english: May I call you later this afternoon?

target: Kirim pesan saja kalau kamu sudah tiba.
english: Just send a message when you have arrived.

target: Maaf, saya terlambat lima belas menit.
english: Sorry, I am fifteen minutes late.

target: Jadi kita ketemu di mana besok?
english: So where are we meeting tomorrow?
grammar: ketemu is the everyday spoken form of bertemu: ketemu jam lima = meet at five.

target: Maaf, rencana kita tidak jadi, ya.
english: Sorry, our plan is not happening after all.
grammar: tidak jadi = (a plan) falls through: Piknik tidak jadi = the picnic is off.

target: Saya ada janji dengan dokter gigi.
english: I have an appointment with the dentist.
grammar: janji = promise or appointment: ada janji = to have an appointment.

target: Dia tidak mengangkat telepon saya tadi.
english: She did not answer my call earlier.

target: Boleh saya minta nomor telepon kamu?
english: May I have your phone number?
grammar: boleh = may (permission): Boleh saya minta nomornya? = may I have the number?

target: Saya akan menelepon kantor itu besok pagi.
english: I will call that office tomorrow morning.

target: Kami berjanji bertemu di depan bioskop.
english: We promised to meet in front of the cinema.

target: Kamu bisa datang jam berapa nanti?
english: What time can you come later?

target: Ayo kita menonton film hari Sabtu ini.
english: Come on, let's watch a movie this Saturday.
grammar: ayo = come on, let's: Ayo kita makan = let's eat.

target: Saya sibuk hari Senin, bagaimana hari Selasa?
english: I am busy on Monday, how about Tuesday?

target: Baik, sampai nanti di kafe ya.
english: Alright, see you later at the cafe.
grammar: sampai nanti = see you later (lit. until later); sampai jumpa = see you.

target: Dia mengirim pesan tapi saya belum membalas.
english: He sent a message but I have not replied yet.

target: Tolong telepon saya kalau kamu tidak bisa datang.
english: Please call me if you cannot come.

target: Kita jadi pergi ke pantai hari Minggu?
english: Are we still going to the beach on Sunday?
grammar: jadi checks a plan is still on: Jadi pergi? = are we still going?

target: Saya lupa menelepon ibu saya kemarin.
english: I forgot to call my mother yesterday.

target: Jangan lupa janji kita jam dua siang.
english: Do not forget our appointment at two in the afternoon.

target: Rapat besok tidak jadi karena bos sakit.
english: Tomorrow's meeting is off because the boss is sick.

target: Dia menelepon saya tiga kali tadi malam.
english: She called me three times last night.

target: Kapan kamu ada waktu minggu ini?
english: When do you have time this week?

target: Saya mengirim alamat hotelnya lewat pesan, ya.
english: I will send the hotel's address by message, okay.
grammar: -nya can mean 'the': hotelnya = the hotel; kuncinya = the key.

target: Kami akan berkumpul di rumah nenek hari Minggu.
english: We will gather at grandma's house on Sunday.

target: Mereka mengundang kami ke pesta pernikahan.
english: They invited us to a wedding party.

target: Tunggu sebentar, ada telepon masuk.
english: Wait a moment, there is an incoming call.

target: Saya berangkat sekarang, tunggu saya di lobi.
english: I am leaving now, wait for me in the lobby.

target: Maaf, tadi saya tidak mendengar ponsel saya berbunyi.
english: Sorry, I did not hear my phone ring earlier.

target: Bagaimana kalau kita bertemu jam sepuluh saja?
english: How about we meet at ten instead?
grammar: saja softens suggestions: jam sepuluh saja = let's just make it ten.

target: Acara mulai jam delapan, jangan terlambat ya.
english: The event starts at eight, do not be late.
grammar: jangan = do not: Jangan terlambat! = don't be late!

target: Saya sedang menunggu balasan darinya.
english: I am waiting for a reply from him.

target: Kamu mau ikut kami ke konser besok malam?
english: Do you want to come with us to the concert tomorrow night?

target: Nanti saya menjemput kamu di stasiun kereta.
english: I will pick you up at the train station later.

target: Dia berjanji akan datang, tapi tidak muncul.
english: He promised he would come, but did not show up.

target: Telepon dari kantor tadi penting sekali.
english: That call from the office earlier was very important.

target: Kita makan siang bersama hari Kamis, bisa?
english: Can we have lunch together on Thursday?

target: Saya harus membatalkan janji kita sore ini.
english: I have to cancel our appointment this afternoon.
grammar: membatalkan = to cancel (root batal): membatalkan janji = cancel an appointment.

target: Jam berapa pesawat kamu tiba besok?
english: What time does your plane arrive tomorrow?

target: Saya menelepon hotel untuk mengubah pesanan kamar.
english: I called the hotel to change the room booking.

target: Kalau tidak jadi hujan, kita jalan-jalan sore.
english: If it does not end up raining, we will take a walk in the late afternoon.

target: Sinyal di sini jelek, saya akan menelepon lagi.
english: The signal here is bad, I will call again.

target: Dia selalu sibuk, susah sekali ditelepon.
english: He is always busy, very hard to reach by phone.
grammar: di- makes a verb passive: ditelepon = to be called; ditunggu = to be waited for.

target: Akhirnya kita bisa bertemu lagi minggu depan.
english: Finally we can meet again next week.

target: Tolong ingatkan saya soal rapat besok pagi.
english: Please remind me about tomorrow morning's meeting.

target: HP saya mati, jadi saya pinjam HP teman.
english: My phone died, so I borrowed a friend's phone.
grammar: HP (say: ha-pe) is the spoken word for phone: HP saya mati = my phone died.

target: Kita ketemu di depan pintu masuk mal, ya.
english: We will meet in front of the mall entrance, okay.
grammar: ketemu is the spoken form of bertemu: kita ketemu jam lima = we meet at five.

target: Senang sekali akhirnya bisa bertemu kamu lagi.
english: So happy to finally be able to see you again.

target: Rumah kami punya tiga kamar tidur.
english: Our house has three bedrooms.

target: Kamar mandi ada di lantai dua.
english: The bathroom is on the second floor.
grammar: lantai dua = the second floor: storeys use plain numbers after lantai.

target: Ibu sedang membersihkan dapur sekarang.
english: Mom is cleaning the kitchen right now.

target: Mobil merah itu punya tetangga kami.
english: That red car belongs to our neighbor.
grammar: Adjectives follow the noun: mobil merah = red car (lit. car red).

target: Saya suka memakai baju biru ke kantor.
english: I like wearing blue clothes to the office.
grammar: memakai = to wear or use: memakai baju biru = wear a blue shirt.

target: Lemari di kamar saya sudah penuh.
english: The wardrobe in my room is already full.

target: Kunci rumah ada di dalam laci meja.
english: The house key is in the desk drawer.

target: Dinding ruang tamu kami putih bersih.
english: Our living room walls are a clean white.

target: Adik memilih sepatu hitam untuk sekolah.
english: My little sibling chose black shoes for school.

target: Jendela kamar saya menghadap ke taman.
english: My bedroom window faces the garden.

target: Tolong tutup pintu dapur itu, ya.
english: Please close that kitchen door, okay.

target: Kami menaruh sofa baru di ruang tamu.
english: We put the new sofa in the living room.

target: Warna apa yang paling kamu suka?
english: What color do you like the most?
grammar: paling = the most: paling suka = like best; paling besar = the biggest.

target: Saya membeli gorden kuning untuk kamar anak.
english: I bought yellow curtains for the child's room.

target: Kulkas kami rusak sejak kemarin sore.
english: Our fridge has been broken since yesterday afternoon.

target: Dia memakai jaket hijau dan topi putih.
