english: He is wearing a green jacket and a white hat.

target: Lampu di kamar mandi tidak mau menyala.
english: The light in the bathroom will not turn on.
grammar: tidak mau + verb for things = won't: lampunya tidak mau menyala = it won't turn on.

target: Tolong nyalakan lampu ruang tamu, sudah gelap.
english: Please turn on the living room light, it is dark already.
grammar: -kan turns a state into an action: menyala = be on, nyalakan = turn it on.

target: Jangan lupa mematikan kompor sebelum pergi.
english: Do not forget to turn off the stove before leaving.
grammar: mematikan = to turn off (lit. make dead): mematikan lampu = turn off the light.

target: Handuk bersih ada di lemari kamar mandi.
english: Clean towels are in the bathroom cupboard.

target: Celana hitam itu terlalu panjang untuk saya.
english: Those black trousers are too long for me.
grammar: terlalu = too (excessive): terlalu panjang = too long; terlalu mahal = too expensive.

target: Saya menyimpan paspor di dalam tas biru.
english: I keep my passport inside the blue bag.

target: Halaman belakang rumah nenek luas sekali.
english: Grandma's backyard is very spacious.

target: Kaus kaki saya hilang sebelah di kamar.
english: One of my socks is missing in the room.
grammar: sebelah = one of a pair: hilang sebelah = one of the two is missing.

target: Kemeja putih ini cocok dengan celana biru.
english: This white shirt goes well with blue trousers.
grammar: cocok = to match or suit: cocok dengan = goes well with.

target: Kami makan malam di meja kayu yang besar.
english: We have dinner at the big wooden table.
grammar: yang picks out 'the ... one': meja yang besar = the big table.

target: Ada cermin besar di dekat pintu kamar.
english: There is a big mirror near the bedroom door.

target: Ayah sedang mengecat pagar warna hijau.
english: Dad is painting the fence green.

target: Karpet ruang tamu kami merah tua.
english: Our living room carpet is dark red.
grammar: tua darkens a color, muda lightens it: merah tua = dark red; biru muda = light blue.

target: Saya mencuci piring dan gelas setelah makan.
english: I wash the plates and glasses after eating.

target: Baju kuning muda itu bagus untuk pesta.
english: That light yellow dress is nice for a party.

target: Kamar hotel kami menghadap ke kolam renang.
english: Our hotel room faces the swimming pool.

target: Tas hijau di kursi itu punya siapa?
english: Whose green bag is that on the chair?
grammar: punya siapa? = whose?: Tas ini punya siapa? = whose bag is this?

target: Dapur rumah baru kami kecil tapi bersih.
english: The kitchen of our new house is small but clean.

target: Dia mengganti seprai setiap minggu.
english: She changes the sheets every week.

target: Sepatu putih saya kotor karena hujan kemarin.
english: My white shoes are dirty because of the rain yesterday.

target: Di garasi ada dua sepeda dan satu mobil.
english: There are two bicycles and one car in the garage.
grammar: ada = there is/are: Di garasi ada sepeda = there is a bicycle in the garage.

target: Saya lebih suka warna biru daripada merah.
english: I prefer blue to red.
grammar: lebih ... daripada = more ... than: lebih suka biru daripada merah = prefer blue to red.

target: Anak-anak menggambar di lantai kamar mereka.
english: The children are drawing on the floor of their room.

target: Jaket hitam itu tergantung di belakang pintu.
english: That black jacket is hanging behind the door.
grammar: ter- describes a state: tergantung = hanging; tertutup = closed.

target: Kami memasang gorden baru di jendela dapur.
english: We put up new curtains on the kitchen window.

target: Bantal dan selimut ada di atas tempat tidur.
english: The pillow and blanket are on top of the bed.

target: Rok merah itu cocok sekali untuk kamu.
english: That red skirt really suits you.

target: Ibu menyapu lantai dapur setiap pagi.
english: Mom sweeps the kitchen floor every morning.
grammar: setiap = every: setiap pagi = every morning; setiap hari = every day.

target: Rumah putih di ujung jalan itu milik paman saya.
english: The white house at the end of the street belongs to my uncle.

target: Saya perlu membeli sabun dan sampo baru.
english: I need to buy new soap and shampoo.

target: Topi biru tua ini hadiah dari kakak.
english: This dark blue hat is a gift from my older sibling.

target: Mereka memindahkan lemari besar itu ke gudang.
english: They moved that big wardrobe to the storeroom.

target: Dinding kamar anak kami biru muda.
english: Our child's bedroom walls are light blue.

target: Setiap warna di rumah ini punya cerita.
english: Every color in this house has a story.

target: Saya cari hotel yang dekat dengan stasiun.
english: I am looking for a hotel that is near the station.
grammar: yang links a noun to its description: hotel yang dekat = a hotel that is near.

target: Ada kamar yang lebih besar untuk keluarga?
english: Is there a bigger room for a family?

target: Kereta lebih cepat daripada bus ke bandara.
english: The train is faster than the bus to the airport.
grammar: lebih ... daripada = more ... than: lebih cepat daripada bus = faster than the bus.

target: Hotel ini paling murah di dekat pantai.
english: This hotel is the cheapest near the beach.
grammar: paling = the most: paling murah = the cheapest.

target: Tolong panggil taksi untuk saya sekarang.
english: Please call a taxi for me now.

target: Boleh saya lihat kamarnya dulu?
english: May I see the room first?
grammar: boleh = may (permission): Boleh saya lihat? = May I see?

target: Bisa minta peta kota ini?
english: Can I get a map of this city?
grammar: minta = ask for a thing: Bisa minta peta? = Can I get a map?

target: Kami tiba di Jakarta kemarin malam.
english: We arrived in Jakarta last night.

target: Tadi saya sudah beli tiket kereta di loket.
english: Earlier I already bought train tickets at the counter.
grammar: tadi = earlier today: tadi saya sudah beli = I already bought (it) earlier.

target: Setelah makan siang, kami pergi ke museum.
english: After lunch, we went to the museum.
grammar: setelah = after: setelah makan siang = after lunch.

target: Kalau hujan, kita naik taksi saja.
english: If it rains, let's just take a taxi.
grammar: kalau = if: kalau hujan = if it rains. No extra word for 'then'.

target: Besok pagi kami akan berangkat ke Bali.
english: Tomorrow morning we will depart for Bali.

target: Jangan lupa bawa paspor dan tiket kamu.
english: Don't forget to bring your passport and ticket.
grammar: jangan lupa = don't forget: jangan lupa bawa paspor = don't forget your passport.

target: Di mana halte bus yang ke pusat kota?
english: Where is the bus stop that goes to the city center?

target: Kamar di lantai atas lebih tenang daripada di bawah.
english: The room upstairs is quieter than the one downstairs.

target: Tolong antar koper ini ke kamar saya.
english: Please take this suitcase to my room.
grammar: tolong + verb = please (do something): tolong antar = please take (it) there.

target: Kemarin kami menginap di hotel dekat bandara.
english: Yesterday we stayed overnight at a hotel near the airport.
grammar: menginap = meN- + inap: kami menginap di hotel = we stayed overnight at a hotel.

target: Sebelum berangkat, saya cek jadwal kereta dulu.
english: Before departing, I check the train schedule first.

target: Kalau ada kamar kosong, saya mau menginap dua malam.
english: If there is a vacant room, I want to stay two nights.

target: Rencananya kami pergi ke pantai hari Minggu.
english: The plan is we go to the beach on Sunday.

target: Semoga cuaca bagus selama liburan kita.
english: Hopefully the weather is good during our vacation.
grammar: semoga = hopefully: semoga cuaca bagus = hope the weather is good.

target: Kami mau kamar yang dekat dengan kolam renang.
english: We want a room that is near the swimming pool.

target: Naik kereta lebih nyaman daripada naik bus malam.
english: Taking the train is more comfortable than taking the night bus.

target: Permisi, boleh saya duduk di kursi dekat jendela?
english: Excuse me, may I sit in the seat by the window?

target: Tadi malam kami jalan kaki ke pasar malam.
english: Last night we walked to the night market.

target: Setelah sampai di hotel, kami langsung tidur.
english: After arriving at the hotel, we went straight to sleep.
grammar: langsung = straight away: kami langsung tidur = we went straight to sleep.

target: Kalau kamu capek, kita istirahat di kafe itu.
english: If you are tired, we can rest at that cafe.

target: Nanti sore kami mau lihat matahari terbenam di pantai.
english: Later this afternoon we want to watch the sunset at the beach.

target: Sebaiknya kamu pesan hotel dari sekarang.
english: You had better book the hotel from now.
grammar: sebaiknya = had better: sebaiknya pesan sekarang = better book now.

target: Restoran yang di sebelah hotel itu enak sekali.
english: The restaurant next to the hotel is very good.

target: Jalan kaki lebih cepat karena jalanan macet sekali.
english: Walking is faster because the streets are very jammed.

target: Bisa tolong foto kami di depan candi ini?
english: Could you please take our photo in front of this temple?

target: Kemarin sore kami turun dari kapal di pelabuhan.
english: Yesterday afternoon we got off the ship at the harbor.

target: Kalau mau tukar uang, di mana yang paling bagus?
english: If I want to exchange money, where is the best place?

target: Minggu depan saya akan terbang ke Lombok.
english: Next week I will fly to Lombok.

target: Laporan yang kamu kirim kemarin sudah saya baca.
english: I have already read the report you sent yesterday.
grammar: yang also points back to things: laporan yang kamu kirim = the report you sent.

target: Tolong kirim ulang dokumen itu ke email saya.
english: Please resend that document to my email.

target: Rapat tadi pagi selesai jam sebelas.
english: This morning's meeting finished at eleven.

target: Kami akan mulai proyek baru bulan depan.
english: We will start a new project next month.

target: Ruang rapat di lantai dua lebih besar.
english: The meeting room on the second floor is bigger.

target: Kalau ada pertanyaan, kirim pesan ke saya.
english: If there are questions, send me a message.

target: Boleh saya pulang lebih awal hari ini?
english: May I go home earlier today?

target: Kemarin saya kerja lembur sampai jam sembilan malam.
english: Yesterday I worked overtime until nine at night.

target: Setelah rapat, kita bahas jadwal proyek ini.
english: After the meeting, let's discuss this project's schedule.

target: Jangan lupa simpan dokumen sebelum pulang.
english: Don't forget to save the document before going home.

target: Saya butuh rekan kerja yang bisa bantu proyek ini.
english: I need a colleague who can help with this project.

target: Kirim laporan itu paling lambat hari Jumat.
english: Send that report by Friday at the latest.
grammar: paling lambat = at the latest: paling lambat hari Jumat = by Friday at the latest.

target: Tolong jelaskan bagian ini sekali lagi.
english: Please explain this part one more time.
grammar: -kan turns a word into a doing-verb: jelas (clear) → jelaskan = explain.

target: Tadi pagi saya sudah telepon klien dari Surabaya.
english: Earlier this morning I already called the client from Surabaya.

target: Sebelum presentasi, saya siapkan semua data dulu.
english: Before the presentation, I prepare all the data first.

target: Kalau laporan belum selesai, bilang ke saya.
english: If the report is not finished yet, tell me.

target: Besok kami akan rapat dengan tim pemasaran.
english: Tomorrow we will have a meeting with the marketing team.
grammar: akan marks the future: kami akan rapat = we will have a meeting.

target: Semoga presentasi kamu berjalan lancar besok.
english: Hopefully your presentation goes smoothly tomorrow.

target: Klien yang datang tadi mau lihat kantor baru.
english: The client who came earlier wants to see the new office.

target: Jadwal minggu ini lebih padat daripada minggu lalu.
english: This week's schedule is fuller than last week's.

target: Bisa bantu saya cek angka di laporan ini?
english: Can you help me check the numbers in this report?

target: Kemarin atasan saya pulang cepat karena sakit.
english: Yesterday my boss went home early because he was sick.

target: Setelah kirim email itu, saya langsung pulang.
english: After sending that email, I went straight home.

target: Kalau rapat batal, saya langsung kabari kamu.
english: If the meeting is cancelled, I'll let you know right away.
grammar: -i makes a verb aim at someone: kabar (news) → kabari = let (someone) know.

target: Bulan depan kantor kami pindah ke gedung baru.
english: Next month our office moves to a new building.

target: Sebaiknya kita tunda rapat sampai besok pagi.
english: We had better postpone the meeting until tomorrow morning.

target: Mana dokumen yang harus saya baca dulu?
english: Which document should I read first?

target: Kantin di kantor lama lebih murah daripada di sini.
english: The canteen at the old office was cheaper than here.

target: Tolong tunggu sebentar, saya panggil manajer dulu.
english: Please wait a moment, I'll call the manager first.

target: Proyek itu sudah selesai minggu lalu.
english: That project was already finished last week.
grammar: sudah marks a finished action, verbs never change: sudah selesai = already done.

target: Sebelum pulang, saya harus balas tiga email lagi.
english: Before going home, I have to reply to three more emails.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, saya bisa hubungi klien itu.
english: If you are busy, I can contact that client.

target: Saya mau ambil cuti dua hari minggu depan.
english: I want to take two days of leave next week.

target: Jangan lupa isi jadwal kamu sebelum rapat besok.
english: Don't forget to fill in your schedule before tomorrow's meeting.

target: Gaji di perusahaan baru itu lebih tinggi.
english: The salary at that new company is higher.

target: Kemarin kami makan malam di rumah nenek.
english: Yesterday we had dinner at grandma's house.

target: Setelah makan malam, ayah cuci piring di dapur.
english: After dinner, dad washes the dishes in the kitchen.

target: Tolong bantu adik kamu mengerjakan tugas sekolahnya.
english: Please help your little brother do his schoolwork.

target: Akhir pekan ini kami mau piknik di taman kota.
english: This weekend we want to picnic in the city park.

target: Anak yang paling kecil sudah tidur dari tadi.
english: The youngest child has been asleep for a while.
grammar: dari tadi = since earlier: sudah tidur dari tadi = has been asleep for a while.

target: Kakak saya lebih tinggi daripada ayah sekarang.
english: My older brother is taller than dad now.

target: Kalau cuaca bagus, kita main bola di halaman.
english: If the weather is nice, we play ball in the yard.

target: Tadi sore ibu jemput adik di sekolah.
english: Earlier this afternoon mom picked up little sister at school.

target: Sebelum tidur, nenek cerita tentang masa kecilnya.
english: Before bed, grandma tells stories about her childhood.

target: Jangan lupa matikan lampu sebelum tidur, ya.
english: Don't forget to turn off the light before bed, okay?
grammar: matikan = mati (off) + -kan: matikan lampu = turn off the light.

target: Besok kami akan mengunjungi kakek di kampung.
english: Tomorrow we will visit grandpa in the village.
grammar: mengunjungi = meN- + kunjung + -i: mengunjungi kakek = to visit grandpa.

target: Sepupu saya yang tinggal di Bandung datang besok.
english: My cousin who lives in Bandung is coming tomorrow.

target: Adik saya lebih suka susu daripada teh manis.
english: My little brother prefers milk to sweet tea.

target: Minta tolong angkat jemuran, sebentar lagi hujan.
english: Please bring in the laundry, it's about to rain.

target: Kemarin anak-anak berenang di kolam dekat rumah.
english: Yesterday the kids swam in the pool near the house.
grammar: ber- verbs describe an activity: renang → berenang = to swim.

target: Setelah sarapan, kami bersihkan rumah bersama-sama.
english: After breakfast, we clean the house together.
grammar: bersama-sama = together: bersihkan rumah bersama-sama = clean the house together.

target: Kalau kamu lapar, ada nasi goreng di meja.
english: If you are hungry, there is fried rice on the table.

target: Liburan sekolah nanti, kami mau ke rumah paman.
english: During the school holidays, we want to go to uncle's house.

target: Semoga adik kamu cepat sembuh, ya.
english: Hope your little brother gets well soon, okay?

target: Foto yang di dinding itu dari pernikahan kami.
english: The photo on the wall is from our wedding.

target: Rumah baru kami lebih dekat ke sekolah anak-anak.
english: Our new house is closer to the children's school.

target: Boleh anak-anak main di rumah teman sampai sore?
english: May the kids play at their friend's house until the afternoon?

target: Tadi malam kami menonton film kartun bersama anak-anak.
english: Last night we watched a cartoon movie with the kids.

target: Sebelum berangkat sekolah, adik selalu sarapan dulu.
english: Before leaving for school, little brother always has breakfast first.

target: Kalau sudah selesai makan, bawa piring ke dapur.
english: When you have finished eating, take your plate to the kitchen.

target: Minggu depan kami akan merayakan ulang tahun ibu.
english: Next week we will celebrate mom's birthday.

target: Sebaiknya anak-anak tidur sebelum jam sembilan malam.
english: The kids had better sleep before nine at night.

target: Kue yang ibu buat kemarin sudah habis.
english: The cake mom made yesterday is all gone.

target: Waktu saya kecil, kami tinggal di dekat pantai.
english: When I was little, we lived near the beach.
grammar: waktu + clause = when (in the past): waktu saya kecil = when I was little.

target: Nanti malam kita masak sup ayam bersama, ya.
english: Tonight let's cook chicken soup together, okay?

target: Makanannya sudah dipesan, tinggal ditunggu saja.
english: The food has already been ordered; now we just wait for it.
grammar: -nya marks a known thing: makanannya = the food (we ordered). New info stays bare: makanan.

target: Kuncinya ditaruh di mana tadi pagi?
english: Where was the key put this morning?
grammar: Indonesian loves fronting the object: Kuncinya ditaruh di mana? = Where was the key put?

target: Mobilnya sudah diparkir di depan rumah kita.
english: The car is already parked in front of our house.

target: Bajunya sedang dicuci, jadi pakai yang lain dulu.
english: The shirt is being washed, so wear a different one for now.

target: Piringnya sudah dicuci dan disimpan di lemari.
english: The plates have been washed and put away in the cupboard.
grammar: Two passives chain smoothly: dicuci dan disimpan = washed and put away. No 'they were' needed.

target: Lampunya belum dimatikan, tolong dicek dulu.
english: The lights haven't been turned off yet; please check first.
grammar: Tolong + di- softens a request: tolong dicek = please check it (lit. 'let it be checked').

target: Pintunya sudah dikunci sebelum kami berangkat tadi.
english: The door was already locked before we left earlier.

target: Jendelanya dibuka sedikit supaya udara segar masuk.
english: The window is opened a little so fresh air can come in.

target: Sampahnya sudah dibuang tadi pagi oleh adik.
english: The trash was already taken out this morning by my little brother.

target: Nasinya sedang dimasak, sebentar lagi matang.
english: The rice is being cooked; it will be done soon.

target: Sayurnya dipotong kecil-kecil dulu sebelum digoreng.
english: The vegetables are cut into small pieces first before being fried.
grammar: Doubling an adjective spreads it out: dipotong kecil-kecil = cut into lots of small pieces.

target: Air panasnya sudah disiapkan untuk membuat kopi.
english: The hot water has been prepared for making coffee.

target: Kamar tamunya dibersihkan dua kali seminggu.
english: The guest room is cleaned twice a week.

target: Bukunya dipinjam teman dan belum dikembalikan sampai sekarang.
english: The book was borrowed by a friend and still hasn't been returned.
grammar: The doer can follow the di- verb directly: dipinjam teman = borrowed by a friend. oleh is optional.

target: Fotonya digantung di dinding dekat jendela.
english: The photo is hung on the wall near the window.

target: Kue ini dibuat ibu khusus untuk ulang tahunmu.
english: This cake was made by Mom especially for your birthday.

target: Obatnya diminum dua kali sehari, pagi dan malam.
english: The medicine is taken twice a day, morning and night.
grammar: Habits use plain di- with no tense word: diminum dua kali sehari = is taken twice a day.

target: Tehnya baru dibuat, masih panas sekali.
english: The tea was just made; it's still very hot.

target: Suratnya ditulis tangan oleh nenek saya.
english: The letter was handwritten by my grandmother.

target: Kamar mandinya sedang dipakai, tunggu sebentar ya.
english: The bathroom is being used; wait a moment, okay?

target: Sepatunya ditaruh di rak dekat pintu depan.
english: The shoes are put on the rack near the front door.

target: Kulkasnya jangan dibuka terlalu lama, ya.
english: Don't open the fridge for too long, okay?
grammar: jangan + di- is a gentle prohibition: jangan dibuka = don't open it. Focus stays on the thing.

target: Sisa makanannya disimpan di kulkas untuk besok.
english: The leftover food is kept in the fridge for tomorrow.

target: Tanamannya disiram setiap sore oleh ayah.
english: The plants are watered every afternoon by Dad.

target: Kasurnya dijemur di bawah matahari supaya tidak lembap.
english: The mattress is dried in the sun so it doesn't get damp.
grammar: supaya = so that: dijemur supaya tidak lembap = dried so it doesn't get damp.

target: Celananya perlu disetrika sebelum dipakai besok pagi.
english: The trousers need to be ironed before being worn tomorrow morning.

target: Gelas kotornya ditaruh di dapur saja dulu.
english: Just put the dirty glasses in the kitchen for now.

target: Rambut adik dipotong pendek kemarin sore.
english: Little brother's hair was cut short yesterday afternoon.

target: Kacamatanya ditemukan di bawah sofa tadi malam.
english: The glasses were found under the sofa last night.

target: Dindingnya baru dicat, jangan disentuh dulu.
english: The wall was just painted; don't touch it yet.

target: Tiketnya sudah dibeli lewat aplikasi minggu lalu.
english: The tickets were already bought through the app last week.
grammar: lewat = via/through: dibeli lewat aplikasi = bought through the app.

target: Kopernya bisa dititip di resepsionis sampai siang.
english: The suitcase can be left with the receptionist until midday.
grammar: titip = leave something in someone's care: dititip di resepsionis = left at the front desk.

target: Kamarnya sudah dibersihkan waktu kami kembali dari pantai.
english: The room had already been cleaned when we got back from the beach.

target: Paspornya harus dibawa setiap kali naik pesawat.
english: The passport must be carried every time you take a plane.
grammar: harus + di- = must be X-ed: harus dibawa = must be brought along.

target: Taksinya sudah dipanggil, lima menit lagi sampai.
english: The taxi has been called; it will arrive in five minutes.

target: Sarapannya disajikan di lantai dua mulai jam enam.
english: Breakfast is served on the second floor starting at six.

target: Oleh-olehnya dibungkus rapi supaya tidak pecah di jalan.
english: The souvenirs are wrapped carefully so they don't break on the way.
grammar: oleh-oleh = the souvenirs you bring people from a trip. Buying them is a real Indonesian custom.

target: Hotelnya dipilih karena dekat dengan stasiun kereta.
english: The hotel was chosen because it is close to the train station.

target: Jadwal keretanya bisa dicek lewat aplikasi ini.
english: The train schedule can be checked through this app.

target: Mejanya sudah dipesan atas nama saya untuk jam tujuh.
english: The table has been booked under my name for seven o'clock.
grammar: atas nama = under the name of: dipesan atas nama saya = booked under my name.

target: Tasnya diperiksa petugas di pintu masuk bandara.
english: The bag was checked by an officer at the airport entrance.

target: Uangnya bisa ditukar di konter dekat pintu keluar.
english: The money can be exchanged at the counter near the exit.

target: Kamarnya akan disiapkan sebelum tamu datang sore ini.
english: The room will be prepared before the guests arrive this afternoon.
grammar: akan + di- = will be X-ed: akan disiapkan = will be prepared.

target: Peta kotanya bisa diminta gratis di lobi hotel.
english: A city map can be requested for free at the hotel lobby.

target: Motornya disewa untuk berkeliling pulau selama dua hari.
english: The motorbike was rented to go around the island for two days.
grammar: sewa = to rent: motornya disewa = the motorbike is rented (from someone).

target: Penerbangannya dibatalkan karena cuaca buruk kemarin sore.
english: The flight was canceled because of bad weather yesterday afternoon.

target: Kamar hotelnya harus dikosongkan sebelum jam dua belas siang.
english: The hotel room must be vacated before twelve noon.
grammar: kosong = empty, dikosongkan = to be emptied out: harus dikosongkan = must be vacated.

target: Laporannya harus dikirim sebelum jam lima sore ini.
english: The report must be sent before five o'clock this afternoon.

target: Rapatnya ditunda sampai hari Kamis minggu depan.
english: The meeting is postponed until Thursday next week.
grammar: tunda = postpone: rapatnya ditunda = the meeting got pushed back.

target: Emailnya sudah dibalas tadi pagi sebelum rapat.
english: The email was already replied to this morning before the meeting.

target: Dokumennya sedang dicetak, tunggu sebentar ya.
english: The documents are being printed; wait a moment, okay?

target: Gajinya dibayar setiap akhir bulan lewat transfer.
english: The salary is paid at the end of every month by transfer.

target: Hasil kerjanya dipuji oleh atasan di depan semua orang.
english: His work was praised by the boss in front of everyone.
grammar: Use oleh when the doer matters: dipuji oleh atasan = praised by the boss.

target: Jadwal rapatnya diubah jadi jam sepuluh pagi.
english: The meeting schedule was changed to ten in the morning.

target: Berkasnya disusun rapi sebelum diserahkan ke atasan.
english: The files are arranged neatly before being handed over to the boss.

target: Komputernya sedang diperbaiki, jadi saya memakai laptop dulu.
english: The computer is being repaired, so I'm using a laptop for now.
grammar: sedang + di- = is being X-ed right now: sedang diperbaiki = is being repaired.

target: Ruang rapatnya sudah dipesan untuk besok pagi.
english: The meeting room has already been booked for tomorrow morning.

target: Idenya dibahas panjang lebar dalam rapat tadi siang.
english: The idea was discussed at length in the meeting earlier today.

target: Kontraknya belum ditandatangani oleh kedua pihak.
english: The contract has not yet been signed by both parties.
grammar: belum + di- = not yet X-ed: belum ditandatangani = not signed yet. belum, not tidak, means 'not yet'.

target: Karyawan baru itu dilatih selama dua minggu pertama.
english: The new employee is trained during the first two weeks.

target: Meja kerjanya dirapikan setiap sore sebelum pulang.
english: The desk gets tidied every afternoon before going home.

target: Pertanyaannya dijawab satu per satu dengan sabar.
english: The questions were answered one by one, patiently.

target: Undangannya sudah dikirim ke semua karyawan lewat email.
english: The invitation has been sent to all employees by email.

target: Proyeknya dikerjakan bersama tim dari kantor cabang.
english: The project is being worked on together with the branch office team.

target: Anak-anak dijemput dari sekolah jam satu siang.
english: The kids are picked up from school at one in the afternoon.
grammar: Daily routines sound natural in the passive: anak-anak dijemput jam satu = the kids get picked up at one.

target: Nasi gorengnya dimasak ayah tadi malam.
english: The fried rice was cooked by Dad last night.

target: Kamar anak-anak dibereskan setiap hari Minggu pagi.
english: The kids' room gets tidied up every Sunday morning.

target: Susunya sudah dihangatkan untuk adik bayi.
english: The milk has been warmed up for the baby.
grammar: hangat = warm, dihangatkan = warmed up: susunya dihangatkan = the milk is warmed.

target: Pakaian kotor dikumpulkan dulu sebelum dicuci bersama.
english: The dirty clothes are gathered first before being washed together.

target: Neneknya dirawat di rumah oleh seluruh keluarga.
english: Grandma is cared for at home by the whole family.

target: Kue ulang tahunnya dipesan dari toko dekat rumah.
english: The birthday cake was ordered from a shop near the house.

target: Mainannya disimpan di kotak besar di bawah tempat tidur.
english: The toys are kept in a big box under the bed.

target: Adik dibangunkan pelan-pelan supaya tidak kaget.
english: Little brother is woken up gently so he isn't startled.
grammar: pelan-pelan = slowly, gently (doubled adjective): dibangunkan pelan-pelan = woken up gently.

target: Foto keluarganya dipajang di ruang tamu.
english: The family photo is displayed in the living room.

target: Tugas cuci piring dibagi rata antara kakak dan adik.
english: The dish-washing chore is split evenly between the older and younger siblings.

target: Rumahnya dijaga tetangga waktu kami mudik minggu lalu.
english: The house was watched by the neighbors while we went back to our hometown last week.
grammar: mudik = travel back to your hometown. A huge Indonesian tradition, especially before Lebaran.

target: Uang sakunya diberikan setiap hari Senin pagi.
english: The pocket money is handed out every Monday morning.

target: Acara keluarganya diadakan di rumah nenek tahun ini.
english: The family gathering is being held at Grandma's house this year.
grammar: diadakan (from ada) = is held: diadakan di rumah nenek = held at grandma's house.

target: Anak bungsunya diajari naik sepeda oleh kakaknya.
english: The youngest child is being taught to ride a bike by his older sibling.

target: Sayur di kebun belakang ditanam bersama anak-anak.
english: The vegetables in the back garden were planted together with the kids.

target: Baju bekas adik disumbangkan ke panti asuhan.
english: Little brother's old clothes were donated to an orphanage.

target: Silakan diminum tehnya selagi masih hangat.
english: Please drink the tea while it's still warm.
grammar: Silakan + di- is a warm invitation: silakan diminum tehnya = please go ahead and drink the tea.

target: Silakan dicoba dulu bajunya sebelum dibeli.
english: Please try the shirt on first before buying it.

target: Silakan dimakan kuenya, jangan malu-malu ya.
english: Please eat the cake -- don't be shy, okay?

target: Silakan diisi formulirnya dengan huruf besar.
english: Please fill in the form in capital letters.
grammar: In polite passive requests the object takes -nya: diisi formulirnya = fill in the form.

target: Silakan ditunggu sebentar, makanannya sedang disiapkan.
english: Please wait a moment; the food is being prepared.

target: Tolong dimatikan lampunya kalau sudah selesai.
english: Please turn off the lights when you're finished.

target: Tolong dibuang sampahnya sebelum tidur, ya.
english: Please take out the trash before bed, okay?
grammar: Tolong + di-verb + object-nya is the everyday polite request: tolong dibuang sampahnya.

target: Tolong diangkat teleponnya, saya sedang memasak.
english: Please answer the phone; I'm cooking.

target: Tolong dijaga barangnya, saya ke toilet sebentar.
english: Please watch the bags; I'm going to the toilet for a moment.

target: Tolong ditutup pintunya, angin masuk dari luar.
english: Please close the door; wind is coming in from outside.

target: Jangan dilupakan janjinya dengan anak-anak besok.
english: Don't forget the promise to the kids tomorrow.

target: Silakan dipakai kamar mandinya lebih dulu.
english: Please go ahead and use the bathroom first.

target: Silakan diambil brosurnya di meja dekat pintu.
english: Please take a brochure from the table near the door.

target: Tolong dicuci gelasnya sesudah dipakai, ya.
english: Please wash the glass after using it, okay?

target: Lagu itu dinyanyikan oleh penyanyi terkenal dari Bandung.
english: That song is sung by a famous singer from Bandung.

target: Rumah ini dibangun oleh kakek empat puluh tahun lalu.
english: This house was built by Grandpa forty years ago.
grammar: bangun has two lives: bangun pagi = wake up early; dibangun = built (a building).

target: Buku ini ditulis oleh penulis muda dari Yogyakarta.
english: This book was written by a young writer from Yogyakarta.

target: Makan malamnya dimasak oleh ibu dan bibi bersama-sama.
english: Dinner was cooked by Mom and Auntie together.

target: Sepeda tua itu diperbaiki oleh tetangga sebelah.
english: That old bicycle was repaired by the next-door neighbor.

target: Acaranya dibuka oleh kepala sekolah jam delapan pagi.
english: The event was opened by the school principal at eight in the morning.

target: Tasnya ditaruh di mana waktu kalian sampai?
english: Where were the bags put when you all arrived?

target: Motornya biasanya diparkir di mana kalau ke pasar?
english: Where is the motorbike usually parked when you go to the market?

target: Tiketnya sudah dibayar atau belum, ya?
english: Have the tickets been paid for yet or not?
grammar: sudah ... atau belum = yet or not yet: sudah dibayar atau belum? = has it been paid yet?

target: Kado untuk ibu sudah dibungkus atau belum?
english: Has the present for Mom been wrapped yet or not?

target: Makanan ini dimakan pakai tangan atau pakai sendok?
english: Is this food eaten with your hands or with a spoon?
grammar: pakai = with/using for tools: dimakan pakai tangan = eaten with your hands.

target: Fotonya diambil siapa waktu kalian di pantai?
english: Who took the photo when you were at the beach?
grammar: Ask the doer right after the di- verb: diambil siapa? = who took it? (lit. taken by whom?)

target: Bajumu dibeli di toko yang mana kemarin?
english: Which shop was your shirt bought at yesterday?

target: Suratnya harus dikirim kapan supaya sampai hari Jumat?
english: When does the letter have to be sent so it arrives by Friday?

target: Kamarnya mau dibersihkan sekarang atau nanti sore?
english: Would you like the room cleaned now or later this afternoon?
grammar: Hotel staff speak in passives: mau dibersihkan sekarang? = would you like it cleaned now?

target: Kipasnya perlu dinyalakan atau ruangannya sudah dingin?
english: Does the fan need to be turned on, or is the room already cool?
grammar: perlu + di- = needs to be X-ed: perlu dinyalakan = needs to be switched on.

target: Obat ini boleh diminum sebelum makan atau harus sesudah makan?
english: Can this medicine be taken before eating, or does it have to be after meals?

target: Sisa nasinya mau dibuang atau disimpan saja?
english: Should the leftover rice be thrown out or just kept?

target: Baju yang dijemur di luar sudah kering semua.
english: The clothes hung out to dry outside are all dry now.

target: Kue yang dibuat nenek selalu habis paling cepat.
english: The cakes Grandma makes always run out the fastest.
grammar: yang + di- = 'the one that was ...': kue yang dibuat nenek = the cake made by grandma.

target: Film yang ditonton anak-anak tadi lucu sekali.
english: The movie the kids watched earlier was really funny.

target: Barang yang dipesan minggu lalu akhirnya sampai hari ini.
english: The item ordered last week finally arrived today.

target: Jalan yang dilewati bus itu sedang diperbaiki.
english: The road that bus goes down is being repaired.

target: Lagu yang diputar di kafe itu enak didengar.
english: The song playing in that cafe is nice to listen to.
grammar: enak di- = nice to X: enak didengar = nice to listen to; enak dimakan = tasty.

target: Kunci yang dicari dari tadi ada di kantong jaket.
english: The key we've been looking for all this time is in the jacket pocket.
grammar: dari tadi = this whole time (since earlier): dicari dari tadi = looked for all this while.

target: Sayur yang dibeli di pasar pagi masih segar.
english: The vegetables bought at the morning market are still fresh.

target: Cerita yang diceritakan kakek selalu seru.
english: The stories Grandpa tells are always exciting.

target: Kursi yang diduduki tamu itu baru dibeli kemarin.
english: The chair the guest is sitting on was just bought yesterday.
grammar: di-...-i often means 'on': diduduki = sat on. Kursi yang diduduki tamu = the chair the guest sits on.

target: Formulirnya harus diisi sebelum masuk ruang tunggu.
english: The form must be filled in before entering the waiting room.

target: Tiket kereta bisa dibeli sampai satu jam sebelum berangkat.
english: Train tickets can be bought up to one hour before departure.
grammar: bisa + di- = can be X-ed: bisa dibeli = can be bought.

target: Penjual buah di pasar itu sangat ramah kepada saya.
english: The fruit seller at that market is very friendly to me.
grammar: pe- turns a verb into the doer: jual (sell) → penjual (seller).

target: Pembeli sering bertanya tentang ukuran sepatu di toko kami.
english: Buyers often ask about shoe sizes at our store.
grammar: pe- + beli = pembeli, the one who buys — the same pattern gives penjual and pekerja.

target: Ayah saya bekerja sebagai penulis buku anak.
english: My father works as a children's book writer.
grammar: pe- copies the meN- sound change: tulis → menulis, so the writer is penulis.

target: Para pekerja pabrik mulai bekerja jam tujuh pagi.
english: The factory workers start working at seven in the morning.

target: Penyanyi terkenal itu menyanyikan lagu daerah tadi malam.
english: That famous singer sang a regional song last night.
grammar: menyanyi has no object; when a song is named, use menyanyikan: menyanyikan lagu daerah.

target: Adik saya ingin menjadi pemain sepak bola terkenal.
english: My younger sibling wants to become a famous soccer player.

target: Penari muda itu berlatih setiap sore di gedung seni.
english: That young dancer practices every afternoon at the arts building.

target: Pelari tercepat dalam lomba itu berasal dari kota kami.
english: The fastest runner in that race comes from our city.

target: Perenang itu berlatih di kolam renang setiap hari Sabtu.
english: That swimmer trains at the swimming pool every Saturday.
grammar: r-roots take pe- without n: renang → perenang (swimmer), like berenang.

target: Pengajar bahasa Inggris kami berasal dari Australia.
english: Our English teacher comes from Australia.

target: Para pelajar rajin membaca buku pelajaran di ruang kelas.
english: The students diligently read their textbooks in the classroom.
grammar: One root, two people: pengajar teaches, pelajar learns — both from ajar.

target: Para penonton bola berteriak gembira sepanjang pertandingan tadi malam.
english: The soccer spectators shouted happily throughout the match last night.

target: Pendengar radio bisa mengirim pertanyaan lewat telepon.
english: Radio listeners can send questions by phone.

target: Pengunjung museum harus menyimpan tas besar di loker.
english: Museum visitors must store large bags in the lockers.

target: Para penumpang harus menunjukkan tiket kepada petugas stasiun.
english: The passengers must show their tickets to the station officer.
grammar: tumpang (ride along) → penumpang: the passenger, the one who rides.

target: Pengemudi taksi itu tahu jalan pintas ke bandara.
english: That taxi driver knows a shortcut to the airport.

target: Pemilik toko itu membuka pintu jam delapan pagi.
english: That shop owner opens the door at eight in the morning.

target: Pencuri itu ditangkap polisi di dekat stasiun kereta.
english: That thief was caught by the police near the train station.

target: Pelukis itu menjual lukisan pemandangan pantai di pasar seni.
english: That painter sells beach scenery paintings at the art market.
grammar: One root, two nouns: pelukis is the painter, lukisan is the painting.

target: Pemandu wisata selalu menjelaskan sejarah candi kepada tamu baru.
english: The tour guide always explains the temple's history to new guests.

target: Pelatih renang memberi latihan baru kepada perenang muda.
english: The swimming coach gives new drills to the young swimmers.

target: Pelayan restoran baru saja membawa minuman dingin ke meja kami.
english: The restaurant waiter just brought cold drinks to our table.

target: Para perawat di rumah sakit itu sangat sabar.
english: The nurses at that hospital are very patient.

target: Petani itu menanam sayuran di belakang rumahnya.
english: That farmer plants vegetables behind his house.
grammar: A few jobs take plain pe- with no sound change: petani (farmer), petugas (officer).

target: Pedagang kecil menjual makanan ringan di depan sekolah.
english: Small vendors sell snacks in front of the school.

target: Penjaga malam memeriksa pintu kantor setiap dua jam.
english: The night guard checks the office doors every two hours.

target: Pengirim surat itu lupa menulis alamat lengkap.
english: The sender of the letter forgot to write the complete address.

target: Penerima hadiah utama akan diumumkan malam ini.
english: The recipient of the main prize will be announced tonight.

target: Penyewa mobil harus mengembalikan kunci sebelum jam lima sore.
english: Car renters must return the key before five in the afternoon.

target: Pembantu rumah tangga itu memasak makanan untuk keluarga kami.
english: That household helper cooks food for our family.

target: Makanan di warung kecil itu murah dan sangat enak.
english: The food at that small food stall is cheap and very delicious.
grammar: -an names the result: makan (eat) → makanan (food, the thing eaten).

target: Ibu sedang menyiapkan minuman hangat untuk para tamu.
english: Mother is preparing warm drinks for the guests.

target: Pakaian kotor itu harus dicuci hari ini.
english: Those dirty clothes must be washed today.
grammar: -an from pakai (wear) gives pakaian — clothing, the things worn.

target: Bangunan tua di pusat kota itu sekarang menjadi museum.
english: That old building in the city center is now a museum.
grammar: bangun (build) → bangunan: the built thing, a building.

target: Saya membawa bacaan ringan untuk perjalanan kereta besok.
english: I am bringing light reading for tomorrow's train trip.

target: Tulisan tangan dokter itu susah sekali dibaca.
english: That doctor's handwriting is very hard to read.

target: Masakan ibu selalu membuat saya rindu rumah.
english: Mother's cooking always makes me miss home.
grammar: masakan is the dish, the result of cooking; the act itself is masak/memasak.

target: Anak kecil itu menyimpan mainan di bawah tempat tidur.
english: That little child keeps toys under the bed.

target: Ada banyak pilihan menu di restoran baru itu.
english: There are many menu choices at that new restaurant.

target: Kiriman dari nenek tiba di rumah tadi pagi.
english: The package from grandma arrived at the house this morning.
grammar: kirim (send) → kiriman: the thing sent, like a parcel from family.

target: Kami menerima undangan pernikahan dari teman kantor kemarin.
english: We received a wedding invitation from an office friend yesterday.

target: Jawaban kamu benar, tapi tulisannya kurang jelas.
english: Your answer is correct, but the writing is not clear enough.

target: Saya selalu menulis catatan penting di buku kecil ini.
english: I always write important notes in this small notebook.

target: Lukisan di dinding kamar itu dibuat oleh kakek saya.
english: The painting on that bedroom wall was made by my grandfather.

target: Sayuran segar dijual murah di pasar pagi.
english: Fresh vegetables are sold cheaply at the morning market.
grammar: sayur is a vegetable dish; sayuran with -an covers vegetables in general.

target: Cucian menumpuk karena mesin cuci rusak minggu ini.
english: The laundry is piling up because the washing machine broke this week.
grammar: cuci (wash) → cucian: the washing, the pile of clothes to wash.

target: Jangan lupa mengangkat jemuran sebelum hujan turun.
english: Don't forget to bring in the drying laundry before the rain falls.

target: Tabungan saya belum cukup untuk membeli motor baru.
english: My savings are not yet enough to buy a new motorbike.
grammar: tabung (save up) → tabungan (savings): the money set aside.

target: Latihan pagi ini lebih berat daripada latihan kemarin.
english: This morning's practice is heavier than yesterday's practice.

target: Tontonan malam ini cocok untuk seluruh keluarga.
english: Tonight's show is suitable for the whole family.
grammar: tonton (watch) → tontonan: the show, the thing watched.

target: Hiburan di pesta besok adalah tarian tradisional dari Bali.
english: The entertainment at tomorrow's party is a traditional dance from Bali.

target: Pesanan kami baru datang setelah tiga puluh menit.
english: Our order only came after thirty minutes.

target: Panggilan dari kantor masuk saat saya sedang makan siang.
english: A call from the office came in while I was having lunch.

target: Kenalan lama saya sekarang tinggal di Surabaya.
english: An old acquaintance of mine now lives in Surabaya.
grammar: kenal (know someone) → kenalan: an acquaintance, someone you know.

target: Pemandangan dari kamar hotel ini indah sekali.
english: The view from this hotel room is very beautiful.
grammar: pandang (gaze) → pemandangan: the view, everything your eyes take in.

target: Pengumuman keberangkatan terdengar jelas di ruang tunggu.
english: The departure announcement could be heard clearly in the waiting room.

target: Potongan harga di toko itu berlaku sampai hari Minggu.
english: The discount at that store is valid until Sunday.
grammar: potong (cut) → potongan: a cut — potongan harga is a price cut.

target: Minuman dingin ini dibuat dari buah segar dan es.
english: This cold drink is made from fresh fruit and ice.

target: Oleh-oleh khas kota ini adalah makanan manis dari kelapa.
english: This city's typical souvenir is sweet food made from coconut.

target: Ibu punya simpanan beras di dapur untuk bulan depan.
english: Mother has a stock of rice in the kitchen for next month.

target: Harapan saya tahun ini adalah hidup lebih sehat.
english: My hope this year is to live more healthily.

target: Terima kasih banyak atas bantuan kamu minggu lalu.
english: Thank you very much for your help last week.
grammar: bantu (help, verb) → bantuan (help, noun): the aid that is given.

target: Ukuran sepatu ini terlalu besar untuk kaki saya.
english: This shoe size is too big for my feet.

target: Aturan baru di kantor mulai berlaku bulan depan.
english: The new rules at the office take effect next month.

target: Pekerjaan baru saya dimulai hari Senin depan.
english: My new job starts next Monday.
grammar: pe-…-an wraps a whole activity into a noun: kerja → pekerjaan (work, a job).

target: Perjalanan ke desa nenek memakan waktu lima jam.
english: The trip to grandma's village takes five hours.
grammar: jalan → perjalanan: the whole journey, not just the road.

target: Pertanyaan siswa itu dijawab dengan sabar oleh guru.
english: That student's question was answered patiently by the teacher.

target: Pertemuan tim pemasaran dipindah ke hari Rabu.
english: The marketing team meeting was moved to Wednesday.

target: Pernikahan kakak saya dirayakan di gedung besar.
english: My older sibling's wedding was celebrated in a big hall.

target: Perbaikan jalan membuat perjalanan kami lebih lambat.
english: The road repairs made our trip slower.
grammar: baik (good) → perbaikan: the act of making good — a repair.

target: Pembayaran kamar hotel bisa dengan kartu atau uang tunai.
english: Payment for the hotel room can be by card or cash.

target: Perbedaan harga di dua toko itu cukup besar.
english: The price difference between those two stores is quite big.

target: Pengalaman kerja di restoran membantu saya mendapat pekerjaan baru.
english: Work experience at a restaurant helped me get a new job.

target: Perusahaan tempat ayah bekerja sudah pindah ke gedung baru.
english: The company where father works has moved to a new building.
grammar: usaha (effort, business) → perusahaan: a company, where business happens.

target: Permainan tradisional itu masih dimainkan anak-anak di desa.
english: That traditional game is still played by children in the village.

target: Perayaan tahun baru di kota ini selalu ramai.
english: The New Year celebration in this city is always lively.

target: Pendaftaran kelas memasak dibuka sampai akhir bulan ini.
english: Registration for the cooking class is open until the end of this month.
grammar: daftar (a list; register) → pendaftaran: the registration process.

target: Penginapan murah dekat pantai selalu penuh saat liburan.
english: Cheap lodgings near the beach are always full during the holidays.
grammar: inap (stay over) → penginapan: a place to stay the night.

target: Pelajaran hari ini tentang nama hari dan bulan.
english: Today's lesson is about the names of days and months.

target: Pengumuman penting akan dibacakan sebelum rapat dimulai.
english: An important announcement will be read out before the meeting starts.

target: Pemeriksaan tiket dilakukan sebelum penumpang naik kereta.
english: Ticket checks are done before passengers board the train.

target: Pertandingan sepak bola sore ini ditunda karena hujan deras.
english: This afternoon's soccer match was postponed because of heavy rain.

target: Persiapan pesta ulang tahun dimulai dari pagi sekali.
english: Preparations for the birthday party started very early in the morning.

target: Pemesanan meja untuk makan malam bisa lewat telepon.
english: Table reservations for dinner can be made by phone.

target: Pengiriman barang ke luar kota butuh waktu tiga hari.
english: Shipping goods out of town takes three days.

target: Kelas bahasa selalu dimulai dengan perkenalan singkat.
english: The language class always begins with a short introduction.

target: Pertolongan pertama diberikan oleh perawat di tempat kejadian.
english: First aid was given by a nurse at the scene.

target: Pembukaan toko baru itu ramai sekali kemarin sore.
english: The opening of that new store was very crowded yesterday afternoon.

target: Penutupan jalan utama membuat kami lewat jalan lain.
english: The closure of the main road made us take another road.

target: Pencarian kunci yang hilang memakan waktu satu jam.
english: The search for the lost key took one hour.

target: Penjualan tiket konser dimulai jam sepuluh pagi besok.
english: Concert ticket sales start at ten tomorrow morning.

target: Pembelian tiket kereta bisa lewat aplikasi di ponsel.
english: Train ticket purchases can be made through a phone app.

target: Pemilihan ketua kelas diadakan hari Jumat depan.
english: The class leader election will be held next Friday.

target: Kesehatan keluarga lebih penting daripada uang banyak.
english: Family health is more important than a lot of money.
grammar: ke-…-an makes a state noun: sehat (healthy) → kesehatan (health).

target: Kebersihan dapur harus dijaga setiap hari.
english: The cleanliness of the kitchen must be maintained every day.
grammar: bersih (clean) → kebersihan (cleanliness): the state of being clean.

target: Keamanan hotel ini baik karena ada penjaga di pintu.
english: This hotel's security is good because there is a guard at the door.

target: Kesalahan kecil dalam laporan itu sudah diperbaiki.
english: The small mistake in that report has been corrected.
grammar: salah (wrong) → kesalahan: a mistake, the wrong thing done.

target: Keputusan penting itu dibuat setelah pertemuan panjang.
english: That important decision was made after a long meeting.

target: Kemacetan di jalan utama membuat saya terlambat ke kantor.
english: The traffic jam on the main road made me late to the office.
grammar: macet (stuck) → kemacetan: a traffic jam, the state of being stuck.

target: Kecelakaan kecil di dapur membuat jari ibu terluka.
english: A small accident in the kitchen left mother's finger injured.

target: Kebiasaan minum teh sore datang dari keluarga nenek saya.
english: The habit of drinking afternoon tea comes from my grandmother's family.
grammar: biasa (usual) → kebiasaan: a habit, what is usually done.

target: Keinginan adik saya tahun ini adalah sepeda baru.
english: My younger sibling's wish this year is a new bicycle.

target: Kedatangan tamu dari Jepang disambut oleh pemilik hotel.
english: The arrival of the guests from Japan was welcomed by the hotel owner.

target: Keberangkatan pesawat kami ditunda dua jam karena cuaca buruk.
english: Our plane's departure was delayed two hours because of bad weather.
grammar: berangkat (depart) → keberangkatan (departure); datang → kedatangan (arrival).

target: Kami kehujanan di tengah jalan menuju pasar.
english: We got caught in the rain on the way to the market.
grammar: ke-…-an can mean 'hit by': hujan (rain) → kehujanan (caught in the rain).

target: Dia kepanasan karena berdiri lama di bawah matahari.
english: He got overheated because he stood for a long time under the sun.

target: Anak itu kedinginan setelah berenang terlalu lama di kolam.
english: That child got cold after swimming too long in the pool.

target: Kehilangan dompet membuat perjalanan kami sedikit kacau.
english: Losing the wallet made our trip a little chaotic.
grammar: hilang (lost) → kehilangan: the loss, or the experience of losing.

target: Kebahagiaan keluarga terlihat dari foto liburan mereka.
english: The family's happiness shows in their vacation photos.

target: Kelelahan setelah kerja lembur membuat dia tidur lebih cepat.
english: Tiredness after working overtime made him go to sleep earlier.

target: Kesempatan kerja di kota besar biasanya lebih banyak.
english: Job opportunities in big cities are usually more plentiful.
grammar: sempat (have the chance) → kesempatan: an opportunity.

target: Kejadian lucu itu terjadi saat pertemuan keluarga besar.
english: That funny incident happened during the big family gathering.

target: Kemenangan tim kami dirayakan dengan makan malam bersama.
english: Our team's victory was celebrated with a dinner together.

target: Kelebihan kamar ini adalah pemandangan gunung dari jendela.
english: The advantage of this room is the mountain view from the window.
grammar: lebih (more) → kelebihan: a plus point; kekurangan is the weak point.

target: Kekurangan uang membuat kami menunda liburan tahun ini.
english: A lack of money made us postpone our vacation this year.

target: Kesulitan terbesar saya adalah bangun pagi setiap hari.
english: My biggest difficulty is waking up early every day.

target: Keramaian pasar malam membuat anak-anak sangat senang.
english: The bustle of the night market made the children very happy.

target: Penjual minuman di depan bangunan itu sudah pulang.
english: The drink seller in front of that building has already gone home.

target: Pekerjaan pelayan hotel dimulai dengan pemeriksaan kamar kosong.
english: The hotel attendant's work begins with a check of the empty rooms.

target: Banyak pengunjung pameran membeli lukisan kecil sebagai oleh-oleh.
english: Many exhibition visitors buy small paintings as souvenirs.
grammar: pamer (show off) → pameran: an exhibition, things put on show.

target: Kesehatan para pekerja dijaga dengan pemeriksaan rutin di kantor.
english: The workers' health is maintained with routine checkups at the office.

target: Perjalanan panjang itu ditutup dengan makanan enak di penginapan.
english: That long trip was rounded off with delicious food at the lodging.

target: Pertanyaan para penonton dijawab langsung oleh penulis buku itu.
english: The audience's questions were answered directly by the book's author.

target: Kebersihan dan keamanan menjadi alasan kami memilih penginapan itu.
english: Cleanliness and safety are the reasons we chose that lodging.
grammar: alas (base) → alasan: a reason, what an opinion stands on.

target: Latihan ringan setiap pagi menjaga kesehatan badan ayah saya.
english: Light exercise every morning maintains my father's health.

target: Kami membatalkan piknik karena hujan turun deras sekali.
english: We canceled the picnic because the rain came down very hard.

target: Dia terlambat ke rapat karena bus kota datang sangat lambat.
english: He was late to the meeting because the city bus came very slowly.

target: Saya memilih kereta karena tiket pesawat mahal sekali bulan ini.
english: I chose the train because plane tickets are very expensive this month.

target: Anak saya senang sekali karena besok kami pergi ke kebun binatang.
english: My child is very happy because tomorrow we are going to the zoo.

target: Kami pindah ke kota ini karena istri saya dapat pekerjaan baru.
english: We moved to this city because my wife got a new job.

target: Restoran itu selalu penuh karena masakannya enak dan murah.
english: That restaurant is always full because its food is tasty and cheap.

target: Karena jalan macet, kami berangkat lebih pagi dari biasanya.
english: Because the roads are jammed, we leave earlier than usual.
grammar: karena = because; the reason clause can come first: Karena hujan, kami pulang = Because it rained, we went home.

target: Ibu menutup semua jendela karena angin sore ini kencang sekali.
english: Mom is closing all the windows because the wind this afternoon is very strong.

target: Saya minum teh jahe hangat karena tenggorokan saya sakit sejak kemarin.
english: I am drinking warm ginger tea because my throat has hurt since yesterday.

target: Kami memesan kamar dengan sarapan karena harganya hampir sama saja.
english: We booked a room with breakfast because the price is almost the same anyway.

target: Dia belajar bahasa Indonesia karena tahun depan dia pindah ke Jakarta.
english: She is studying Indonesian because next year she is moving to Jakarta.

target: Ayah tidur lebih awal karena besok dia harus berangkat jam lima.
english: Dad is going to bed earlier because tomorrow he has to leave at five.
grammar: Clock times use jam + number: jam lima = five o'clock, jam lima pagi = five in the morning.

target: Kami makan di rumah karena semua restoran dekat sini sudah tutup.
english: We are eating at home because all the restaurants near here are already closed.

target: Saya selalu membawa payung karena musim hujan sudah mulai.
english: I always carry an umbrella because the rainy season has already started.

target: Saya pulang dulu, soalnya besok saya harus bangun pagi sekali.
english: I'm heading home now, because tomorrow I have to get up very early.
grammar: soalnya = spoken 'because', after the statement: ..., soalnya sudah malam = ..., because it's late. In writing: karena.

target: Kita lewat jalan belakang saja, soalnya jalan besar pasti macet.
english: Let's just take the back road, because the main road is definitely jammed.

target: Jangan pesan sup itu, soalnya porsinya kecil dan harganya mahal.
english: Don't order that soup, because the portion is small and the price is high.

target: Aku tidak ikut menonton film, soalnya dompetku ketinggalan di rumah.
english: I'm not coming along to watch the movie, because my wallet got left at home.
grammar: ketinggalan = got left behind by accident: dompetku ketinggalan = my wallet got left behind.

target: Kami duduk di dalam saja, soalnya di luar panas sekali.
english: We'll just sit inside, because it's very hot outside.

target: Dia tidak masuk kerja hari ini, soalnya anaknya sakit.
english: She isn't coming to work today, because her child is sick.
grammar: soalnya gives the excuse after the fact: Dia tidak masuk, soalnya anaknya sakit = ..., because her child is sick.

target: Beli tiketnya sekarang saja, soalnya kursi kereta cepat habis.
english: Just buy the tickets now, because train seats run out fast.

target: Saya jarang memasak ikan, soalnya anak saya tidak suka baunya.
english: I rarely cook fish, because my child doesn't like the smell.

target: Hujan turun deras sekali, jadi kami menunggu di dalam kafe.
english: The rain came down very hard, so we waited inside a cafe.
grammar: jadi = so; it starts the result: Hujan deras, jadi kami menunggu = It rained hard, so we waited.

target: Baterai ponsel saya habis, jadi saya tidak bisa menelepon kamu.
english: My phone battery ran out, so I couldn't call you.

target: Besok hari libur, jadi kita bisa sarapan pelan-pelan di rumah.
english: Tomorrow is a holiday, so we can have a slow breakfast at home.
grammar: Doubling slows it down: pelan-pelan = slowly, sarapan pelan-pelan = a leisurely breakfast.

target: Kopinya sudah habis, jadi saya memesan segelas teh manis.
english: The coffee was already gone, so I ordered a glass of sweet tea.

target: Hotel itu penuh, jadi kami mencari penginapan lain dekat stasiun.
english: That hotel was full, so we looked for other lodging near the station.

target: Rapatnya selesai lebih cepat, jadi saya bisa pulang sebelum gelap.
english: The meeting finished early, so I can go home before dark.

target: Adik saya sudah bisa memasak, jadi ibu bisa istirahat lebih lama.
english: My younger sibling can already cook, so Mom can rest longer.

target: Toko roti itu tutup hari Senin, jadi kita datang besok saja.
english: That bakery is closed on Mondays, so let's just come tomorrow.
grammar: This jadi = 'so'. jadi also means 'become' (jadi guru = become a teacher) — context decides.

target: Saya lupa membawa dompet, jadi teman saya membayar makan siang.
english: I forgot to bring my wallet, so my friend paid for lunch.

target: Cuaca sore ini cerah, jadi kami jalan kaki ke taman.
english: The weather this afternoon is clear, so we're walking to the park.

target: Tiket pesawat sedang murah, jadi kami memesan untuk bulan Desember.
english: Plane tickets are cheap right now, so we booked for December.

target: Kamar ini kecil, jadi kami menaruh lemari di ruang keluarga.
english: This room is small, so we put the wardrobe in the family room.

target: Saya menulis daftar belanja supaya tidak lupa di toko.
english: I write a shopping list so that I don't forget things at the store.
grammar: supaya = so that (a goal): supaya tidak lupa = so that I don't forget. No extra word for 'that'.

target: Kami berangkat pagi sekali supaya jalan tol masih kosong.
english: We leave very early so that the toll road is still empty.

target: Tolong bicara pelan-pelan supaya nenek bisa mendengar dengan jelas.
english: Please speak slowly so that Grandma can hear clearly.

target: Ibu memotong buah kecil-kecil supaya anak-anak mudah makan.
english: Mom cuts the fruit into small pieces so that the kids can eat it easily.
grammar: Doubled adjective = 'into pieces that size': potong kecil-kecil = cut into small pieces.

target: Simpan tiketmu di kantong depan tas supaya mudah diambil nanti.
english: Keep your ticket in the bag's front pocket so that it's easy to take out later.

target: Kami menabung setiap bulan supaya bisa membeli rumah kecil.
english: We save money every month so that we can buy a small house.

target: Saya menyalakan kipas angin supaya kamar tidak terlalu panas.
english: I turn on the fan so that the room doesn't get too hot.

target: Dia berolahraga tiga kali seminggu supaya badannya tetap sehat.
english: She exercises three times a week so that her body stays healthy.

target: Tutup pintunya rapat-rapat supaya nyamuk tidak masuk malam ini.
english: Close the door tightly so that mosquitoes don't get in tonight.
grammar: supaya tidak = so that ... not: supaya nyamuk tidak masuk = so the mosquitoes don't get in.

target: Mohon datang lima belas menit lebih awal agar acara mulai tepat waktu.
english: Please come fifteen minutes early so that the event starts on time.
grammar: agar = supaya in formal settings (announcements, notices): agar acara mulai tepat waktu. Say supaya in chat.

target: Tamu hotel diminta menunggu di lobi agar semuanya berjalan lancar.
english: Hotel guests are asked to wait in the lobby so that everything runs smoothly.

target: Matikan lampu ruang rapat agar kantor bisa hemat listrik.
english: Turn off the meeting room lights so that the office can save electricity.

target: Kirim laporanmu hari ini agar tim bisa membacanya sebelum rapat.
english: Send your report today so that the team can read it before the meeting.

target: Pengumuman itu dipasang di pintu agar semua karyawan segera tahu.
english: The announcement was put up on the door so that all employees would know right away.

target: Cuci tanganmu dengan sabun agar kuman tidak ikut masuk ke makanan.
english: Wash your hands with soap so that germs don't get into the food.

target: Meskipun hujan deras, pesta pernikahan itu tetap berjalan lancar.
english: Although it rained hard, the wedding party still went smoothly.
grammar: tetap = still/anyway after meskipun: Meskipun hujan, tetap berjalan = Although it rained, it still went ahead.

target: Meskipun sudah malam, toko kopi di sudut itu masih buka.
english: Although it's already late at night, the coffee shop on that corner is still open.
grammar: masih = still (ongoing now): masih buka = still open, masih hujan = still raining.

target: Meskipun harganya mahal, durian itu habis dalam satu jam.
english: Although the price was high, that durian was gone within an hour.

target: Meskipun lelah, ayah tetap menjemput kami di stasiun malam itu.
english: Although he was tired, Dad still picked us up at the station that night.

target: Meskipun kantornya jauh, dia tidak pernah datang terlambat.
english: Although his office is far away, he never arrives late.
grammar: No tapi after a meskipun clause: Meskipun jauh, dia datang — not 'tapi dia datang'.

target: Meskipun baru belajar setahun, bahasa Indonesianya sudah lancar sekali.
english: Although he has only studied for a year, his Indonesian is already very fluent.

target: Meskipun kamarnya kecil, hotel itu bersih dan dekat pantai.
english: Although the rooms are small, that hotel is clean and close to the beach.

target: Meskipun sedang diet, dia mencicipi kue buatan ibunya.
english: Although she is on a diet, she tasted the cake made by her mother.
grammar: buatan = made by: kue buatan ibunya = a cake made by her mother, buatan tangan = handmade.

target: Walaupun sudah tua, kakek masih berkebun setiap pagi di belakang rumah.
english: Although he is old, Grandpa still gardens every morning behind the house.
grammar: walaupun and meskipun both mean 'although' — swap freely: Walaupun tua = Meskipun tua = although (he's) old.

target: Walaupun jalannya jauh, kami memilih naik sepeda ke pasar.
english: Although the way is far, we choose to ride bikes to the market.

target: Walaupun gajinya lebih kecil, dia lebih suka pekerjaan barunya.
english: Although the salary is smaller, she prefers her new job.

target: Walaupun sudah minum obat, kepala saya masih pusing sampai sekarang.
english: Although I've taken medicine, my head is still dizzy even now.

target: Walaupun harus menunggu lama, kami tetap membeli tiket konser itu.
english: Although we had to wait a long time, we still bought the concert tickets.

target: Walaupun hari libur, ayah tetap membalas pesan dari kantornya.
english: Although it's a holiday, Dad still replies to messages from his office.

target: Walaupun masakan itu pedas sekali, turis itu menghabiskannya.
english: Although that dish was very spicy, the tourist finished all of it.
grammar: menghabiskan = to finish off: menghabiskannya = finished it (-nya = it).

target: Walaupun cuaca panas, anak-anak terus bermain bola di lapangan.
english: Although the weather is hot, the kids keep playing ball on the field.

target: Saya sudah mengetuk pintu dua kali, tetapi tidak ada jawaban.
english: I knocked on the door twice, but there was no answer.
grammar: tetapi = 'but' in careful or written style; in everyday talk say tapi: Mahal, tapi enak = Pricey, but tasty.

target: Kami ingin duduk di luar, tetapi semua meja sudah penuh.
english: We wanted to sit outside, but all the tables were already full.

target: Laporan itu sudah selesai, tetapi belum dikirim ke kantor pusat.
english: The report is finished, but it hasn't been sent to the head office yet.

target: Harga kamarnya murah, tetapi sarapannya tidak termasuk.
english: The room rate is cheap, but breakfast isn't included.
grammar: termasuk = included: sarapan tidak termasuk = breakfast not included — check this when booking.

target: Dia sudah tiba di bandara, tetapi pesawatnya tertunda dua jam.
english: He has arrived at the airport, but his plane is delayed by two hours.

target: Saya suka apartemen itu, tetapi jaraknya terlalu jauh dari kantor.
english: I like that apartment, but the distance to the office is too far.

target: Aku mau ikut ke pasar malam, tapi besok ada ujian.
english: I want to come along to the night market, but tomorrow there's an exam.
grammar: tapi is the everyday 'but' — fine in conversation: mau ikut, tapi ada ujian = want to come, but there's an exam.

target: Filmnya bagus, tapi kursi bioskopnya kurang nyaman.
english: The movie was good, but the cinema seats weren't very comfortable.

target: Saya sudah memanggil taksi, tapi mobilnya belum datang juga.
english: I've already called a taxi, but the car still hasn't come.
grammar: belum ... juga = STILL not: belum datang juga = still hasn't come (with impatience).

target: Kue ini enak, tapi terlalu manis untuk ayah saya.
english: This cake is tasty, but too sweet for my father.

target: Kami ingin berenang, tapi ombak sore ini besar sekali.
english: We want to swim, but the waves this afternoon are very big.

target: Dia rajin bekerja, tapi jarang mengambil cuti panjang.
english: He works hard, but rarely takes long leave.

target: Saya mencari sandal ukuran empat puluh, tapi warnanya tinggal hitam.
english: I'm looking for size forty sandals, but the only color left is black.
grammar: tinggal here = left/remaining: warnanya tinggal hitam = the only color left is black.

target: Rumah nenek jauh, tapi kami mengunjunginya setiap bulan.
english: Grandma's house is far away, but we visit her every month.

target: Tadi saya mampir ke tokomu, tapi pintunya sudah dikunci.
english: Earlier I stopped by your shop, but the door was already locked.

target: Bahasa Indonesianya belum lancar, tapi dia berani berbicara dengan siapa saja.
english: His Indonesian isn't fluent yet, but he dares to speak with anyone.

target: Hujan sudah berhenti, tapi jalan di depan rumah masih banjir.
english: The rain has stopped, but the road in front of the house is still flooded.

target: Ibu menyanyikan lagu lama sambil menjemur pakaian di halaman.
english: Mom sings an old song while hanging out the laundry in the yard.

target: Dia mendengarkan radio sambil menyetir ke kantor.
english: He listens to the radio while driving to the office.
grammar: sambil = while (one person, two actions at once): mendengarkan radio sambil menyetir = listen while driving.

target: Kami membahas rencana liburan sambil menunggu pesanan datang.
english: We discuss our holiday plans while waiting for our order to arrive.

target: Ayah minum kopi hitam sambil membaca koran pagi di teras.
english: Dad drinks black coffee while reading the morning paper on the porch.

target: Anak itu belajar berhitung sambil bermain kartu warna-warni.
english: That child learns to count while playing with colorful cards.

target: Saya menunggu bus sambil membalas pesan dari teman lama.
english: I wait for the bus while replying to messages from an old friend.

target: Mereka berjalan pelan-pelan di pantai sambil mencari kerang kecil.
english: They walk slowly along the beach while looking for little seashells.

target: Jangan main ponsel sambil menyeberang jalan, itu bahaya sekali.
english: Don't play on your phone while crossing the street; that's very dangerous.

target: Kakak memotong sayur sambil menonton acara masak di televisi.
english: Big sister chops vegetables while watching a cooking show on television.

target: Kami mengobrol santai sambil menikmati teh hangat di warung.
english: We chat casually while enjoying warm tea at the food stall.

target: Sebelum tamu datang, kami membersihkan ruang tamu bersama-sama.
english: Before the guests arrive, we clean the living room together.
grammar: sebelum can front a whole clause: Sebelum tamu datang, kami membersihkan = Before guests arrive, we clean.

target: Isi formulir ini sebelum namamu dipanggil di loket.
english: Fill in this form before your name is called at the counter.
grammar: di- = 'gets ...-ed': dipanggil = gets called, namamu dipanggil = your name is called.

target: Sebelum harga naik lagi, kami membeli tiket untuk liburan akhir tahun.
english: Before prices go up again, we're buying tickets for the year-end holiday.

target: Saya mengecek kompor dan jendela sebelum kami pergi berlibur.
english: I check the stove and the windows before we go on vacation.

target: Sebelum rapat dimulai, tolong bagikan laporan ini ke semua orang.
english: Before the meeting starts, please hand out this report to everyone.

target: Kami tiba di stasiun sebelum kereta pertama berangkat.
english: We arrived at the station before the first train departed.

target: Sebelum anak-anak bangun, ibu sudah menyiapkan sarapan di meja.
english: Before the kids wake up, Mom has already set out breakfast on the table.
grammar: No tense word after sebelum: sebelum anak-anak bangun covers 'before the kids wake / woke up'.

target: Sebelum hujan turun, angkat jemuran di halaman belakang, ya.
english: Before the rain comes down, bring in the laundry in the backyard, okay?
grammar: ya at the end softens a request: angkat jemuran, ya = bring in the laundry, okay?

target: Sebelum kamu tanda tangan, baca dulu semua halaman kontrak itu.
english: Before you sign, first read every page of that contract.

target: Sesudah hujan berhenti, kami melanjutkan perjalanan ke arah selatan.
english: After the rain stopped, we continued the journey southward.
grammar: sesudah = after; setelah means the same: Sesudah hujan berhenti = After the rain stopped.

target: Sesudah tamu terakhir pulang, kami mencuci semua piring kotor.
english: After the last guest went home, we washed all the dirty dishes.

target: Sesudah dia lulus kuliah, dia langsung bekerja di bank daerah.
english: After he graduated from college, he went straight to work at a local bank.

target: Sesudah kamu mencoba baju itu, gantung lagi di tempatnya, ya.
english: After you try on that dress, hang it back in its place, okay?

target: Sesudah pesawat mendarat, kami langsung mencari taksi ke hotel.
english: After the plane landed, we immediately looked for a taxi to the hotel.

target: Sesudah makan malam selesai, ayah mencuci piring dan saya mengeringkannya.
english: After dinner is over, Dad washes the dishes and I dry them.

target: Sesudah obatnya habis, jangan lupa kembali ke klinik lagi.
english: After the medicine runs out, don't forget to come back to the clinic.

target: Sesudah kelas selesai, kami mengobrol dalam bahasa Indonesia di kantin.
english: After class ends, we chat in Indonesian in the canteen.

target: Sesudah gajian, dia selalu mengajak keluarganya makan di luar.
english: After payday, he always takes his family out to eat.
grammar: gajian = payday (from gaji, salary): sesudah gajian = after payday.

target: Berangkat sekarang, kalau tidak kita ketinggalan kereta pagi.
english: Leave now; otherwise we'll miss the morning train.
grammar: kalau tidak = otherwise (literally 'if not'): kalau tidak, kita ketinggalan kereta = otherwise we miss the train.

target: Tulis alamatnya sekarang, kalau tidak kamu pasti lupa lagi.
english: Write down the address now; otherwise you'll definitely forget again.

target: Simpan kue itu di kulkas, kalau tidak semut datang.
english: Put that cake in the fridge; otherwise the ants will come.

target: Pakai topi dan kacamata hitam, kalau tidak kepalamu kepanasan.
english: Wear a hat and sunglasses; otherwise your head will get overheated.

target: Kita harus memesan meja dulu, kalau tidak restorannya pasti penuh.
english: We have to reserve a table first; otherwise the restaurant will definitely be full.

target: Kerjakan tugasmu malam ini, kalau tidak besok kamu akan repot.
english: Do your assignment tonight; otherwise tomorrow you'll be in trouble.

target: Bawa jaket tebal ke gunung, kalau tidak kamu kedinginan malam hari.
english: Bring a thick jacket to the mountain; otherwise you'll be freezing at night.
grammar: ke-...-an = badly affected by: kedinginan = freezing cold, kehujanan = caught in the rain.

target: Catat semua pengeluaranmu, kalau tidak uang gajimu cepat habis.
english: Write down all your expenses; otherwise your salary will run out fast.

target: Karena besok ada rapat penting, saya menyiapkan bahannya malam ini.
english: Because there's an important meeting tomorrow, I'm preparing the materials tonight.

target: Dia bekerja sambil kuliah, jadi waktunya untuk istirahat sedikit sekali.
english: He works while going to college, so he has very little time to rest.

target: Kalau kamu lelah, istirahat dulu sebelum kita melanjutkan latihan ini.
english: If you're tired, rest first before we continue this practice.

target: Meskipun sudah larut, dia menunggu di bandara supaya bisa menjemput tamunya.
english: Although it was late, he waited at the airport so that he could pick up his guest.

target: Saya membawa kamus kecil, jadi saya bisa membaca menu walaupun tidak ada gambarnya.
english: I brought a small dictionary, so I can read the menu even though there are no pictures.
grammar: walaupun can sit mid-sentence: bisa membaca walaupun tidak ada gambar = can read even though no pictures.

target: Tanya dulu harganya sebelum kamu membayar, soalnya di pasar bisa tawar-menawar.
english: Ask the price first before you pay, because at the market you can haggle.
grammar: tawar-menawar = haggling (back-and-forth doubling): bisa tawar-menawar = you can bargain.

target: Kami berangkat sebelum matahari terbit supaya tiba di puncak sebelum siang.
english: We set off before sunrise so that we'd reach the peak before midday.

target: Dia bilang dia akan datang sedikit terlambat.
english: He said he will come a little late.
grammar: bilang is the everyday 'say/tell': Dia bilang dia sibuk. = He said he's busy.

target: Ibu bilang makan malam sudah siap di meja.
english: Mom said dinner is already ready on the table.

target: Ayah bilang kita berangkat jam tujuh besok pagi.
english: Dad said we leave at seven tomorrow morning.

target: Manajer bilang rapat dimulai jam sepuluh pagi.
english: The manager said the meeting starts at ten in the morning.

target: Teman saya bilang restoran itu enak dan murah.
english: My friend said that restaurant is tasty and cheap.

target: Dia bilang kunci kamar ada di tasnya.
english: She said the room key is in her bag.

target: Petugas bilang kereta berikutnya datang jam sebelas.
english: The officer said the next train comes at eleven.

target: Adik saya bilang dia mau ikut ke pasar.
english: My little sibling said he wants to come along to the market.

target: Dokter bilang saya perlu minum lebih banyak air.
english: The doctor said I need to drink more water.

target: Dia bilang filmnya bagus, tapi terlalu panjang.
english: He said the movie is good, but too long.

target: Kakak bilang dia sudah membeli tiket untuk kita.
english: My older sibling said she already bought tickets for us.

target: Tetangga bilang cuaca akan panas sekali minggu ini.
english: The neighbor said the weather will be very hot this week.

target: Bos saya bilang laporan ini harus selesai hari Jumat.
