english: My boss said this report must be finished on Friday.

target: Dia bilang toko itu tutup setiap hari Minggu.
english: He said that shop is closed every Sunday.

target: Sopir bilang jalan ke bandara sedang macet.
english: The driver said the road to the airport is congested right now.

target: Mereka bilang pantai di sana bersih dan tenang.
english: They said the beach over there is clean and calm.

target: Guru bilang anak saya rajin sekali di kelas.
english: The teacher said my child is very diligent in class.

target: Dia bilang harganya sudah termasuk sarapan.
english: He said the price already includes breakfast.

target: Kata siapa? Saya tidak pernah bilang begitu.
english: Says who? I never said that.
grammar: kata + person = 'X says': Kata siapa? = Says who? Kata ibu, boleh. = Mom says it's allowed.

target: Dia bilang ke saya dia tidak bisa datang malam ini.
english: He told me he can't come tonight.
grammar: bilang ke X = tell X: Dia bilang ke saya. = He told me.

target: Manajer bilang bahwa jadwal rapat berubah lagi.
english: The manager said that the meeting schedule changed again.
grammar: bahwa = 'that' is written-style; speakers usually drop it: Dia bilang (bahwa) dia setuju.

target: Dia bilang bahwa dia sudah membaca email saya.
english: He said that he had already read my email.

target: Petugas bilang bahwa penerbangan kami ditunda dua jam.
english: The officer said that our flight is delayed two hours.

target: Ibu bilang bahwa nenek akan menginap di rumah kita.
english: Mom said that grandma will stay over at our house.

target: Dia bilang bahwa kabar itu belum tentu benar.
english: She said that that news is not necessarily true.
grammar: belum tentu = not necessarily: Katanya begitu, tapi belum tentu benar.

target: Dalam suratnya, dia bilang bahwa dia ingin cepat pulang.
english: In his letter, he said that he wants to come home soon.

target: Dia hanya bilang dia lelah, tidak bilang kenapa.
english: He only said he was tired, he didn't say why.

target: Saya sudah bilang berkali-kali bahwa pintunya harus dikunci.
english: I have said many times that the door must be locked.

target: Tolong bilang ke ayah bahwa saya pulang agak malam.
english: Please tell dad that I'm coming home a bit late.
grammar: tolong bilang ke X = please tell X: Tolong bilang ke ibu, ya.

target: Tolong bilang ke sopir supaya menunggu di depan hotel.
english: Please tell the driver to wait in front of the hotel.
grammar: bilang supaya + verb = tell someone to do it: Bilang supaya dia menunggu.

target: Tolong bilang ke ibu kalau nasi di dapur sudah habis.
english: Please tell mom that the rice in the kitchen is finished.
grammar: After bilang, spoken Indonesian often uses kalau for 'that': Dia bilang kalau macet.

target: Tolong bilang ke tim bahwa rapat sore ini dibatalkan.
english: Please tell the team that this afternoon's meeting is canceled.

target: Tolong sampaikan salam saya ke keluarga kamu di Bandung.
english: Please pass on my greetings to your family in Bandung.
grammar: sampaikan salam = pass on greetings: Sampaikan salam saya ke ibu kamu.

target: Tolong sampaikan pesan ini ke manajer sebelum jam dua.
english: Please pass this message to the manager before two o'clock.

target: Jangan bilang ke siapa-siapa dulu, ini masih rahasia.
english: Don't tell anyone yet, this is still a secret.
grammar: siapa-siapa after a negative = anyone: Jangan bilang ke siapa-siapa.

target: Kalau kamu bertemu dia, tolong bilang saya menunggu di sini.
english: If you meet him, please tell him I'm waiting here.

target: Tolong bilang ke tamu bahwa kamarnya sudah siap.
english: Please tell the guest that their room is ready.

target: Bilang ke adikmu, makan siangnya ada di kulkas.
english: Tell your little sibling, his lunch is in the fridge.

target: Nanti saya bilang ke resepsionis soal AC yang rusak itu.
english: Later I'll tell the receptionist about the broken air conditioner.

target: Dia sudah bilang ke saya soal rencana liburan kalian.
english: He already told me about your vacation plans.

target: Katanya besok akan hujan deras sepanjang hari.
english: They say tomorrow it will rain heavily all day long.
grammar: katanya = 'they say / (s)he said' — a one-word rumor marker: Katanya besok libur.

target: Katanya restoran baru itu selalu ramai malam hari.
english: They say that new restaurant is always crowded at night.

target: Katanya dia pindah ke Surabaya bulan depan.
english: They say he's moving to Surabaya next month.

target: Katanya tiket konser itu sudah habis terjual.
english: They say the concert tickets are already sold out.

target: Katanya museum ini gratis setiap hari Kamis.
english: They say this museum is free every Thursday.

target: Katanya bos akan memberi tugas baru minggu depan.
english: They say the boss will give out new assignments next week.

target: Katanya jalan itu ditutup karena ada perbaikan.
english: They say that road is closed because there are repairs.

target: Katanya keluarga mereka sudah tinggal di sini sejak dulu.
english: They say their family has lived here since long ago.
grammar: sejak dulu = since long ago: Mereka di sini sejak dulu. = They've been here forever.

target: Katanya dia berhenti kerja karena mau membuka usaha sendiri.
english: They say he quit his job because he wants to open his own business.

target: Katanya hotel itu penuh sampai akhir bulan ini.
english: They say that hotel is full until the end of this month.

target: Katanya kopi di warung itu paling enak di kota ini.
english: They say the coffee at that stall is the tastiest in this city.

target: Katanya dia sakit, makanya dia tidak masuk hari ini.
english: They say he's sick, that's why he didn't come in today.

target: Katanya ada pasar malam di dekat stasiun minggu ini.
english: They say there's a night market near the station this week.

target: Saya belum yakin, tapi katanya harga bensin naik lagi.
english: I'm not sure yet, but they say the price of gasoline is going up again.

target: Katanya paman akan datang membawa oleh-oleh dari Bali.
english: They say uncle will come bringing souvenirs from Bali.

target: Menurut saya, warna biru lebih cocok untuk kamu.
english: In my opinion, the color blue suits you better.
grammar: menurut saya = in my opinion: Menurut saya, itu ide bagus.

target: Menurut dia, film itu terlalu sedih untuk anak-anak.
english: According to him, that movie is too sad for children.

target: Menurut dokter, ayah tidak boleh makan terlalu banyak gula.
english: According to the doctor, dad may not eat too much sugar.

target: Menurut berita, sore ini akan turun hujan deras.
english: According to the news, this afternoon heavy rain will fall.

target: Menurut peta ini, museumnya tidak jauh dari sini.
english: According to this map, the museum isn't far from here.
grammar: menurut also cites sources: menurut peta = according to the map.

target: Menurut ibu, masakan rumah lebih sehat daripada makanan restoran.
english: According to mom, home cooking is healthier than restaurant food.

target: Menurut kamu, baju yang mana yang paling bagus?
english: In your opinion, which shirt is the nicest?
grammar: Menurut kamu…? asks someone's opinion: Menurut kamu, yang mana lebih bagus?

target: Menurut mereka, kantor baru kita terlalu jauh dari stasiun.
english: According to them, our new office is too far from the station.

target: Menurut petugas, loket tiket dibuka jam delapan pagi.
english: According to the officer, the ticket counter opens at eight in the morning.

target: Menurut saya, rencana ini masih perlu dibahas lagi.
english: In my opinion, this plan still needs to be discussed again.

target: Menurut kakak, jalan kaki lebih cepat daripada naik mobil di sini.
english: According to my older sibling, walking is faster than taking a car here.

target: Menurut berita tadi pagi, jalan tol masih ditutup.
english: According to the news this morning, the toll road is still closed.

target: Menurut dia, kita sebaiknya berangkat lebih pagi besok.
english: According to her, we had better leave earlier tomorrow.
grammar: sebaiknya = it'd be better to: Sebaiknya kita pulang sekarang.

target: Menurut banyak orang, pegawai toko itu ramah dan sopan.
english: According to many people, the employees of that shop are friendly and polite.

target: Menurut ayah, harga mobil itu masih terlalu mahal.
english: According to dad, the price of that car is still too expensive.

target: Menurut teman kantor saya, kantin di lantai dua lebih murah.
english: According to my office friend, the canteen on the second floor is cheaper.

target: Menurut saya, kita tidak perlu buru-buru mengambil keputusan.
english: In my opinion, we don't need to rush into making a decision.

target: Menurut jadwal, bus terakhir berangkat jam sembilan malam.
english: According to the schedule, the last bus departs at nine at night.

target: Saya pikir kita harus mencoba restoran baru itu.
english: I think we have to try that new restaurant.
grammar: saya pikir = I think: Saya pikir dia benar. = I think he's right.

target: Saya rasa harga kamar ini terlalu mahal untuk kita.
english: I feel the price of this room is too expensive for us.
grammar: saya rasa = I feel / I'd say — a soft opinion: Saya rasa itu cukup.

target: Saya pikir dia sudah pulang, ternyata masih di kantor.
english: I thought he had gone home; it turns out he's still at the office.
grammar: saya pikir also = 'I thought (wrongly)': Saya pikir kamu sudah pulang.

target: Saya rasa kopi ini kurang manis untuk saya.
english: I feel this coffee isn't sweet enough for me.

target: Saya pikir rapat ini bisa selesai sebelum jam dua belas.
english: I think this meeting can finish before twelve o'clock.

target: Saya rasa dia tidak akan datang ke pesta malam ini.
english: I feel he won't come to the party tonight.

target: Saya pikir jalan kaki saja, soalnya hotelnya dekat.
english: I think let's just walk, since the hotel is close.
grammar: soalnya = everyday 'because': Kami di rumah, soalnya hujan.

target: Saya rasa kita pernah bertemu di suatu tempat sebelumnya.
english: I feel we have met somewhere before.
grammar: pernah = have ever / once: Saya pernah ke Bali. = I've been to Bali.

target: Saya pikir warna ini cocok dengan tasmu.
english: I think this color goes well with your bag.

target: Saya rasa ukuran baju ini terlalu kecil untuk ayah.
english: I feel the size of this shirt is too small for dad.

target: Saya pikir kamu benar soal masalah jadwal kemarin.
english: I think you're right about yesterday's schedule problem.

target: Saya rasa anak-anak sudah terlalu lelah untuk jalan-jalan lagi.
english: I feel the kids are already too tired to walk around any more.

target: Awalnya saya pikir ini mudah, ternyata cukup sulit.
english: At first I thought this was easy; it turns out it's quite hard.
grammar: ternyata = it turns out: Saya pikir mahal, ternyata murah.

target: Saya rasa lebih baik kita tanya orang di sana.
english: I feel it's better if we ask the person over there.

target: Saya pikir dia setuju, ternyata dia menolak rencana itu.
english: I thought he agreed; it turns out he rejected the plan.
grammar: menolak = to turn down: Dia menolak tawaran itu. = He turned down that offer.

target: Kamu pikir kita bisa sampai sebelum toko tutup?
english: Do you think we can get there before the shop closes?

target: Saya rasa porsi di sini cukup besar untuk dua orang.
english: I feel the portions here are big enough for two people.

target: Saya pikir begitu juga, kita memang perlu istirahat.
english: I think so too, we really do need a rest.

target: Saya setuju dengan ide itu, tapi waktunya kurang tepat.
english: I agree with that idea, but the timing isn't quite right.
grammar: setuju = agree; the opposite is simply tidak setuju: Saya tidak setuju.

target: Kami semua setuju rapatnya dipindah ke hari Rabu.
english: We all agree the meeting is moved to Wednesday.

target: Ibu tidak setuju kalau kamu pulang terlalu malam.
english: Mom doesn't agree with you coming home too late.

target: Apakah kamu setuju dengan pendapatnya tadi?
english: Do you agree with his opinion just now?
grammar: apakah opens a yes/no question: Apakah kamu setuju? = Do you agree?

target: Ayah setuju, tapi dia meminta kita hati-hati di jalan.
english: Dad agrees, but he asks us to be careful on the road.

target: Saya kurang setuju dengan rencana itu, terlalu berisiko.
english: I don't quite agree with that plan; it's too risky.
grammar: kurang softens a no: kurang setuju = don't quite agree, kurang suka = don't really like.

target: Mereka belum setuju soal harga sewa rumah itu.
english: They haven't agreed yet about the rent for that house.

target: Kalau semua setuju, kita berangkat hari Sabtu pagi.
english: If everyone agrees, we leave on Saturday morning.

target: Dia setuju membantu kita menyiapkan acara ulang tahun nenek.
english: She agrees to help us prepare grandma's birthday party.

target: Saya setuju sekali, tempat ini memang cocok untuk keluarga.
english: I totally agree, this place really is suitable for families.

target: Bos belum setuju dengan anggaran baru untuk proyek kita.
english: The boss hasn't agreed yet to the new budget for our project.

target: Kenapa kamu tidak setuju? Coba jelaskan alasanmu pelan-pelan.
english: Why don't you agree? Try to explain your reason slowly.

target: Akhirnya kami setuju untuk membayar biaya bensin bersama-sama.
english: In the end we agreed to pay the fuel costs together.

target: Suami saya sudah setuju, jadi kami akan membeli rumah itu.
english: My husband has agreed, so we are going to buy that house.

target: Dia tanya kapan kita datang ke rumahnya.
english: He asked when we're coming to his house.
grammar: tanya + question word reports a question: Dia tanya kapan kita datang.

target: Ibu tanya di mana kamu menyimpan kunci motornya.
english: Mom asked where you keep the motorbike's key.

target: Petugas tanya berapa lama kami akan tinggal di sini.
english: The officer asked how long we will stay here.
grammar: berapa lama = how long: Berapa lama kamu tinggal di sini?

target: Dia tanya apakah kamar ini masih kosong besok malam.
english: He asked whether this room is still vacant tomorrow night.
grammar: apakah mid-sentence = 'whether': Dia tanya apakah saya lapar.

target: Teman saya tanya siapa yang akan menjemput kita di bandara.
english: My friend asked who will pick us up at the airport.

target: Bos tanya kenapa laporan penjualan bulan lalu belum masuk.
english: The boss asked why last month's sales report hasn't come in yet.

target: Saya tidak tahu apakah dia jadi datang atau tidak.
english: I don't know whether he's actually coming or not.
grammar: jadi before a verb = 'actually end up': Jadi berangkat? = Still going?

target: Dia tidak bilang di mana kita akan bertemu besok.
english: He didn't say where we will meet tomorrow.

target: Tolong tanya ke petugas jam berapa loket ini dibuka.
english: Please ask the officer what time this counter opens.

target: Saya lupa menanyakan berapa harga tiket untuk anak-anak.
english: I forgot to ask how much tickets for children cost.
grammar: menanyakan X = to ask about X: menanyakan harga = to ask the price.

target: Kakak tanya apakah kamu mau ikut makan malam bersama.
english: My older sibling asked whether you want to join dinner together.

target: Dia ingin tahu bagaimana cara memesan taksi lewat aplikasi.
english: She wants to know how to order a taxi through the app.
grammar: bagaimana cara + verb = how to: Bagaimana cara memesan tiket?

target: Tamu itu tanya apakah harga kamar sudah termasuk sarapan.
english: That guest asked whether the room price already includes breakfast.

target: Anak saya terus tanya kapan kita pergi ke kebun binatang.
english: My child keeps asking when we're going to the zoo.

target: Dia tanya bagaimana rasanya tinggal jauh dari keluarga.
english: She asked what it feels like to live far from family.
grammar: rasanya = 'it feels / the taste of it': Bagaimana rasanya? = How is it?

target: Saya mau tanya dulu ke istri saya sebelum memutuskan.
english: I want to ask my wife first before deciding.

target: Mereka tanya kenapa kami pindah ke kota sekecil ini.
english: They asked why we moved to a town this small.

target: Dia belum menjawab pertanyaan saya tentang jadwal minggu depan.
english: He hasn't answered my question about next week's schedule yet.

target: Kalau tidak jelas, jangan malu bertanya sekali lagi.
english: If it's not clear, don't be embarrassed to ask one more time.
grammar: jangan malu = don't be shy: Jangan malu bertanya di kelas.

target: Sebelum pulang, dia sempat tanya kabar keluargamu.
english: Before going home, he found a moment to ask how your family is.
grammar: sempat = found a moment to: Saya sempat mampir tadi.

target: Permisi, berapa harga sepatu kulit ini?
english: Excuse me, how much are these leather shoes?

target: Harga tas ini dua ratus lima puluh ribu rupiah.
english: This bag costs two hundred and fifty thousand rupiah.
grammar: Big prices stack left to right: dua ratus lima puluh ribu = 250,000.

target: Kemeja batik ini seratus dua puluh ribu, Pak.
english: This batik shirt is one hundred and twenty thousand, sir.

target: Totalnya tiga ratus empat puluh lima ribu, Kak.
english: The total is three hundred and forty-five thousand, miss.

target: Harga kamarnya empat ratus ribu semalam, sudah termasuk sarapan.
english: The room costs four hundred thousand a night, breakfast already included.

target: Satu kilo mangga di pasar ini lima belas ribu.
english: One kilo of mangoes at this market is fifteen thousand.
grammar: belas = -teen, puluh = tens: lima belas = 15, lima puluh = 50.

target: Ongkos ojek ke stasiun biasanya dua puluh ribu.
english: The motorbike-taxi fare to the station is usually twenty thousand.

target: Kalau mau ambil dua, dua ratus ribu saja, Bu.
english: If you want to take two, just two hundred thousand, ma'am.

target: Berapa harga satu dus air mineral di sini?
english: How much is one carton of mineral water here?

target: Harga tiket masuk museum tiga puluh ribu untuk dewasa.
english: The museum entrance ticket is thirty thousand for adults.

target: Sewa motor di sini tujuh puluh lima ribu sehari.
english: Renting a motorbike here is seventy-five thousand a day.

target: Total belanjaan kamu enam ratus sembilan puluh ribu rupiah.
english: Your total shopping comes to six hundred and ninety thousand rupiah.

target: Durian ini sembilan puluh ribu, sudah paling murah.
english: This durian is ninety thousand, already the lowest price.

target: Harga bensin naik lagi mulai minggu ini.
english: The price of petrol is going up again starting this week.

target: Biaya kirim ke Surabaya lima belas ribu per kilo.
english: Shipping to Surabaya costs fifteen thousand per kilo.
grammar: biaya = cost, fee: biaya kirim = shipping cost. You will also hear ongkir (ongkos kirim).

target: Harganya masih boleh ditawar sedikit, Bu?
english: Can the price still be bargained down a little, ma'am?
grammar: di- flips who acts: ditawar = get bargained; harganya boleh ditawar = the price can be haggled.

target: Kalau dua ratus ribu bagaimana? Ini uangnya.
english: How about two hundred thousand? Here is the money.

target: Wah, masih terlalu mahal untuk saya, Pak.
english: Wow, that is still too expensive for me, sir.

target: Turunkan sedikit, Pak, nanti saya ambil dua pasang.
english: Lower it a little, sir, and I will take two pairs.
grammar: -kan makes 'cause to': turun = go down, turunkan = lower it. Turunkan harganya!

target: Ini harga pas, tidak bisa kurang lagi.
english: This is a fixed price, it cannot go down any more.
grammar: harga pas = fixed price — the seller's polite signal that bargaining is over.

target: Kalau boleh seratus delapan puluh ribu, saya ambil sekarang.
english: If one hundred and eighty thousand is okay, I will take it now.

target: Di toko sebelah, barang yang sama lebih murah.
english: At the shop next door, the same item is cheaper.

target: Baiklah, khusus untuk kamu, dua ratus ribu saja.
english: Alright, just for you, only two hundred thousand.

target: Penjualnya tidak mau menurunkan harga sama sekali.
english: The seller does not want to lower the price at all.

target: Saya menawar seratus ribu, dan penjualnya langsung mau.
english: I offered one hundred thousand, and the seller immediately said yes.

target: Kalau tidak bisa kurang, saya mau mencari di toko lain.
english: If it cannot go down, I want to look in another shop.

target: Tawar saja dulu, harga di pasar selalu bisa turun.
english: Just bargain first, prices at the market can always come down.

target: Jangan malu menawar kalau berbelanja di pasar tradisional.
english: Do not be shy about bargaining when you shop at a traditional market.
grammar: menawar = to haggle; menawarkan = to offer. Saya menawar harganya = I bargained over the price.

target: Mau bayar pakai kartu atau tunai, Kak?
english: Would you like to pay by card or cash, miss?

target: Saya membayar dengan kartu kredit di kasir.
english: I pay with a credit card at the register.

target: Maaf, warung ini hanya menerima uang tunai.
english: Sorry, this food stall only accepts cash.

target: Bisa bayar pakai QRIS di sini?
english: Can I pay with QRIS here?
grammar: QRIS (say: kris) is the QR code payment used everywhere: bayar pakai QRIS.

target: Mesin kartunya rusak, jadi saya membayar tunai.
english: The card machine is broken, so I am paying cash.

target: Uangnya sudah saya transfer ke rekening kamu tadi pagi.
english: I already transferred the money to your account this morning.
grammar: Put the thing first for done deals: uangnya sudah saya transfer = the money, I already sent.

target: Tolong kirim bukti transfer lewat WhatsApp, ya.
english: Please send proof of the transfer via WhatsApp, okay?

target: Pembayaran dengan transfer bank juga bisa, Pak.
english: Payment by bank transfer is also possible, sir.

target: Jangan lupa minta struk setelah membayar.
english: Do not forget to ask for a receipt after paying.

target: Saya salah memasukkan PIN tiga kali tadi.
english: I entered my PIN wrong three times earlier.

target: Kartu saya ditolak, mungkin saldonya kurang.
english: My card was declined, maybe the balance is not enough.
grammar: saldo = account balance: saldonya kurang = the balance is not enough.

target: Sopir bus biasanya meminta uang pas dari penumpang.
english: Bus drivers usually ask passengers for exact change.
grammar: uang pas = exact change: bayar dengan uang pas = pay with the exact amount.

target: Boleh minta nota untuk laporan kantor saya?
english: May I ask for a receipt for my office report?
grammar: nota = handwritten receipt from small shops; struk = the printed one.

target: Aplikasi bank saya tidak bisa dibuka, jadi saya membayar tunai.
english: My banking app could not be opened, so I paid in cash.

target: Ini kembaliannya lima puluh ribu, silakan dihitung dulu.
english: Here is your change, fifty thousand, please count it first.
grammar: kembalian = your change, from kembali (come back): Ini kembaliannya.

target: Maaf, saya tidak punya uang kecil untuk kembalian.
english: Sorry, I do not have small bills for the change.

target: Maaf Mbak, kembaliannya kurang lima ribu.
english: Sorry, miss, the change is five thousand short.
grammar: Mbak politely addresses a young woman: Maaf, Mbak = excuse me, miss.

target: Penjual itu mengembalikan uang saya karena barangnya rusak.
english: That seller returned my money because the item was broken.

target: Simpan kembaliannya untuk parkir nanti sore.
english: Keep the change for parking later this afternoon.

target: Ada uang pas? Saya tidak ada kembalian sama sekali.
english: Do you have exact change? I have no change at all.

target: Dia menghitung kembalian dengan cepat tanpa kalkulator.
english: He counts the change quickly without a calculator.

target: Tolong tukar uang seratus ribu ini dengan uang kecil.
english: Please change this one hundred thousand note into small bills.

target: Kembalian dari warung tadi masih di kantong celana saya.
english: The change from the food stall earlier is still in my trouser pocket.

target: Kasirnya memberi kembalian permen karena tidak ada uang receh.
english: The cashier gave candy as change because there were no coins.
grammar: uang receh = coins, loose change: tidak ada receh = no coins.

target: Saya harus menarik uang di ATM dulu.
english: I have to withdraw money at an ATM first.
grammar: tarik = pull; menarik uang = withdraw money: menarik uang di ATM.

target: ATM terdekat ada di depan minimarket itu.
english: The nearest ATM is in front of that minimarket.

target: Antrean di ATM panjang sekali hari ini.
english: The queue at the ATM is very long today.
grammar: antre = to queue; antrean = the queue: antreannya panjang = the line is long.

target: Mesin ATM ini sedang rusak, coba yang di seberang.
english: This ATM machine is out of order, try the one across the street.

target: Kartu ATM saya tertelan di mesin kemarin sore.
english: My ATM card got swallowed in the machine yesterday afternoon.
grammar: ter- often means 'by accident': tertelan = got swallowed. Kartu saya tertelan.

target: Masukkan kartu, lalu pilih bahasa Indonesia atau Inggris.
english: Insert your card, then choose Indonesian or English.

target: Jangan lupa mengambil kartu setelah menarik uang.
english: Do not forget to take your card after withdrawing money.

target: Saya menarik satu juta rupiah untuk belanja bulanan.
english: I withdrew one million rupiah for the monthly shopping.
grammar: juta = million: satu juta rupiah = 1,000,000 rupiah.

target: ATM ini hanya mengeluarkan pecahan seratus ribu.
english: This ATM only dispenses one-hundred-thousand notes.
grammar: pecahan = note size: pecahan seratus ribu = 100,000 notes.

target: Biaya tarik tunai di ATM bank lain lima ribu.
english: The cash withdrawal fee at another bank's ATM is five thousand.

target: Tutup layar dengan tangan waktu memasukkan PIN.
english: Cover the screen with your hand when entering your PIN.

target: Saldo saya tinggal dua ratus ribu sampai gajian.
english: My balance is only two hundred thousand left until payday.
grammar: gajian = payday, from gaji (salary): sampai gajian = until payday.

target: Saya mau mengisi pulsa lima puluh ribu.
english: I want to top up fifty thousand of phone credit.
grammar: pulsa = prepaid phone credit: mengisi pulsa = to top up your phone.

target: Pulsa saya habis, jadi tidak bisa menelepon.
english: My phone credit has run out, so I cannot make calls.

target: Di konter itu bisa mengisi pulsa semua operator.
english: At that kiosk you can top up credit for all operators.
grammar: konter = small phone-credit shop; konter pulsa signs are on every street.

target: Pulsanya sudah masuk, silakan cek HP kamu.
english: The credit has come through, please check your phone.

target: Nanti pulsanya saya kirimkan ke nomor kamu.
english: I will send the phone credit to your number later.

target: Sekarang banyak orang membeli pulsa lewat aplikasi.
english: Nowadays many people buy phone credit through an app.

target: Paket data saya habis sebelum akhir bulan.
english: My data package ran out before the end of the month.

target: Tetangga saya berjualan pulsa dan token listrik.
english: My neighbor sells phone credit and electricity tokens.
grammar: token listrik = prepaid electricity code: beli token listrik = buy power credit.

target: Kalau membeli pulsa dua puluh lima ribu, ada bonus internet.
english: If you buy twenty-five thousand of credit, there is an internet bonus.

target: Tolong isikan pulsa ke nomor ibu saya, ya.
english: Please top up credit for my mother's number, okay?
grammar: isikan = fill it for someone: isikan pulsa ke nomor ini = top up this number.

target: Saya mau mengirim paket ini ke Bandung.
english: I want to send this package to Bandung.

target: Kantor pos buka sampai jam empat sore.
english: The post office is open until four in the afternoon.

target: Berapa ongkos kirim paket satu kilo ke Bali?
english: How much does it cost to ship a one-kilo package to Bali?

target: Paketnya tiba dalam tiga hari kalau pakai kilat.
english: The package arrives within three days if you use express.
grammar: kilat = lightning: pos kilat = express mail. Kalau pakai kilat = if you use express.

target: Tolong bungkus paketnya dengan rapi supaya tidak rusak.
english: Please wrap the package neatly so it does not get damaged.

target: Saya mau mengambil paket, ini nomor resinya.
english: I want to pick up a package, here is the tracking number.
grammar: resi = tracking number: nomor resi = the code to trace your package.

target: Ada paket untuk kamu di pos satpam.
english: There is a package for you at the security post.
grammar: pos satpam = the guard post; couriers often leave packages there.

target: Kurir sudah menelepon, katanya paketnya tiba sore ini.
english: The courier already called, he said the package arrives this afternoon.

target: Jangan lupa menulis alamat lengkap di atas paket.
english: Do not forget to write the full address on the package.

target: Saya membeli perangko untuk mengirim kartu pos ke teman.
english: I bought stamps to send a postcard to a friend.

target: Paket dari ibu saya belum tiba juga.
english: The package from my mother still has not arrived.

target: Tolong cek resinya, paket saya sudah seminggu belum datang.
english: Please check the tracking number, my package has not come for a week already.

target: Loket pengambilan paket ada di sebelah kiri pintu.
english: The package pickup counter is to the left of the door.
grammar: loket = service window: loket pengambilan paket = package pickup counter.

target: Tolong kirim dokumen kantor ini lewat pos kilat.
english: Please send these office documents by express mail.

target: Petugas pos menimbang paket saya sebelum menghitung ongkosnya.
english: The post office clerk weighed my package before calculating the cost.

target: Tulis nama dan alamat penerima dengan jelas.
english: Write the receiver's name and address clearly.

target: Boleh saya pinjam uang lima puluh ribu sampai besok?
english: May I borrow fifty thousand until tomorrow?
grammar: pinjam = borrow: Boleh saya pinjam...? = May I borrow...? — the polite ask.

target: Maaf, bulan ini saya juga sedang tidak punya uang.
english: Sorry, this month I am out of money too.

target: Dia meminjam uang dari kakaknya untuk membayar kos.
english: He borrows money from his older sibling to pay for his boarding room.
grammar: kos = rented room near campus or work: membayar kos = pay the room rent.

target: Saya akan mengembalikan uangnya hari Jumat, janji.
english: I will return the money on Friday, I promise.

target: Teman baik pun harus mengembalikan pinjaman tepat waktu.
english: Even a good friend must return a loan on time.

target: Kakak meminjamkan saya uang untuk membeli buku kuliah.
english: My older sibling lent me money to buy college books.
grammar: meminjam = borrow, meminjamkan = lend: Kakak meminjamkan saya uang.

target: Jangan meminjamkan uang kalau kamu sendiri masih butuh.
english: Do not lend money if you yourself still need it.

target: Utang saya di warung sudah saya bayar semua.
english: I have already paid all my debt at the food stall.
grammar: utang = debt: punya utang = to owe, bayar utang = pay it back.

target: Dia selalu mencatat utang pelanggan di buku kecil.
english: She always writes down customers' debts in a small book.

target: Boleh pinjam dulu seratus ribu? Gajian saya minggu depan.
english: May I borrow one hundred thousand first? My payday is next week.

target: Ibu menitipkan uang belanja kepada anak sulungnya.
english: Mother entrusts the shopping money to her eldest child.

target: Terima kasih pinjamannya, ini saya kembalikan semua.
english: Thank you for the loan, here I am returning it all.

target: Struknya mau dibawa atau tidak, Kak?
english: Would you like the receipt or not, miss?
grammar: struk = printed receipt. Cashiers ask: Struknya mau dibawa? = Want the receipt?

target: Simpan struk belanja untuk laporan kantor bulan ini.
english: Keep the shopping receipts for this month's office report.

target: Saya perlu struk ini untuk klaim ke kantor.
english: I need this receipt for a claim at the office.

target: Struk ATM jangan dibuang sembarangan, ya.
english: Do not throw ATM receipts away carelessly, okay?

target: Harga di struk tidak sama dengan harga di rak.
english: The price on the receipt is not the same as the price on the shelf.

target: Tolong periksa struknya sebelum keluar dari toko.
english: Please check the receipt before leaving the store.

target: Kasir mencetak struk dan memasukkannya ke kantong plastik.
english: The cashier prints the receipt and puts it into the plastic bag.

target: Tanpa struk, barang ini tidak bisa ditukar.
english: Without a receipt, this item cannot be exchanged.

target: Semua struk belanjaan saya simpan di dompet.
english: All my shopping receipts I keep in my wallet.

target: Di struk ini ada diskon sepuluh persen, lumayan.
english: There is a ten percent discount on this receipt, not bad.
grammar: lumayan = not bad, pretty good — the word for pleasant surprises: Diskonnya lumayan!

target: Saya menukar dolar di tempat penukaran uang dekat hotel.
english: I exchange dollars at the money-exchange place near the hotel.

target: Kurs dolar hari ini enam belas ribu rupiah.
english: The dollar exchange rate today is sixteen thousand rupiah.
grammar: kurs = exchange rate: kurs dolar hari ini = today's dollar rate.

target: Sekarang saya lebih sering membayar pakai dompet digital.
english: Nowadays I more often pay using a digital wallet.
grammar: dompet = wallet; dompet digital = e-wallet apps like GoPay or Dana.

target: Setiap bulan dia menabung lima ratus ribu di bank.
english: Every month she saves five hundred thousand in the bank.

target: Tagihan listrik bulan ini naik karena AC baru.
english: This month's electricity bill went up because of the new AC.

target: Saya harus membayar tagihan air sebelum tanggal sepuluh.
english: I have to pay the water bill before the tenth.

target: Parkir motor di sini bayarnya dua ribu saja.
english: Motorbike parking here costs only two thousand.

target: Titip beli sabun di minimarket ya, uangnya nanti.
english: Please buy me soap at the minimarket, okay, I will give you the money later.
grammar: titip = ask someone to bring or get something: Titip beli sabun, ya = please get me soap.

target: Saya lupa membawa dompet, boleh saya bayar besok?
english: I forgot to bring my wallet, may I pay tomorrow?

target: Uang kertas ini sobek, bisa ditukar di bank?
english: This banknote is torn, can it be exchanged at the bank?

target: Dompet saya ketinggalan di rumah, boleh pinjam uang dulu?
english: My wallet got left at home, may I borrow some money first?

target: Semua urusan bank sekarang bisa lewat HP.
english: All banking business can now be done through your phone.

target: Hari ini saya ada urusan di bank dan kantor pos.
english: Today I have errands at the bank and the post office.

target: Rapat sore ini mundur satu jam, ya.
english: This afternoon's meeting is pushed back one hour, okay?
grammar: For meetings, mundur = pushed later: rapat mundur satu jam = the meeting moved back an hour.

target: Rapat besok maju jadi jam delapan pagi.
english: Tomorrow's meeting is moved up to eight in the morning.
grammar: maju = moved earlier: rapat maju jadi jam delapan = the meeting moved up to eight.

target: Kenapa rapat tim kita mundur lagi minggu ini?
english: Why is our team meeting pushed back again this week?

target: Rapat dengan klien batal, kita atur ulang minggu depan.
english: The meeting with the client is canceled; we'll rearrange it next week.

target: Jadwal rapat berubah, sekarang jam dua siang.
english: The meeting schedule changed; it's now at two in the afternoon.

target: Klien minta rapat diundur ke minggu depan.
english: The client asked for the meeting to be postponed to next week.
grammar: di- = done to it: diundur = postponed (by someone) — rapat diundur ke minggu depan.

target: Bisa kita tunda rapat ini sampai hari Kamis?
english: Can we postpone this meeting until Thursday?

target: Bos memajukan rapat karena dia harus ke bandara.
english: The boss moved the meeting up because he has to go to the airport.

target: Ruang rapat besar sedang dipakai tim lain.
english: The big meeting room is being used by another team.

target: Saya tidak bisa hadir di rapat sore ini.
english: I cannot attend the meeting this afternoon.
grammar: hadir = to attend, be present: hadir di rapat = attend the meeting.

target: Jangan lupa, rapat proyek dimulai jam sepuluh tepat.
english: Don't forget, the project meeting starts at ten sharp.

target: Kalau rapat mundur lagi, tolong langsung kabari saya.
english: If the meeting is pushed back again, please let me know right away.

target: Siapa yang memimpin rapat kalau bos cuti?
english: Who leads the meeting if the boss is on leave?
grammar: memimpin = to lead (root: pimpin): memimpin rapat = lead the meeting.

target: Rapat online lebih praktis kalau semua orang sibuk.
english: Online meetings are more practical when everyone is busy.

target: Agenda rapat besok sudah saya kirim ke semua orang.
english: I have already sent tomorrow's meeting agenda to everyone.

target: Rapat tadi selesai lebih cepat dari biasanya.
english: The meeting earlier finished faster than usual.

target: Pak Hasan, apakah Bapak bisa hadir di rapat jam tiga?
english: Mr. Hasan, can you attend the three o'clock meeting, sir?
grammar: Formal: use the title instead of kamu — apakah Bapak bisa hadir? = can you attend, sir?

target: Catat hasil rapat ini dan kirim ke tim, ya.
english: Note down the results of this meeting and send them to the team, okay?

target: Tenggat laporan ini hari Kamis jam lima sore.
english: The deadline for this report is Thursday at five in the afternoon.
grammar: tenggat = deadline: tenggat laporan hari Kamis = the report deadline is Thursday.

target: Saya harus menyelesaikan revisi ini sebelum tenggat.
english: I have to finish this revision before the deadline.

target: Kirim datanya paling lambat besok siang, ya.
english: Send the data by tomorrow noon at the latest, okay?
grammar: paling lambat = at the latest: kirim paling lambat besok siang = send by tomorrow noon at the latest.

target: Kalau butuh waktu tambahan, bilang ke saya sebelum Rabu.
english: If you need extra time, tell me before Wednesday.

target: Laporan keuangan harus masuk sebelum akhir bulan.
english: The financial report has to be in before the end of the month.

target: Tim kami sedang mengejar tenggat proyek minggu ini.
english: Our team is chasing the project deadline this week.
grammar: mengejar tenggat = to chase a deadline: kami sedang mengejar tenggat = we're racing the deadline.

target: Maaf, saya belum selesai karena datanya baru masuk tadi.
english: Sorry, I'm not finished yet because the data only came in just now.

target: Jangan tunggu sampai hari terakhir untuk mulai tugas ini.
english: Don't wait until the last day to start this task.

target: Tenggatnya besok, tapi laporan saya sudah selesai hari ini.
english: The deadline is tomorrow, but my report is already finished today.
grammar: -nya can mean 'the one we know': tenggatnya besok = the deadline is tomorrow.

target: Bos minta presentasi itu selesai sebelum rapat hari Senin.
english: The boss asked for that presentation to be finished before Monday's meeting.

target: Ayo kita bagi tugas supaya selesai sebelum tenggat.
english: Let's divide the tasks so we finish before the deadline.

target: Waktu kita tinggal dua hari sebelum tenggat proyek.
english: We only have two days left before the project deadline.
grammar: tinggal = left: waktu kita tinggal dua hari = we only have two days left.

target: Dia selalu mengumpulkan laporan tepat waktu.
english: He always hands in his reports on time.

target: Kalau kami terlambat mengirim laporan, klien bisa kecewa.
english: If we are late sending the report, the client could be disappointed.

target: Saya lembur malam ini supaya laporan selesai besok pagi.
english: I'm working overtime tonight so the report is finished tomorrow morning.

target: Bu Rina, mohon maaf, laporan saya terlambat satu hari.
english: Mrs. Rina, my apologies, my report is one day late.
grammar: mohon maaf = formal apology, softer than plain maaf: Mohon maaf, Bu, saya terlambat.

target: Jadwal proyek ini terlalu padat untuk tim kecil kami.
english: This project schedule is too tight for our small team.

target: Setelah revisi kedua, laporan itu akhirnya diterima klien.
english: After the second revision, the report was finally accepted by the client.

target: Saya mau mengajukan cuti tiga hari bulan depan.
english: I want to put in for three days of leave next month.
grammar: mengajukan cuti = to put in for leave: saya mengajukan cuti tiga hari.

target: Sisa cuti saya tahun ini tinggal lima hari.
english: My remaining leave this year is only five days.

target: Boleh saya minta izin menjemput anak siang ini?
english: May I ask permission to pick up my child this noon?

target: Dia sedang cuti melahirkan sampai bulan Agustus.
english: She is on maternity leave until August.
grammar: cuti melahirkan = maternity leave (melahirkan = give birth): dia sedang cuti melahirkan.

target: Kantor kami libur saat hari raya minggu depan.
english: Our office is closed for the holiday next week.

target: Saya ambil cuti untuk menemani ibu ke dokter.
english: I'm taking leave to accompany my mother to the doctor.

target: Kalau mau cuti panjang, ajukan dari jauh hari.
english: If you want a long leave, put in for it well in advance.

target: Pak Dedi, saya mohon izin cuti pada hari Jumat.
english: Mr. Dedi, I would like to request leave on Friday.
grammar: mohon izin = formal 'I request permission': saya mohon izin cuti = I request leave.

target: Permohonan cuti kamu sudah disetujui atasan.
english: Your leave request has been approved by the boss.

target: Selama saya cuti, Rina yang menggantikan saya.
english: While I'm on leave, Rina is the one covering for me.
grammar: yang marks who does it: Rina yang menggantikan saya = it's Rina who covers for me.

target: Kami menyimpan cuti tahun ini untuk liburan ke Bali.
english: We are saving our leave this year for a vacation to Bali.

target: Jangan lupa pasang balasan otomatis sebelum mulai cuti.
english: Don't forget to set up an automatic reply before starting your leave.

target: Dia jarang ambil cuti karena proyeknya banyak.
english: He rarely takes leave because he has a lot of projects.

target: Saya minta izin datang terlambat besok karena urusan keluarga.
english: I'm asking permission to come in late tomorrow because of a family matter.

target: Cuti bersama tahun ini jatuh pada bulan Desember.
english: This year's collective leave falls in December.
grammar: cuti bersama = collective leave the whole office takes at once: cuti bersama bulan Desember.

target: Setelah cuti dua minggu, saya semangat lagi bekerja.
english: After two weeks of leave, I'm excited to work again.

target: Halo Bu, saya tidak bisa masuk hari ini karena demam.
english: Hello ma'am, I can't come in today because I have a fever.
grammar: tidak masuk = not coming in (to work): saya tidak bisa masuk = I can't come in.

target: Suara saya hilang, jadi saya kerja dari rumah saja.
english: I've lost my voice, so I'll just work from home.

target: Anak saya sakit, jadi saya minta izin setengah hari.
english: My child is sick, so I'm asking permission for half a day off.

target: Dokter menyarankan saya istirahat dua hari di rumah.
english: The doctor advised me to rest at home for two days.

target: Kepala saya pusing sejak pagi, saya mau pulang cepat.
english: My head has been dizzy since morning; I want to go home early.

target: Jangan masuk kalau masih demam, istirahat saja dulu.
english: Don't come in if you still have a fever; just rest for now.

target: Surat keterangan sakit akan saya kirim ke HRD besok.
english: I will send the doctor's note to HR tomorrow.
grammar: surat keterangan sakit = doctor's note: kirim surat keterangan sakit ke kantor.

target: Dia batuk terus di kantor, sebaiknya dia pulang saja.
english: He keeps coughing at the office; he should just go home.

target: Saya sudah sembuh, besok masuk kerja seperti biasa.
english: I've recovered; tomorrow I'll come to work as usual.

target: Selama saya sakit, tugas saya dikerjakan rekan tim.
english: While I was sick, my tasks were done by a teammate.

target: Kalau badan tidak enak, jangan paksakan diri bekerja.
english: If you're feeling unwell, don't force yourself to work.
grammar: badan tidak enak = feeling unwell (lit. body not nice): kalau badan tidak enak, istirahat.

target: Saya sudah minum obat, tapi kepala masih sakit.
english: I've already taken medicine, but my head still hurts.

target: Tolong sampaikan ke bos bahwa saya sakit hari ini.
english: Please tell the boss that I'm sick today.
grammar: sampaikan ke = pass the word to: tolong sampaikan ke bos = please tell the boss.

target: Flu sedang menyebar di kantor, banyak orang tidak masuk.
english: The flu is spreading at the office; many people aren't coming in.

target: Pak Anwar, mohon izin, saya perlu periksa ke dokter siang ini.
english: Mr. Anwar, with your permission, I need to see the doctor this noon.

target: Setelah dua hari demam, akhirnya dia sembuh total.
english: After two days of fever, he finally recovered completely.

target: Saya melamar kerja di perusahaan teknologi di Jakarta.
english: I applied for a job at a technology company in Jakarta.
grammar: melamar kerja = to apply for a job — melamar alone can also mean to propose marriage!

target: Besok dia ada wawancara kerja di bank besar.
english: Tomorrow he has a job interview at a big bank.

target: Surat lamaran kamu harus jelas dan tidak terlalu panjang.
english: Your application letter has to be clear and not too long.

target: Mereka mencari karyawan baru untuk tim pemasaran.
english: They are looking for new employees for the marketing team.

target: Saya gugup sekali sebelum wawancara tadi pagi.
english: I was very nervous before the interview this morning.

target: Ceritakan pengalaman kerja kamu di perusahaan lama.
english: Tell me about your work experience at your old company.

target: Kenapa kamu mau pindah dari kantor lama?
english: Why do you want to move on from your old office?

target: Gaji di sini lebih tinggi, tapi kerjanya juga berat.
english: The salary here is higher, but the work is also heavy.
grammar: kerjanya berat = the work is heavy — -nya makes kerja 'the work here'.

target: Dia diterima kerja setelah dua kali wawancara.
english: He got the job after two interviews.
grammar: diterima = accepted: dia diterima kerja = he got the job.

target: Selamat, ya! Kapan hari pertama kamu di kantor baru?
english: Congratulations! When is your first day at the new office?

target: Tawaran kerja itu menarik, tapi kantornya jauh sekali.
english: That job offer is interesting, but the office is very far away.

target: Saya masih pikir-pikir soal tawaran itu.
english: I'm still thinking over that offer.
grammar: Doubling a verb softens it: pikir-pikir = mull it over for a while.

target: Perusahaan itu menawarkan gaji dan tunjangan yang bagus.
english: That company offers a good salary and benefits.

target: Kamu sudah mengirim surat lamaran ke perusahaan itu?
english: Have you sent your application letter to that company?

target: Wawancara kedua biasanya dengan manajer dan tim HRD.
english: The second interview is usually with the manager and the HR team.

target: Dia berhenti kerja karena mau membuka usaha sendiri.
english: He quit his job because he wants to open his own business.

target: Pengalaman organisasi juga penting untuk pelamar muda.
english: Organizational experience is also important for young applicants.

target: Bu Maya, terima kasih atas kesempatan wawancara ini.
english: Mrs. Maya, thank you for this interview opportunity.
grammar: In thanks, atas = for: terima kasih atas kesempatan ini = thank you for this opportunity.

target: Setelah wawancara, mereka berjanji mengabari saya minggu depan.
english: After the interview, they promised to let me know next week.

target: Latihan menjawab pertanyaan wawancara dengan teman sangat membantu.
english: Practicing answering interview questions with a friend helps a lot.

target: Bisa bantu saya angkat kotak dokumen ini?
english: Can you help me lift this box of documents?

target: Rekan kerja saya mengajari saya memakai sistem baru.
english: My coworker taught me how to use the new system.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, biar saya yang balas email klien.
english: If you're busy, let me be the one to reply to the client's email.
grammar: biar saya yang... = let me be the one to...: biar saya yang balas = let me reply.

target: Terima kasih sudah membantu presentasi saya kemarin.
english: Thank you for helping with my presentation yesterday.

target: Dia selalu siap membantu rekan yang kesulitan.
english: She is always ready to help colleagues who are struggling.

target: Jangan sungkan bertanya kalau ada yang belum jelas.
english: Don't hesitate to ask if anything isn't clear yet.
grammar: sungkan = shy to impose: jangan sungkan bertanya = don't hesitate to ask.

target: Kami saling membantu supaya pekerjaan cepat selesai.
english: We help each other so the work gets finished quickly.
grammar: saling = each other: saling membantu = help each other.

target: Boleh saya pinjam charger laptop kamu sebentar?
english: May I borrow your laptop charger for a moment?

target: Nanti saya akan menemani kamu bertemu klien baru.
english: Later I will accompany you to meet the new client.

target: Tolong jelaskan cara mengisi formulir ini ke saya.
english: Please explain to me how to fill in this form.

target: Dia meminjamkan payungnya ke saya waktu hujan deras.
english: She lent me her umbrella when it was raining hard.
grammar: pinjam = borrow, meminjamkan = lend: dia meminjamkan payungnya = she lent her umbrella.

target: Tim kami makan siang bersama setiap hari Jumat.
english: Our team has lunch together every Friday.

target: Rekan baru itu cepat belajar dan ramah ke semua orang.
english: That new colleague learns fast and is friendly to everyone.

target: Kalau saya lembur, dia sering membawakan saya kopi.
english: When I work overtime, she often brings me coffee.
grammar: -kan can add 'for someone': bawa → membawakan saya kopi = bring me coffee.

target: Kami merayakan akhir proyek dengan makan malam bersama.
english: We celebrated the end of the project with dinner together.

target: Pak Tono, boleh saya minta tolong periksa dokumen ini?
english: Mr. Tono, may I ask you to please check this document?
grammar: minta tolong = ask a favor: boleh saya minta tolong? = may I ask a favor?

target: Senior di kantor membimbing karyawan baru selama sebulan.
english: Seniors at the office mentor new employees for a month.

target: Suasana kantor jadi enak karena kami saling percaya.
english: The office atmosphere is pleasant because we trust each other.

target: Tolong lampirkan file anggaran di email berikutnya.
english: Please attach the budget file in the next email.
grammar: lampirkan = attach: tolong lampirkan file itu = please attach that file.

target: Saya sudah melampirkan jadwal proyek di email tadi.
english: I already attached the project schedule in the earlier email.

target: Dokumen kontrak ini perlu tanda tangan Pak Direktur.
english: This contract document needs the director's signature.
grammar: tanda tangan = signature (lit. hand mark): perlu tanda tangan = needs a signature.

target: Tolong tanda tangan di halaman terakhir, ya.
english: Please sign on the last page, okay?

target: Jangan kirim email penting waktu kamu masih emosi.
english: Don't send important emails while you're still upset.

target: Saya salah kirim email ke klien lain.
english: I sent the email to a different client by mistake.
grammar: salah + verb = do it wrong: salah kirim = sent to the wrong place.

target: Cetak dokumen ini dua rangkap untuk arsip kantor.
english: Print this document in duplicate for the office files.
grammar: dua rangkap = in duplicate: cetak dua rangkap = print two copies.

target: Printer di lantai tiga rusak lagi sejak kemarin.
english: The printer on the third floor has been broken again since yesterday.

target: Balas email klien dulu sebelum kamu rapat.
english: Reply to the client's email first before your meeting.

target: Simpan semua kontrak di folder yang sama, ya.
english: Save all the contracts in the same folder, okay?

target: Email saya penuh setelah cuti seminggu.
english: My email is full after a week of leave.

target: Malam ini saya lembur karena presentasi besok pagi.
english: Tonight I'm working overtime because of tomorrow morning's presentation.
grammar: lembur = (work) overtime: saya lembur malam ini = I'm working late tonight.

target: Jangan terlalu sering lembur, kesehatan kamu lebih penting.
english: Don't work overtime too often; your health is more important.

target: Uang lembur bulan ini masuk bersama gaji.
english: This month's overtime pay comes in with the salary.

target: Kami lembur bersama dan memesan makan malam ke kantor.
english: We worked overtime together and ordered dinner to the office.

target: Sudah jam delapan malam, ayo pulang, jangan lembur terus.
english: It's already eight at night; come on, go home, don't keep working overtime.

target: Tolong kirim ulang lampirannya, file tadi tidak bisa dibuka.
english: Please re-send the attachment; the earlier file couldn't be opened.
grammar: verb + ulang = do it again: kirim ulang = re-send it.

target: Bu Sinta, mohon periksa dokumen ini sebelum saya kirim ke klien.
english: Mrs. Sinta, please check this document before I send it to the client.
grammar: mohon + verb = very polite request, softer than tolong: mohon periksa = please check.

target: Setelah lembur seminggu, akhirnya proyek kami selesai juga.
english: After a week of overtime, our project is finally done.
grammar: akhirnya ... juga = finally, at last: akhirnya selesai juga = it's finally done.

target: Kami harus check-in dua jam sebelum pesawat berangkat.
english: We have to check in two hours before the plane departs.
grammar: Indonesians use English check-in as-is at airports and hotels: check-in dua jam sebelumnya = check in two hours early.

target: Konter check-in untuk penerbangan ke Bali ada di sebelah kiri.
english: The check-in counter for the flight to Bali is on the left side.

target: Boleh saya lihat paspor dan tiket Anda?
english: May I see your passport and ticket?
grammar: Anda (capital A) is the polite you that staff use with strangers: paspor Anda = your passport.

target: Bagasi saya beratnya dua puluh tiga kilo.
english: My luggage weighs twenty-three kilos.
grammar: -nya turns a describing word into a noun: berat = heavy, beratnya = its weight.

target: Maaf, bagasi Anda lebih berat dari batas dua puluh kilo.
english: Sorry, your luggage is heavier than the twenty-kilo limit.
grammar: batas = limit: batas dua puluh kilo = the twenty-kilo limit.

target: Saya mau bayar untuk bagasi tambahan ini.
english: I want to pay for this extra luggage.

target: Tas kecil ini saya bawa ke dalam pesawat saja.
english: This small bag I'll just take into the plane.

target: Petugas menimbang koper kami satu per satu.
english: The officer weighs our suitcases one by one.

target: Tolong taruh koper Anda di atas timbangan.
english: Please put your suitcase on the scale.

target: Paspor saya masih berlaku sampai tahun depan.
english: My passport is still valid until next year.
grammar: berlaku = valid: paspor masih berlaku = the passport is still valid.

target: Jangan sampai paspor kamu ketinggalan di taksi.
english: Don't let your passport get left behind in the taxi.
grammar: ketinggalan = left behind by accident: paspor ketinggalan di taksi = the passport got left in the taxi.

target: Setelah check-in, kami langsung ke pemeriksaan keamanan.
english: After check-in, we go straight to the security check.

target: Tolong keluarkan laptop dari tas sebelum diperiksa.
english: Please take the laptop out of the bag before it is checked.

target: Ini boarding pass Anda, pesawat berangkat dari pintu lima.
english: Here is your boarding pass; the plane departs from gate five.
grammar: boarding pass stays English at Indonesian airports; pintu = gate here.

target: Penumpang mulai naik ke pesawat lima belas menit lagi.
english: Passengers start boarding the plane in fifteen minutes.

target: Pintu keberangkatan kami pindah ke nomor tujuh.
english: Our departure gate moved to number seven.

target: Kami menunggu di ruang tunggu dekat pintu enam.
english: We are waiting in the waiting room near gate six.

target: Pesawat ke Surabaya berangkat tepat waktu pagi ini.
english: The plane to Surabaya departed on time this morning.

target: Dia lupa mengisi formulir kedatangan di pesawat.
english: He forgot to fill in the arrival form on the plane.
grammar: formulir kedatangan = arrival form; mengisi formulir = fill in a form.

target: Antrean di imigrasi panjang sekali pagi ini.
english: The line at immigration is very long this morning.
grammar: antre = queue up; antrean = the line itself: antrean panjang = a long line.

target: Kami mengantre hampir satu jam di pemeriksaan paspor.
english: We queued for almost an hour at passport control.

target: Koper saya belum keluar, padahal penumpang lain sudah pergi.
english: My suitcase hasn't come out yet, even though the other passengers have already left.

target: Bagasi kami akhirnya muncul setelah tiga puluh menit.
english: Our luggage finally appeared after thirty minutes.

target: Di mana tempat pengambilan bagasi untuk penerbangan ini?
english: Where is the baggage claim for this flight?
grammar: pengambilan bagasi = baggage claim, from ambil (take).

target: Setelah mengambil bagasi, kami mencari taksi resmi.
english: After picking up the luggage, we look for an official taxi.

target: Penerbangan kami ditunda satu jam karena hujan deras.
english: Our flight is delayed one hour because of heavy rain.
grammar: di- flips who does it: menunda = postpone, ditunda = postponed: penerbangan ditunda = the flight is delayed.

target: Pesawat ke Medan dibatalkan, jadi kami mencari jadwal lain.
english: The plane to Medan was canceled, so we look for another schedule.

target: Kenapa penerbangan sore ini ditunda lagi?
english: Why is this afternoon's flight delayed again?

target: Kereta ke Semarang ditunda karena ada masalah di rel.
english: The train to Semarang is delayed because there is a problem on the tracks.

target: Semua penerbangan ke pulau itu dibatalkan karena angin kencang.
english: All flights to that island were canceled because of strong wind.

target: Kalau penerbangan dibatalkan, uang tiket bisa diminta kembali.
english: If the flight is canceled, the ticket money can be asked back.
grammar: diminta kembali = asked back: uang bisa diminta kembali = the money can be refunded.

target: Keberangkatan kami mundur dua jam, jadi kami makan dulu.
english: Our departure slipped back two hours, so we eat first.

target: Pesawatnya masih di kota lain, jadi kita menunggu lagi.
english: The plane is still in another city, so we wait some more.

target: Penumpang diminta menunggu pengumuman berikutnya di ruang tunggu.
english: Passengers are asked to wait for the next announcement in the waiting room.

target: Maskapai memberi kami makan malam karena pesawat ditunda lama.
english: The airline gave us dinner because the plane was delayed a long time.

target: Kata petugas, jadwal baru keluar satu jam lagi.
english: According to the officer, the new schedule comes out in an hour.

target: Penerbangan pengganti baru ada besok pagi jam enam.
english: The replacement flight is only available tomorrow morning at six.
grammar: pengganti = replacement, from ganti (change): penerbangan pengganti = replacement flight.

target: Kami ketinggalan pesawat karena macet di jalan tol.
english: We missed the plane because of a traffic jam on the toll road.

target: Tiket kami masih bisa dipakai untuk penerbangan berikutnya?
english: Can our tickets still be used for the next flight?

target: Kereta terakhir sudah berangkat, jadi kami menginap di dekat stasiun.
english: The last train had already departed, so we stayed overnight near the station.
grammar: menginap = stay overnight: kami menginap di dekat stasiun = we stay the night near the station.

target: Bus malam ke Yogyakarta dibatalkan karena jalannya banjir.
english: The night bus to Yogyakarta was canceled because the road is flooded.

target: Untung saja penerbangan kami tidak ikut dibatalkan.
english: Luckily our flight was not canceled as well.
grammar: Untung saja = luckily: Untung saja tidak dibatalkan = luckily it was not canceled.

target: Dia marah karena penerbangannya ditunda tiga kali hari ini.
english: He is angry because his flight was delayed three times today.

target: Rapat di Jakarta batal karena pesawat saya ditunda lama.
english: The meeting in Jakarta fell through because my plane was delayed a long time.

target: Kalau ditunda lagi, kami naik kereta malam saja.
english: If it is delayed again, we'll just take the night train.

target: Permisi, AC di kamar kami rusak sejak tadi malam.
english: Excuse me, the AC in our room has been broken since last night.
grammar: AC is said a-se; rusak = broken: AC-nya rusak = the AC is broken.

target: Air panas di kamar mandi kami mati total.
english: The hot water in our bathroom is completely dead.

target: Keran di wastafel bocor terus, airnya menetes semalaman.
english: The tap on the sink keeps leaking; the water dripped all night.
grammar: bocor = leaking: keran bocor = the tap leaks.

target: Boleh kami minta kamar lain yang lebih tenang?
english: May we ask for another room that is quieter?
grammar: minta = ask for something: minta kamar lain = ask for another room.

target: Kamar sebelah berisik sekali sampai kami tidak bisa tidur.
english: The room next door is so noisy that we can't sleep.

target: Lampu di dekat tempat tidur tidak mau menyala.
english: The lamp near the bed won't turn on.

target: Wi-Fi di kamar lantai tiga lemah sekali.
english: The Wi-Fi in the third-floor rooms is very weak.

target: Kartu kunci kamar kami tidak bisa membuka pintu.
english: Our room key card can't open the door.

target: Tolong kirim teknisi untuk mengecek AC kamar kami.
english: Please send a technician to check the AC in our room.

target: Handuk di kamar kami belum diganti sejak kemarin.
english: The towels in our room haven't been replaced since yesterday.
grammar: diganti = replaced (by staff): handuk belum diganti = the towels have not been replaced.

target: Bisa minta handuk bersih dan air minum lagi?
english: Can we ask for clean towels and more drinking water?

target: Kamarnya bau rokok, padahal kami minta kamar bebas rokok.
english: The room smells of cigarettes, even though we asked for a non-smoking room.
grammar: bebas = free of: kamar bebas rokok = non-smoking room.

target: Toilet di kamar kami tersumbat sejak siang tadi.
english: The toilet in our room has been clogged since midday.

target: Kami pindah ke kamar lain karena jendelanya tidak bisa ditutup.
english: We moved to another room because the window couldn't be closed.

target: Resepsionis minta maaf dan memberi kami kamar yang lebih besar.
english: The receptionist apologized and gave us a bigger room.

target: Air di kamar mandi keluar kecil sekali pagi ini.
english: The water in the bathroom comes out very weakly this morning.

target: Lift hotelnya rusak, jadi kami naik tangga ke lantai empat.
english: The hotel's lift is broken, so we take the stairs to the fourth floor.

target: Kasur di kamar ini terlalu keras untuk punggung saya.
english: The mattress in this room is too hard for my back.

target: Semalam ada banyak nyamuk di kamar kami.
english: Last night there were a lot of mosquitoes in our room.

target: Kami melapor ke resepsionis soal suara AC yang keras.
english: We reported to the receptionist about the loud AC noise.

target: Kami sudah menelepon dua kali, tapi belum ada yang datang.
english: We have already called twice, but no one has come yet.

target: Kalau kamarnya masih berisik, kami mau pindah hotel besok.
english: If the room is still noisy, we want to move hotels tomorrow.

target: Untung stafnya ramah dan cepat membantu kami.
english: Luckily the staff were friendly and helped us quickly.

target: Akhirnya kami dapat kamar baru dengan pemandangan kolam renang.
english: Finally we got a new room with a view of the swimming pool.

target: Masalah air panasnya selesai setelah teknisi datang.
english: The hot water problem was resolved after the technician came.
grammar: -nya points back to the thing discussed: air panasnya = its hot water (the hotel's).

target: Kami mau menyewa motor untuk berkeliling pulau ini.
english: We want to rent a motorbike to ride around this island.
grammar: menyewa = to rent: kami menyewa motor = we rent a motorbike.

target: Berapa harga sewa mobil dengan sopir untuk sehari?
english: How much is the rental price of a car with a driver for one day?

target: Sewa motornya tujuh puluh ribu sehari, sudah termasuk dua helm.
english: The motorbike rental is seventy thousand a day, two helmets already included.

target: Boleh lihat SIM Anda sebelum motornya dibawa?
english: May I see your driving licence before the motorbike is taken?
grammar: SIM = driving licence (Surat Izin Mengemudi); said sim.

target: Jangan lupa mengisi bensin sebelum motornya dikembalikan.
english: Don't forget to fill up the petrol before the motorbike is returned.
grammar: dikembalikan = returned (by someone): motornya dikembalikan = the bike gets returned.

target: Kalau motornya rusak di jalan, telepon nomor ini.
english: If the motorbike breaks down on the road, call this number.

target: Kami menyewa mobil kecil karena jalannya sempit di sana.
english: We rented a small car because the roads are narrow there.

target: Helm ini terlalu besar, ada ukuran yang lebih kecil?
english: This helmet is too big; is there a smaller size?

target: Motor matic lebih mudah dipakai di jalan kota.
english: An automatic motorbike is easier to use on city roads.

target: Kembalikan mobilnya sebelum jam delapan malam, ya.
english: Return the car before eight in the evening, okay?

target: Kami meninggalkan paspor sebagai jaminan sewa motor itu.
english: We left a passport as the deposit for that motorbike rental.
grammar: sebagai = as: paspor sebagai jaminan = a passport as the deposit.

target: Ban belakang motornya kempis waktu kami di pantai.
english: The motorbike's rear tire was flat while we were at the beach.
grammar: kempis = flat (tire): ban kempis = a flat tire.

target: Ada tempat sewa sepeda di dekat penginapan ini?
english: Is there a bicycle rental place near this guesthouse?

target: Sewa seminggu lebih murah daripada sewa harian.
english: Renting for a week is cheaper than daily rental.
grammar: harian = daily, from hari: sewa harian = daily rental.

target: Sopirnya ramah dan tahu banyak tempat makan enak.
english: The driver is friendly and knows lots of good places to eat.

target: Kami menyewa mobil lewat aplikasi waktu liburan ke Lombok.
english: We rented a car through an app during the holiday to Lombok.

target: Sebelum dibawa, cek dulu rem dan lampu motornya.
english: Before it is taken, first check the motorbike's brakes and lights.

target: Bensinnya harus penuh waktu motornya dikembalikan besok.
english: The petrol has to be full when the motorbike is returned tomorrow.

target: Ayah menyewa mobil besar supaya semua keluarga muat.
english: Dad rented a big car so the whole family would fit.

target: Tempat sewa mobil di bandara buka dua puluh empat jam.
english: The car rental place at the airport is open twenty-four hours.

target: Tiket kereta ke Malang untuk besok masih ada?
english: Are there still train tickets to Malang for tomorrow?

target: Saya mau dua tiket dewasa dan satu tiket anak.
english: I'd like two adult tickets and one child ticket.

target: Kereta berikutnya berangkat jam sebelas dari peron dua.
english: The next train departs at eleven from platform two.

target: Jadwal bus ke pelabuhan bisa dilihat di papan itu.
english: The bus schedule to the harbor can be seen on that board.

target: Tiket pulang pergi lebih murah daripada dua tiket sekali jalan.
english: A round-trip ticket is cheaper than two one-way tickets.
grammar: pulang pergi = round trip: tiket pulang pergi = a return ticket.

target: Kapal ke pulau berangkat dua kali sehari dari pelabuhan.
english: The boat to the island departs twice a day from the harbor.

target: Loket tiket tutup jam sembilan malam setiap hari.
english: The ticket window closes at nine at night every day.

target: Anak di bawah tiga tahun tidak perlu tiket kereta.
english: Children under three don't need a train ticket.

target: Kursi dekat jendela masih kosong untuk keberangkatan sore.
english: Window seats are still free for the afternoon departure.

target: Jadwal feri berubah kalau ombak sedang tinggi.
english: The ferry schedule changes when the waves are high.

target: Simpan tiketnya sampai kamu keluar dari stasiun.
english: Keep the ticket until you exit the station.

target: Tiket konser bisa ditukar dengan gelang di pintu masuk.
english: Concert tickets can be exchanged for a wristband at the entrance.

target: Kami salah beli tanggal, tiketnya harus diubah di loket.
english: We bought the wrong date; the ticket has to be changed at the window.
grammar: salah + verb = do it wrong: salah beli = bought the wrong one.

target: Berapa lama perjalanan kereta dari sini ke Surabaya?
english: How long is the train journey from here to Surabaya?

target: Kereta cepat ke Bandung penuh terus akhir pekan ini.
english: The fast train to Bandung keeps being full this weekend.

target: Permisi, numpang tanya, stasiun kereta arah mana, ya?
english: Excuse me, may I ask, which way is the train station?
grammar: Numpang tanya = set phrase to stop a stranger politely, like excuse me, may I ask.

target: Permisi, numpang tanya, halte bus terdekat di mana?
english: Excuse me, may I ask, where is the nearest bus stop?

target: Maaf mengganggu, apakah bus ini lewat alun-alun kota?
english: Sorry to bother you, does this bus pass the town square?
grammar: Maaf mengganggu = sorry to bother you — softens a question to a stranger.

target: Permisi, boleh saya duduk di kursi kosong ini?
english: Excuse me, may I sit in this empty seat?

target: Maaf, Pak, jalan ke pelabuhan lewat mana, ya?
english: Excuse me, sir, which way is the road to the harbor?
grammar: Pak or Bu before a question keeps it polite: Maaf, Pak, ... = excuse me, sir.

target: Permisi, Bu, ada toilet umum di sekitar sini?
english: Excuse me, ma'am, is there a public toilet around here?

target: Numpang tanya, warung yang enak dekat sini di mana, ya?
english: May I ask, where is a good food stall near here?

target: Terima kasih banyak, Pak, sudah menunjukkan jalannya.
english: Thank you very much, sir, for showing the way.
grammar: menunjukkan = show, point out: menunjukkan jalan = show the way.

target: Maaf sudah merepotkan, terima kasih atas bantuannya.
english: Sorry for the trouble, and thank you for your help.
grammar: Maaf sudah merepotkan = sorry for the trouble — polite closer after someone helps.

target: Kalau boleh tahu, Bapak asalnya dari mana?
english: If I may ask, where are you from, sir?
grammar: Kalau boleh tahu = if I may ask — softens personal questions.

target: Liburan ke sini sama keluarga atau sendiri, Mas?
english: Are you on holiday here with family or alone, sir?

target: Sudah berapa lama Anda liburan di pulau ini?
english: How long have you been on holiday on this island?

target: Ini pertama kali kami ke Indonesia, dan kami senang sekali.
english: This is our first time in Indonesia, and we are very happy.

target: Besok kami mau lihat matahari terbit di gunung.
english: Tomorrow we want to see the sunrise on the mountain.

target: Pantai di sini jauh lebih sepi daripada di kota kami.
english: The beaches here are far quieter than in our city.

target: Kami sudah tiga kali liburan ke pulau ini.
english: We have been on holiday to this island three times already.

target: Cuaca di kampung halaman kamu seperti apa sekarang?
english: What is the weather like in your hometown right now?
grammar: kampung halaman = hometown, the place you are from.

target: Malam ini ada pertunjukan tari di dekat pantai.
english: Tonight there is a dance performance near the beach.

target: Foto liburan kalian bagus sekali, di mana itu?
english: Your holiday photos are really nice; where is that?

target: Semoga liburan kalian menyenangkan sampai hari terakhir.
english: May your holiday be enjoyable until the last day.
grammar: menyenangkan = enjoyable, from senang (happy): liburan menyenangkan = an enjoyable holiday.

target: Sabtu depan kami mengadakan acara keluarga di rumah nenek.
english: Next Saturday we are holding a family event at grandma's house.

target: Kami ingin mengundang kamu ke acara syukuran rumah baru.
english: We would like to invite you to a housewarming celebration.
grammar: Syukuran = a small thanksgiving do for good news; syukuran rumah baru = a housewarming.

target: Kamu mau datang ke ulang tahun anak saya hari Minggu?
english: Do you want to come to my child's birthday on Sunday?
grammar: Datang ke + event or place = come to: datang ke ulang tahun = come to the birthday. The ke never drops.

target: Undangan pernikahan sepupu saya sudah sampai kemarin sore.
english: My cousin's wedding invitation arrived yesterday afternoon.

target: Mereka mengundang seluruh keluarga besar ke acara itu.
english: They invited the whole extended family to that event.

target: Maaf, kami tidak bisa datang ke acara kamu minggu depan.
english: Sorry, we can't come to your event next week.

target: Kamu jadi datang ke nikahan teman kantor besok?
english: Are you still coming to our coworker's wedding tomorrow?
grammar: Jadi before a verb checks a plan still holds: Kamu jadi datang? = Are you still coming?

target: Tolong balas undangan itu sebelum hari Jumat, ya.
english: Please reply to that invitation before Friday, okay?

target: Dia mengajak kami makan malam di rumahnya minggu ini.
english: She invited us to have dinner at her house this week.
grammar: Mengajak = casually ask someone along; mengundang = properly invite. Dia mengajak kami makan = asked us to eat.

target: Apakah kamu sudah menerima undangan dari keluarga Pak Budi?
english: Have you received the invitation from Pak Budi's family?

target: Kami mengundang tetangga baru untuk makan siang bersama.
english: We invited the new neighbors for lunch together.

target: Jangan lupa ajak suami kamu ke acara arisan nanti.
english: Don't forget to bring your husband to the arisan later.
grammar: Arisan = a monthly savings-and-social gathering; members pool money and one takes the pot.

target: Acara dimulai jam tujuh malam di rumah paman saya.
english: The event starts at seven in the evening at my uncle's house.

target: Boleh saya bawa teman ke pesta ulang tahun kamu?
english: May I bring a friend to your birthday party?

target: Mereka belum membalas undangan kami sampai hari ini.
english: They still haven't replied to our invitation as of today.

target: Kami akan mengundang kira-kira lima puluh tamu ke resepsi.
english: We are going to invite about fifty guests to the reception.

target: Datang saja langsung, tidak perlu bawa apa-apa.
english: Just come right over; no need to bring anything.
grammar: After a negative, apa-apa = anything: tidak perlu bawa apa-apa = no need to bring anything.

target: Ibu menyuruh saya mengantar undangan ke rumah tetangga.
english: Mom told me to deliver the invitations to the neighbors' houses.

target: Kalau kamu sibuk, tidak apa-apa, acaranya masih lama.
english: If you're busy, that's fine — the event is still a long way off.

target: Kami menunggu kabar dari kamu soal acara Sabtu itu.
english: We're waiting for word from you about that Saturday event.

target: Nikahan sepupu saya bulan depan di gedung dekat alun-alun.
english: My cousin's wedding is next month at a hall near the town square.
grammar: Nikahan is the everyday word for a wedding; pernikahan is the formal one on invitations.

target: Akad nikah dimulai jam sembilan pagi, resepsinya sore hari.
english: The vow ceremony starts at nine in the morning; the reception is in the afternoon.
grammar: Akad (nikah) = the short vow ceremony; the resepsi is the big party afterwards.

target: Mereka akan menikah di kampung halaman mereka tahun depan.
english: They are going to get married in their hometown next year.

target: Kamu akan memakai baju apa ke nikahan besok malam?
english: What will you wear to the wedding tomorrow night?

target: Banyak tamu memakai batik ke resepsi pernikahan itu.
english: Many guests wore batik to that wedding reception.
grammar: Batik is wedding wear: a good batik shirt is always right at a resepsi.

target: Kedua keluarga bertemu untuk membicarakan tanggal pernikahan.
english: The two families met to discuss the wedding date.

target: Adik saya baru bertunangan dengan teman kuliahnya.
english: My younger sister just got engaged to her college friend.

target: Lamaran mereka berjalan lancar minggu lalu di rumah calon mertua.
english: Their proposal went smoothly last week at the future in-laws' house.
grammar: Calon = future/-to-be: calon mertua = future in-laws, calon suami = husband-to-be.

target: Kami datang ke resepsi hanya sebentar karena anak kami masih kecil.
english: We only came to the reception briefly because our child is still little.

target: Amplopnya ditaruh di kotak dekat pintu masuk gedung.
english: The envelope is placed in a box near the hall entrance.
grammar: Wedding guests give cash in an amplop (envelope), dropped in a box at the door — not handed over.

target: Pengantin kelihatan bahagia sekali waktu memotong kue.
english: The bride and groom looked really happy while cutting the cake.

target: Mereka menikah setelah tujuh tahun saling kenal.
english: They got married after knowing each other for seven years.

target: Selamat menempuh hidup baru untuk kalian berdua!
english: Congratulations on your new life together, you two!
grammar: Selamat menempuh hidup baru = the set wedding wish: 'safe journey into the new life'.

target: Setiap acara keluarga, paman selalu bertanya kapan saya menikah.
english: At every family event, my uncle always asks when I'm getting married.

target: Mereka menyewa gedung besar karena tamunya hampir seribu orang.
english: They rented a big hall because they have almost a thousand guests.

target: Saya jadi panitia di nikahan teman baik saya.
english: I'm on the committee at my best friend's wedding.

target: Setiap tamu dapat suvenir kipas kecil dari pengantin.
english: Every guest got a small fan as a souvenir from the couple.

target: Fotonya bagus sekali, siapa fotografer di nikahan kemarin?
english: The photos are really good — who was the photographer at yesterday's wedding?

target: Orang tuanya menangis bahagia waktu akad nikah selesai.
english: Her parents cried tears of joy when the vow ceremony ended.

target: Setelah menikah, mereka tinggal sementara di rumah mertua.
english: After getting married, they are living at the in-laws' house for a while.
